title: Preserve non-Void tail values through final hygiene
description:
## Problem

A fresh build of examples/14-abstraction-lab proves a semantic regression: ImmediateRetryPolicy.nextDelayMs(_attempt:Int):Int returns 0 in Haxe, but LocalAssignUnusedUnderscore_Scoped_Final removes the tail literal and emits an empty Elixir function returning nil.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Compile examples/14-abstraction-lab from the current source checkout.
2. Inspect lib/abstraction_lab/immediate_retry_policy.ex.
3. Observe that next_delay_ms/2 has an empty body and returns nil instead of 0.
4. Enable granular AST snapshots and compare the snapshots immediately before and after LocalAssignUnusedUnderscore_Scoped_Final.

## Root Cause Evidence

Granular snapshots place the value-removal transition in LocalAssignUnusedUnderscoreScopedTransforms. Fix the root statement/value-context classification rather than skipping the fixture, disabling hygiene, or special-casing integer zero.
design: A tail expression in a non-Void function is a return value even when it is syntactically a pure literal or resembles an unused expression. Make final hygiene reason about value context and remove only expressions proven semantically discardable in statement context. Preserve existing unused-binding warning cleanup and avoid a new final repair pass.
acceptance_criteria: ImmediateRetryPolicy.next_delay_ms/2 returns 0 in freshly generated Elixir and an Elixir runtime assertion proves it; focused Haxe-to-ExUnit coverage exercises primitive literal, nil/Null where valid, tuple/map-like target values, local-variable, call, and branch tail returns; a regression fails against the old pass behavior; example 14 gains meaningful strict-Elixir and runtime QA instead of hiding the method behind compile-only coverage, or the focused runtime harness is justified in its manifest; snapshots, upstream stdlib runtime, all examples/output/WAE/runtime, Mix tests, package parity, and async todo Playwright sentinel pass; changelog and developer-facing notes identify the semantic fix.
notes: Root cause confirmed in LocalAssignUnusedUnderscoreScopedTransforms: function bodies that were scalar AST nodes were wrapped in a synthetic EBlock for unused-binder analysis and returned still wrapped, so the printer treated the value as a discardable block statement. rewriteFunctionBody now restores scalar value context after analysis while leaving real EBlock/EDo bodies unchanged. Added executable snapshot coverage for int, bool, string, float, nil, list, map, tuple, local, call, and branch tails; updated the pre-existing hygiene snapshot and example 14 output/QA rationale. Full snapshots, npm test, 132 Haxe ExUnit stdlib tests, example compile/WAE/runtime, CI guards, Mix, source/package parity smoke, and todo-app sentinel Playwright 5/5 passed locally. Tuple-shaped anonymous-object field access exposed a separate pre-existing issue tracked as haxe.elixir.codex-3qh.19; this fixture validates the tuple tail directly to keep this repair scoped.
close_reason: Preserved scalar non-Void function results through final hygiene with focused snapshot/runtime coverage and updated example/docs QA.

title: HXX2: markup parser + build-macro rewrite
description:
PLAN_REF: plans/active/hxx2-default-authoring-path.md#-1-macro-rewrite-beads-haxeelixir-hxx22

FILES
- src/reflaxe/elixir/macros/InlineMarkup.hx

WHAT
- Make inline markup default-on for Phoenix-facing modules by rewriting `@:markup` into the canonical entrypoint: `phoenix.hxx.HeexTemplate.root(<typed template expr>)`.
- Parse `{ ... }` blocks inside inline markup into real Haxe `Expr` nodes using `Context.parseInlineString`, then reconstruct the template as a typed Haxe expression (string fragments + embedded expressions).

ALGORITHM
- Rewrite rule:
  - Before: `@:markup <payload>` -> `HXX.hxx(<payload>)` (legacy string-template path)
  - After:  `@:markup <payload>` -> `phoenix.hxx.HeexTemplate.root(<typedExpr>)`
- Payload scanning must be deterministic and quote-aware:
  - Split payload into literal chunks and expression chunks delimited by braces.
  - Track quote state for `"` and `'` so braces inside quoted attribute values do not start expressions.
  - Track brace depth for nested braces inside an expression.
  - Fail fast on: unclosed `{`, stray `}`, empty `{}`.
- Expression parsing:
  - For each expression chunk, call `Context.parseInlineString(exprText, pos)` to produce a typed Haxe `Expr`.
  - Parenthesize parsed expressions when stitching to avoid precedence issues.
- Reconstruction:
  - Build a Haxe AST equivalent to: `"<lit1>" + (expr1) + "<lit2>" + (expr2) + ...`.
  - Fast path: if no expressions exist, call `HeexTemplate.root(<stringConst>)` directly.

DEFAULTS / OPT-OUT / LEGACY
- Default-on for Phoenix-facing modules (same concept as current `shouldProcessLocalType`).
- Global opt-out: `-D hxx_no_inline_markup`.
- Per-class opt-out: `@:hxx_no_inline_markup`.
- Legacy escape hatch: `@:hxx_legacy` forces legacy rewrite to `HXX.hxx(...)` for that class.

FAILURE MODES / DIAGNOSTICS
- Errors must be positional: point at the offending span inside the inline-markup payload.
- Messages must include the fix (correct braces, or opt-out / legacy escape hatch).

TESTS (add fixtures)
- Positive: test/snapshot/phoenix/heex_template_inline_markup_basic
- Positive: test/snapshot/phoenix/heex_template_inline_markup_attrs_expr
- Negative: test/snapshot/negative/heex_template_inline_markup_brace_errors

VERIFICATION
- npm test
- npm run qa:sentinel then scripts/qa-logpeek.sh --run-id <RUN_ID> --until-done 120

ROLLOUT
- Keep HXX1 (string templates) working unchanged.
- Enable inline markup rewrite by default only for Phoenix-facing modules; opt-outs available.

NOTES
- Canonical entrypoint is `phoenix.hxx.HeexTemplate.root/1`; `phoenix.hxx.HXX2.root/1` remains as deprecated alias.
acceptance_criteria:
- Inline markup works without -D
- { ... } blocks parsed as Haxe Expr (Context.parseInlineString)
- Errors are positional + fail-fast
- Opt-out exists: -D hxx_no_inline_markup and @:hxx_no_inline_markup
- Legacy escape hatch exists: @:hxx_legacy
close_reason: Completed by commit 7a10c5dc

title: HXX2: builder lowering to ~H
description:
PLAN_REF: plans/active/hxx2-default-authoring-path.md#-2-builder-lowering-beads-haxeelixir-hxx23

FILES
- src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/builders/CallExprBuilder.hx
- src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/HeexStringReturnToSigilTransforms.hx

WHAT
- Lower `phoenix.hxx.HeexTemplate.root/1` to `ESigil("H", content, "")` deterministically in the typed AST (same semantics as `HXX.hxx/1`).

ALGORITHM
- In `CallExprBuilder`, detect static calls where:
  - class is `phoenix.hxx.HeexTemplate` (also accept deprecated alias `phoenix.hxx.HXX2`)
  - method is `root`
  - arity is 1
- Build the argument expression as ElixirAST (`innerAst`).
- Convert to HEEx string:
  - `content = TemplateHelpers.collectTemplateContent(innerAst)`
  - `content = HeexControlTagTransforms.rewrite(content)` (same normalization as HXX1 lowering)
- Enforce raw-HEEx escape hatch policy:
  - If `content` contains raw markers (`<%`, `<%=` etc.) and not allowed, raise.
  - Allowed only under `@:allow_heex` (method/class) or `-D hxx_allow_raw_heex`.
- Return `ESigil("H", content, "")`.

VAR-BINDING LOWERING
- Extend `HeexStringReturnToSigilTransforms` to recognize `HeexTemplate.root(...)` as a template producer in returned-var patterns.

TESTS
- Positive: test/snapshot/phoenix/heex_template_inline_markup_basic
- Positive: test/snapshot/phoenix/heex_template_var_binding_root

VERIFICATION
- npm test

NOTES
- Canonical entrypoint is `phoenix.hxx.HeexTemplate.root/1`; `phoenix.hxx.HXX2.root/1` remains as deprecated alias.
acceptance_criteria:
- phoenix.hxx.HeexTemplate.root/1 lowers to ~H
- Raw HEEx remains escape-hatch-only
- Var-binding conversions recognize HeexTemplate.root
- Existing HXX1 snapshots remain green

design: Chat architecture: Haxe-authored LiveView for UI; messages broadcast via Phoenix.PubSub; online users via Phoenix.Presence; optional OTP GenServer (Haxe) to keep last N messages in-memory for new joiners. Prefer server-only first; JS hooks optional. Use typed externs for Phoenix APIs; avoid __elixir__ in app code.

title: DevX: detach from external Haxe server after internal crash
description: When the default --wait port is occupied by an external Haxe server (often from another repo/session), we may attach and then get internal compiler crashes like: File "src/core/globals.ml" ... Assertion failed. Current restart path (stop/start) doesn't kill the external server, so we can loop. Detect internal failures on server compile when owns_server=false, detach, and start our own server on a fresh port for subsequent compiles.
notes: Default HaxeServer behavior no longer attaches to external --wait servers; opt-in via HAXE_SERVER_ALLOW_ATTACH=1. This avoids cross-project cache corruption (globals.ml assertion) and prevents stop/start loops from reattaching.

title: Phase 1.3: Create FinalUnderscorePrefixTransforms - move ALL underscore prefixing to final pass
description:
## Problem
`_this` is used after being set, which Elixir warns about:
```
warning: variable "_this" is unused (if the variable is not meant to be used, prefix it with an underscore)
```

The variable has underscore prefix but is still being used later in the code.

## Root Cause
Underscore prefix is applied in builders (too early), but usage is detected in transforms (too late).

Timeline problem:
1. Builder creates `_this` with underscore (assuming unused)
2. Later code uses `_this` 
3. Transform runs but underscore already applied
4. Elixir sees underscore-prefixed var being used = warning

## Solution
Move ALL underscore prefixing to a FINAL sentinel pass that runs after all other transforms.

## Files to Modify
- src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/builders/*.hx - Remove early underscore prefixing
- UPDATE: src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/FinalUnderscorePrefixTransforms.hx (may exist)

## Implementation
1. Remove underscore logic from all builders
2. Create/update final pass that:
   - Scans entire module for ALL variable definitions
   - Collects ALL variable usages across entire module
   - Only THEN applies underscore prefix to truly unused variables
3. Register as LAST pass in transformation pipeline

## Key Principle
Underscore prefix decision must happen AFTER all transformations that might add/remove usages.

## Dependencies
- Should run after: Phase 1.0A (this1 cleanup)
- Blocks: Phase 1.2 (removal pass needs correct usage data)

## Acceptance Criteria
- No "underscore variable used after set" warnings
- All truly unused variables get underscore prefix
- All used variables do NOT get underscore prefix
- npm test passes
- mix compile --force shows no underscore-usage warnings

## Effort: 2-3 hours | Impact: Fixes 2 warnings + prevents future issues
notes: Duplicate/outdated: Phase 1.3 underscore-prefixing work was already completed (see haxe.elixir-2co). Closing to keep backlog accurate.

6. Keep optional builds deterministic and require every absent optional target to be declared optional rather than tolerated as a misspelling.

- silently deduplicating pass IDs or recovering from a cycle;
- treating all currently missing names as optional without evidence;

title: Centralize exhaustive ElixirAST child and pattern traversal
description:
The generic AST entry points previously duplicated incomplete child switches. A new child-bearing
constructor could compile while capability analysis, variable-use analysis, or a rewrite silently
treated it as a leaf. Deliver one exhaustive structural traversal authority and migrate generic
entry points onto it without parallel universal walkers or compile-time regressions.

## FILES

- `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/ElixirASTTransformer.hx`
- `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/ElixirPatternChildren.hx`
- `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/ASTUtils.hx`

- `test/snapshot/core/maps/**`
- compiler architecture/flow documentation and package test scripts

## ALGORITHM

1. Keep one no-default fused child switch in `transformNodeScopedInternal` for every
   `ElixirASTDef` constructor and one coordinated no-default mapper for every `EPattern`
   constructor, including AST values carried by patterns.
2. Derive one-level `transformAST` from the fused engine by treating direct children as
   transformable boundaries. Derive `iterateAST` from that map and recursive `ASTUtils.walk`
   from `iterateAST`; none owns another constructor switch.
3. Preserve metadata, source positions, optional record fields, HEEx attribute spans, deterministic
   order, raw opacity, and existing scoped-boundary semantics. Internal object identity is not a
   public contract.
4. Keep scope, control-flow, metadata, and raw-authority policies outside the structural engine.
   A pass whose rewrite depends on binders owns the smallest explicit scope rule it needs.
5. Classify newly exposed behavior with generated/runtime parity. Fix real semantic failures at
   their owner and protect them with ordinary Haxe source.
6. Benchmark the heaviest HXX fixture against the pre-refactor commit. Reject a design that restores
   exhaustive behavior by materially increasing compiler eval/JIT or traversal cost.

## FAILURE MODES

- a catch-all silently treats a future constructor as a leaf;
- traversal omits guards, module attributes, receiver operations, fragments, quoted children, or
  AST values embedded in patterns;
- mapping drops metadata, positions, attribute spans, or optional fields;
- immediate or read-only entry points grow independent constructor switches;
- generic structural traversal incorrectly claims lexical-scope knowledge;
- raw target injection is rewritten;
- a correct but over-abstract mapper makes parallel CI or consumer compilation time out;
- another permanent walker, architecture receipt, or semantic-boundary inventory duplicates tests.

## TESTS

- executable constructor-set coverage for all 66 AST constructors and 11 pattern constructors;
- immediate child counts, embedded-pattern AST mapping, deterministic preorder,
  position/metadata/attribute-span preservation, raw opacity, and explicit boundary behavior;
- generic transformer delegation including `EReceiverEffect.operation`;
- ordinary-Haxe reducer/enum-switch regression proving an anonymous-function case binder cannot
  replace the enclosing map accumulator;
- controlled `phoenix/HXXTypeSafety` timing against the pre-refactor worktree;
- complete snapshot categories, result invariant, pass inventory/scope parity, handwritten output,
  example compile/output/WAE/runtime, installed-package parity, and todo-app browser smoke.

## VERIFICATION

Run `npm run test:ast-children`, all snapshot chunks, `npm run test:result-invariant`, pass inventory
and scope guards, handwritten-output, example compile/output/WAE/runtime suites,
`npm run test:haxelib-package`, documentation/path/diff guards, and the async bounded todo-app
sentinel with focused Playwright. Require exact-head CI/CodeQL before starting the next child.

## ROLLOUT

Internal output-preserving compiler refactor. The fused engine replaces duplicated child knowledge;
it does not add a public mode or a second semantic IR. Roll back the slice if generated/runtime
parity or the controlled compile-time budget cannot be proven.
design: Use one typed, no-default fused AST traversal engine plus the exhaustive pattern mapper. Derive immediate map, immediate visit, and recursive walk behavior from that engine through explicit boundary policy. Preserve raw/metadata opacity and local scope ownership. Executable Haxe behavior contracts, full parity, and a controlled HXX compile-time comparison replace architecture receipts or duplicate traversal frameworks.
acceptance_criteria: All 66 AST constructors and 11 pattern variants have explicit no-default child behavior; immediate map/visit and recursive walk derive from one fused AST switch; metadata, positions, optional fields, and spans are preserved; raw remains opaque; the accumulator regression is fixed at its owner; focused/full generated-runtime-package-browser gates pass; the controlled HXX fixture remains near the pre-refactor compile-time baseline; exact-head CI is green.

title: Freeze architecture-refactor regression baselines
description:
The compiler architecture refactor needs a reproducible no-regression starting point before traversal, scheduling, receiver, or printer ownership changes. The repository already has the right evidence layers: generated pass inventory/scope guards, Haxe snapshots and negative fixtures, function-result invariants, scoped-versus-all-pass parity, runtime tests, package checks, and determinism gates. Use those mechanisms and reviewed source evidence; do not create a parallel regex-generated architecture receipt or string-anchor database.

## FILES

- `AGENTS.md`
- `docs/03-compiler-development/LEAN_PASS_PIPELINE.md`
- `docs/05-architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `docs/05-architecture/COMPILATION_FLOW.md`

- `plans/active/semantic-plans-and-structural-ast.md`

- existing snapshot, result-invariant, pass-scope, package, and determinism test surfaces

No new receipt generator, source-string anchor catalog, or duplicate architecture database belongs in this slice.

## ALGORITHM

1. Reconcile the documented granular pass baseline with the existing generated inventory and guards; do not reimplement or digest the registry in a second tool.
2. Record the reviewed architecture observations in the ADR with direct source references and explicit observed/inferred/unknown status: AST/walker gaps, permissive registry behavior, opaque bundles, receiver replay, printer policy/state, result-printer coupling, and incomplete LoopIR planning.
3. Identify the existing executable gate that protects each refactor dimension: pass order/scope, output bytes, value results, runtime semantics, package parity, determinism, and bounded example QA.
4. Run the smallest current baseline suite that proves this planning/documentation slice is output-inert.
5. Require each later implementation slice to add its focused Haxe-authored contract tests beside the owning code—for example exhaustive child preservation, fail-closed registry validation, granular pass attribution, or conservative analysis invalidation—plus ordinary source-level regression and byte/runtime parity evidence.
6. Keep one-off discovery scripts and static reports disposable unless a concrete recurring failure proves durable CI value.

## FAILURE MODES

- introducing a source-scan receipt, string-anchor catalog, or parallel audit database merely to freeze implementation details;
- treating constructor counts, source paths, names, regex matches, or line locations as semantic authority;
- duplicating the generated pass inventory or pass registry;
- claiming that snapshots alone prove runtime semantics;
- adding broad new test infrastructure when an existing fixture/guard can express the contract;
- changing compiler output or pass order in this slice;
- refreshing expected output without reviewing every changed output class;
- machine-local paths in documentation or generated evidence.

## TESTS

- existing pass inventory and pass-scope guards remain green at the documented 578-pass baseline;
- existing result-invariant smoke remains green;
- focused core/stdlib/regression snapshots prove no generated-output change;
- documentation links, formatting/diff, and path-hygiene guards pass;
- Beads lint and dependency readiness remain valid.

No new architecture-receipt test suite is created. Contract tests for new traversal/pass/analysis behavior land in the child that implements that behavior.

Run `npm run guard:pass-inventory`, `npm run guard:pass-scopes`, `npm run test:result-invariant`, `npm run test:quick`, `npm run guard:docs-links`, `git diff --check`, the repository path-hygiene scan, `bd lint --json`, and `bd ready --json`. Commands must be bounded and non-watch. Before closure/push, require the latest exact-head CI according to `AGENTS.md`.

## ROLLOUT

Output-inert baseline/documentation slice only. Land separately before the traversal implementation. Later children own executable architecture contracts and may not use a receipt or inventory as a substitute for behavior, structural, runtime, package, or determinism tests.
design: Use the repository's existing executable evidence and reviewed ADR source references. Architecture contracts are implemented and tested beside their owning traversal, registry, pass-manager, legality, analysis, receiver, result, printer, or LoopIR slice. Do not create a generated source receipt or parallel audit database.
acceptance_criteria: The current 578-pass baseline and architecture observations are reconciled in canonical docs; existing pass inventory/scope, result-invariant, focused snapshot, docs, path, and Beads gates pass without compiler/generated-output drift; AGENTS.md directs agents to prefer executable contracts over architecture ceremony; no architecture receipt generator, string-anchor catalog, or duplicate audit artifact is added; exact-head CI is green before the traversal child begins.

title: Strengthen semantic plans and structural AST boundaries
description:
Strengthen the existing `TypedExpr -> ElixirAST -> ordered passes -> printer` compiler by making structural traversal, pass scheduling, legality, analysis invalidation, and printer ownership executable. Add richer structural nodes or narrow semantic plans only after that substrate proves they cannot become silent leaves. This implements GitHub issue #38 incrementally. It does not replace `ElixirAST`, copy haxe.c HxcIR/CFG machinery, create another backend, or duplicate the managed-reference runtime program.

## FILES

- `docs/05-architecture/SEMANTIC_PLANS_AND_STRUCTURAL_AST.md`
- `plans/active/semantic-plans-and-structural-ast.md`
- `docs/05-architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `docs/05-architecture/COMPILATION_FLOW.md`
- `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/ElixirAST.hx`

1. Freeze a reproducible semantic-boundary, static-state, traversal, printer-policy, and pass-order evidence baseline.
2. Centralize exhaustive immediate-child and pattern traversal; shadow current walkers before switching.
3. Freeze the 578-pass effective order and make hard registry errors fail closed without rescheduling it.
4. Replace seven opaque executable bundles with transparent nested groups through one runner.
5. Add request-local pass state plus conservative, differential-tested analysis invalidation.
6. Add report-only then enforced legality for narrowly admitted semantic/raw families.
7. Instrument and consolidate persistent receiver effects under one owner.
8. Detach result correctness from printer sentinel deletion.
9. Keep compiler-owned interpolation structural through printing.
10. Move remaining semantic policy and correctness-visible naming out of the printer one family at a time.
11. Tighten LoopIR into a complete builder-local plan without a universal CFG.
12. Extract only proven owners after byte/runtime, scoped/all-pass, package, determinism, and performance evidence.

## FAILURE MODES

- adding new semantic nodes before exhaustive traversal and legality exist;
- copying HxcIR or introducing a whole-program SSA/CFG without Elixir-specific pressure;
- changing current pass order while adding validation or grouping;
- silent duplicate/dependency/cycle recovery;
- opaque bundle execution hiding inner failures or stale analyses;
- a broad metadata flag cloud or semantic-marker payload becoming a parallel IR;
- printing AST to build compiler-owned AST children;
- using app names, paths, profiles, function names, or printed shapes to infer ownership;
- printer repair of unresolved semantics;
- combining traversal, pass reorder, semantic nodes, printer policy, and runtime ABI in one branch;
- claiming managed-reference support from compiler scaffolding.

## TESTS

Children provide constructor/pattern coverage, old/new traversal and runner differential checks, strict registry negatives, analysis forced-recompute checks, legality diagnostics, receiver and result runtime semantics, interpolation escaping/order, printer determinism, closed loop plans, full generated-tree parity, and applicable examples/package/browser evidence.

## ROLLOUT

1.x internal compiler architecture work. No user mode, profile semantics, or 1.0 blocker edge. Infrastructure slices are output-inert; intentional code-quality or correctness changes land separately with ordinary-Haxe regressions and reviewed output. Each child is independently revertible.
design: Keep ElixirAST as the single persistent target IR. First make child traversal exhaustive and pass boundaries transparent, then add request-local invalidation and phase legality. Admit structural nodes or semantic markers only for proven source/ABI gaps, with one owner and printer illegality after that boundary.

title: Implement exact stateful iterator EReg and Xml aliases
description:
Iterator objects carry mutable cursor state, EReg.match and matchSub update later matched* observations, and Xml nodes expose mutable attributes, names, parent/child links, and cycles. Current native/process-state shortcuts and module-level tests do not prove aliases, package ABI, same-node process behavior, or lifecycle. Implement these stateful core objects after their source collection carriers are stable.

FILES

- managed cursor/match/node runtime operations
- focused snapshots and ordinary-Haxe runtime fixtures
- upstream/local conformance evidence and stdlib parity inventory
design:
ALGORITHM
1. Inventory every compiler/runtime-produced iterator carrier and give cursor aliases one explicit state contract; collection-specific iteration remains coordinated with the owning Array/Map/List tasks.
2. Preserve EReg receiver-owned match state across aliases for match, matchSub, matched, matchedLeft, matchedRight, and matchedPos without inferring identity from regex text.
3. Preserve Xml node allocation identity, mutable node/attribute state, parent/child ownership, detach/reparent/order behavior, and cyclic graph edges.
4. Carry descriptors through Dynamic, reflection, serialization, generic/package boundaries, same-node process messages, and managed graph lifetime.
5. Run replacement callbacks, serializers, inspectors, and user iteration code outside heap locks; explicit native regex/XML extern boundaries remain separately typed.

FAILURE MODES
Independent iterator snapshots for aliases, global regex state shared by separate allocations, process-local make_ref state, rebuilt Xml trees that stale external node aliases, broken parent links/cycles, hidden-ID serialization, or lock-held callbacks are blockers.

TESTS
Alias cursor advancement for IntIterator and collection/key-value iterators; separate cursor independence; EReg alias and separate-allocation match histories; replace/map callbacks and throws; Xml attribute/name/value/child/reparent/remove mutations through external aliases; graph reflection/serialization; generic/package/same-node process and lifetime evidence.
acceptance_criteria: All audited iterator cursor, EReg match-state, and Xml node mutations are visible through aliases while separate allocations remain independent; Xml parent/child identity and cycles survive reflection/serialization under their owning graph contract; callbacks execute unlocked; no process-dictionary-only support claim remains; focused snapshots/runtime tests, relevant upstream/local conformance, inventory, minimum/primary toolchains, package smoke, WAE, full suites, examples, handwritten-output, and sentinel gates pass. Rollout stays gated until the complete state family and collection integration are green.

title: Implement exact mutable builder and checksum aliases
description:
StringBuf, BytesBuffer, Crc32, and Adler32 mutate receiver-owned state. Existing direct-receiver runtime tests and receiver-return conventions do not prove that aliases observe add/update/clear operations. Implement these ordinary objects with shared state and remove one-binding repair ownership only after complete parity.

FILES
- typed builder/checksum lowering under src/reflaxe/elixir/**
- managed state/runtime operations
- focused snapshots, ordinary-Haxe runtime fixtures, and upstream/local conformance evidence
- ReceiverReturnConventions and stdlib parity inventory
design:
ALGORITHM
1. Classify each builder/checksum allocation and public ABI as a managed mutable object or a rigorously equivalent shared-storage carrier.
2. Lower the complete add/addChar/addSub/addBytes/numeric-write/clear/update/read surface with single evaluation and exact results.
3. Ensure toString/getBytes/get/copy-like observations follow Haxe 4.3.7 ownership and snapshot rules and preserve nested Bytes semantics.
4. Remove persistent receiver-return entries only when every mutator is routed through shared state.
5. Carry representation through generics, Dynamic/reflection, packages, and same-node process transfer.

FAILURE MODES
Passing only direct-receiver tests, discarding updated receivers, mixing managed and persistent operations, returning a buffer snapshot with the wrong sharing contract, process-local state, or holding locks during formatting/conversion are blockers.

TESTS
Two aliases for every mutator; mixed add types and boundaries; checksum incremental versus one-shot values; repeated observations; clear/reset where present; Bytes integration; exceptions; Dynamic/generic/package/same-node process flows; source and package parity.
acceptance_criteria: Every audited StringBuf, BytesBuffer, Crc32, and Adler32 mutation is visible through aliases and produces exact observations/results; no ordinary builder/checksum relies on caller rebinding; representation and package descriptors are stable; focused snapshots/runtime tests, upstream/local conformance, inventory, minimum/primary toolchains, package smoke, WAE, full suites, examples, handwritten-output, and sentinel gates pass. Rollout is family-complete, not method-by-method.

title: Implement exact Bytes Vector and typed-view shared storage
description:
Bytes, Vector, ArrayBufferView, and typed byte views expose mutable indexed storage. Views may intentionally share a backing Bytes allocation, while Bytes.sub and Vector.copy create independent storage. Current process-dictionary cells prove only process-local behavior and do not establish lifetime, same-node process aliases, or package ABI. Implement one explicit shared-storage graph contract.

FILES
- typed storage/view representation and semantic indexed operations under src/reflaxe/elixir/**
- managed backing-store runtime and view descriptors
- Bytes/Vector/view snapshots, runtime fixtures, and upstream unitstd evidence
- stdlib parity inventory
design:
ALGORITHM
1. Classify storage owners and non-owning views separately while giving aliases to one owner the same managed backing identity.
2. Lower Bytes set/blit/fill/numeric writes, Vector set/fill/blit, and typed-view writes to bounds-checked shared operations with exact source results and exceptions.
3. Preserve view offset/length and source sharing for fromBytes, fromData, subarray, and related APIs; make documented copy/sub operations allocate independent backing storage.
4. Carry element/storage descriptors through Dynamic, reflection, serialization, generics, packages, and same-node process messages.
5. Retire process-local make_ref/process-dictionary representations only after parity, lifetime, concurrency, and package evidence; preserve explicit native binary boundaries via typed projections.

FAILURE MODES
Treating a view as a copy, making Bytes.sub share unexpectedly, process-local aliases that diverge across BEAM processes, silent native-binary mutation, late boxing, incorrect overlap blit, or inconsistent bounds/endianness are blockers.

TESTS
Direct and nested aliases; overlapping blit/fill/index/numeric operations; view offsets/subarrays/fromData/toData; copy independence; endianness; invalid bounds; Dynamic/reflection/serialization; generic/package flow; same-node process sharing and lifetime; explicit binary projection.
acceptance_criteria: Bytes, Vector, ArrayBufferView, and supported typed views preserve the audited backing-store alias and copy graph across locals, fields, packages, and same-node processes; bounds, overlap, result, and endianness behavior match Haxe 4.3.7; explicit native binaries remain immutable boundary values; no process-dictionary-only support claim remains; focused snapshots/runtime tests, upstream unitstd, inventory, minimum/primary toolchains, package smoke, WAE, full suites, examples, handwritten-output, and sentinel gates pass.

title: Implement exact List and GenericStack aliases
description:
haxe.ds.List and GenericStack mutate shared head/tail/length state. Haxe 4.3.7 source and reference probes show aliases observe add, push, pop, remove, and clear, while current receiver-return conventions preserve only one binding. Implement both linked collection families over shared managed state; ListSort node rewiring remains a separate gate.

FILES
- typed linked-collection lowering under src/reflaxe/elixir/**
- managed List/GenericStack runtime operations
- focused snapshots/runtime fixtures and upstream unitstd evidence
- receiver-return inventory and stdlib parity inventory
design:
ALGORITHM
1. Classify ordinary List<T> and GenericStack<T> as managed collection objects in fields, closures, generics, Dynamic domains, and package manifests.
2. Lower all reads and mutators against shared head/tail/length state with exact result and exception behavior.
3. Preserve shallow element aliases and independent collection identity for any copy-producing operation.
4. Implement iterator cursors through the stateful-cursor owner and run user callbacks outside locks.
5. Remove these ordinary types from persistent receiver-return repair paths after managed parity is complete; do not enable ListSort here.

FAILURE MODES
Rebinding only the caller, rebuilding replacement nodes while external aliases remain, mixing managed and persistent mutators, leaking internal node IDs, lock-held callbacks, or prematurely removing the ListSort diagnostic are blockers.

TESTS
Alias every List and GenericStack mutator through locals, fields, returns, generics, Dynamic, and package boundaries; cover length/head/tail, shallow elements, empty/error cases, iterator behavior and mutation, nested managed leaves, and unchanged ListSort negative coverage.
acceptance_criteria: List and GenericStack aliases observe every audited mutation with exact results and ordering; complete families use one representation; generic/package and reflection descriptors agree; iterators satisfy their dedicated stateful contract; ListSort remains gated; focused snapshots/runtime tests, upstream unitstd, inventory, minimum/primary toolchains, package smoke, WAE, full suites, examples, handwritten-output, and sentinel gates pass.

title: Implement exact ordinary Map tree and HashMap aliases
description:
Ordinary Haxe Map specializations, StringMap, IntMap, EnumValueMap/BalancedTree, and HashMap expose shared set/remove/clear state and copy-to-independent-map behavior. Current raw BEAM map and receiver-rebind paths lose aliases. Implement the native-key map families coherently; object-key Map remains owned by the separate ObjectMap slice.

FILES
- typed Map-specialization and semantic collection lowering under src/reflaxe/elixir/**
- managed map runtime operations
- map/tree/hash snapshots and ordinary-Haxe runtime fixtures
- upstream unitstd/evidence manifests and stdlib parity inventory
design:
ALGORITHM
1. Resolve Map specialization from the typed Haxe contract before AST shape erasure: StringMap, IntMap, EnumValueMap/BalancedTree, HashMap, or the separately gated ObjectMap path.
2. Give each ordinary mutable native-key map object shared managed identity; lower set, remove, clear, array access, and all reads/iteration through typed operations.
3. Preserve exact key equality/order/hashCode contracts and make copy return a new shallow map identity whose later writes do not affect the source.
4. Carry key/value representations and capabilities through generic and package ABI descriptors.
5. Keep elixir.ElixirMap and declared native/framework maps raw and persistent; reject object-key support until the ObjectMap gate.

FAILURE MODES
Structural fallback for object keys, one-binding Map.put rebinding, treating every Haxe Map as one BEAM map, changing HashMap collision semantics, copying nested managed values incorrectly, or running iterator callbacks under lock are blockers.

TESTS
Direct/nested aliases for every mutator across String, Int, enum/tree, and hashCode key families; copy independence; missing/null values; collisions; iteration snapshots and mutation; Dynamic/generic/package flows; explicit native-map parity; object-key diagnostic remains until its owner lands.
acceptance_criteria: Every native-key ordinary Haxe map family preserves shared aliases for its complete mutation surface and exact copy/key behavior; typed specialization and package ABI are deterministic; object-key Map remains with ObjectMap and has no structural fallback; explicit native maps remain raw persistent terms; focused snapshots/runtime tests, upstream unitstd, inventory, minimum/primary toolchains, package smoke, WAE, full suites, examples, handwritten-output, and sentinel gates pass. No family is advertised while it mixes managed and persistent mutators.

title: Implement exact Array aliases and mutable array operations
description:
Haxe 4.3.7 specifies Array mutators as changing the array in place, and official unitstd plus the pinned reference probe show that an alias observes push, indexed writes, reverse, and the rest of the mutation family. Current BEAM-list receiver rebinding updates at most one lexical binding. Implement Array as one coherent managed collection without changing explicit target-native immutable list APIs.

FILES
- typed representation and semantic collection lowering under src/reflaxe/elixir/**
- the selected managed runtime facade/package
- focused Array snapshots and ordinary-Haxe runtime fixtures
- upstream unitstd manifest/evidence and stdlib parity inventory
design:
ALGORITHM
1. Classify ordinary Array<T> allocations, literals, parameters, fields, returns, generic instantiations, and package signatures as one managed collection ABI.
2. Lower indexed read/write and every mutator (push, pop, shift, unshift, insert, remove, splice, resize, reverse, sort, and related operations) to semantic managed-array operations with single evaluation and source result/exception behavior.
3. Make copy, concat, slice, map, and filter allocate independent arrays while preserving managed leaves and shallow-copy rules.
4. Run comparators/callbacks outside heap locks and define iteration/mutation behavior from Haxe 4.3.7 evidence.
5. Keep explicit native-list descriptors raw and persistent; never select representation from profile or final target shape.

FAILURE MODES
Partial per-method conversion, caller rebinding, a BEAM list hidden behind an identity token, late boxing, callback execution under lock, inconsistent nested/generic/package carriers, or silently converting explicit native lists are release blockers.

TESTS
Alias every mutator through locals, fields, returned values, Dynamic narrowing, generics, and a separately compiled package; cover shallow copies, nested managed leaves, exceptions/evaluation order, comparator mutation/throw, iteration, and explicit NativeList parity.
acceptance_criteria: All audited Array operations preserve alias-visible mutation and exact return/exception ordering; no managed Array mutator lowers to list append plus one-binding rebind; copy-producing APIs have independent collection identity; generic and separate-package carriers agree; explicit native lists remain raw persistent BEAM lists; focused snapshots/runtime tests, upstream unitstd, inventory, minimum/primary toolchains, package smoke, WAE, full suites, examples, handwritten-output, and sentinel gates pass. Rollout remains gated for the complete Array family until every mutator and boundary test is green.

title: Prove Haxe-authored React components through the PhoenixHx LiveReact integration
description:
Prove the preferred Haxe-first browser path for PhoenixHx LiveReact: an inner React component authored in Haxe, expressed with Genes TypeScript/TSX inline HXX, and consumed through the same static LiveReact registry without changing the server API or adding a bundler. Before the flagship consumers land, update the single canonical Lix dependency from the admitted genes-ts v1.36.7 baseline to the latest canonical release that passes the full downstream matrix. At planning time the official latest release is v1.36.8 at commit 7fc5aa2b72e9a5d6d5feaab9cb9ddfc08be121c6; reverify immediately before changing the pin.

## FILES

- tooling/phoenix_scaffold/src_haxe/phoenix_scaffold_tooling/GenesContract.hx
- regenerated root, scaffold, todo-app, and example-12 genes-ts descriptors
- focused Haxe React source and strict TypeScript/TSX inline-HXX fixture
- classic split-ESM compatibility fixtures
- static registry and trusted boundary fixtures
- source-map, React, Vite, browser, scaffold, example, and package evidence
- compatibility notes in the active LiveReact and Genes workflow documents

## ALGORITHM

1. Wait for the static registry and app-local wrapper foundation in haxe.elixir.codex-msb.5.
2. Capture the exact v1.36.7 generated artifacts, runtime traces, module/import ABI, DCE, source maps, and existing example/browser baseline.
3. Reverify the latest canonical genes-ts release and exact commit. Never use a sibling checkout, worktree, branch name, dirty tree, or local-only commit as the committed input.
4. Update only the Haxe-owned GenesContract, regenerate every owned descriptor, and download the exact release through a clean Lix cache path.
5. Run classic split-ESM parity for every current Genes-backed consumer before authoring new React behavior.
6. Implement one bounded React component in Haxe using Genes TypeScript/TSX inline HXX, closed props/events, the static registry, and the trusted LiveReact boundary.
7. Feed the generated module through Vite, prove strict type errors and React runtime behavior, and compare portable source maps.
8. Run example 12, todo-app, all other Genes-backed examples, scaffold lifecycle, and installed-package regression gates.
9. If the latest release exposes a Genes defect, retain the last admitted pin, keep this task open, reduce the defect generically in an isolated Genes worktree, and consume only an exact pushed SHA under the documented temporary-pin rules until a canonical commit or release lands.

## FAILURE MODES

Second bundler; React or LiveReact fork; machine-local Genes path; floating or unpushed pin; hand-editing generated descriptors; framework-specific Genes patches; different server API; weak prop/event types; raw bridge leakage; unreviewed generated output; TSX success with classic ESM regressions; stale or absolute source-map paths; todo-app or example-12 browser regression; claiming general Haxe React support from one component.

## TESTS

Clean Lix resolution; Haxe-owned pin regeneration; strict TypeScript/TSX inline-HXX positive and negative cases; classic ESM semantic/output/import/DCE parity; exact prop/event contract; Vite build; React runtime; portable source maps; scaffold apply/rerun/remove; every Genes-backed example compile/output/WAE/runtime lane; bounded example-12 and todo-app browser QA; installed-package smoke and path hygiene.

## VERIFICATION

Run focused Genes dual-profile gates first, then LiveReact registry and event tests, all Genes-backed example gates, async bounded example-12 and todo-app sentinels with focused Playwright, scaffold lifecycle, installed-package parity, documentation/path guards, and exact-head CI. Record the old and new exact version/commit identities and review generated classic ESM and TSX artifacts rather than treating compilation alone as evidence.

## ROLLOUT

This P1 conformance gate follows haxe.elixir.codex-msb.5 and blocks the independent LiveReact example and todo-app adoption. It remains experimental 1.x work and does not block Reflaxe.Elixir 1.0. Keep Vite as the sole bundler, Genes as the source compiler, and the classic ESM profile as a supported compatibility lane.
design: Use one exact canonical Lix-resolved genes-ts source. Admit a newer release only after the existing classic ESM corpus and the strict TypeScript/TSX inline-HXX React lane both pass. The Haxe-authored component uses the same static registry, trusted boundary, LiveReact server API, and Vite bundle as a TSX component. Generic Genes defects are fixed upstream through the documented worktree and exact pushed-SHA workflow; PhoenixHx carries no local compiler fork.
acceptance_criteria: The latest canonical genes-ts release observed at implementation time is pinned by exact commit through the Haxe-owned GenesContract and regenerated descriptors; one bounded Haxe-authored React component uses Genes TypeScript/TSX inline HXX with closed prop/event parity, static-registry consumption, Vite runtime, and portable source maps; every existing classic Genes consumer, including example 12 and todo-app, preserves reviewed module/import ABI, async/HXX, DCE, runtime, source maps, browser QA, scaffold lifecycle, and installed-package behavior; no second compiler source, local path, runtime fork, second bundler, framework-specific Genes patch, or weakened type boundary is introduced.
notes:
2026-07-18 scope promotion: the project owner selected genes-ts strict TypeScript/TSX as the Haxe-first LiveReact browser lane. This task remains broader end-to-end conformance, but the static-registry task now requires a focused Haxe/Genes fixture and depends on the vendored-to-pinned Genes migration. A machine-local Genes checkout path remains forbidden as a committed input.

Admission requires unchanged reviewed behavior for every existing Genes-backed example, especially examples/todo-app and examples/12-phoenix-chat, plus module/import ABI, async/HXX, DCE, source maps, Vite consumption, bounded browser QA, scaffold lifecycle, and installed-package smoke. title: Add static React island registry and app-local typed wrapper scaffolding
description:
A low-level LiveReact.react call is insufficient for safe ergonomic application authoring. Add a reusable static registry plus starter pattern for app-local typed wrappers and trusted browser boundaries without runtime discovery or a universal schema compiler.

## FILES

- integration manifest schema and parser under lib
- registry generator and canonical templates
- optional component generator Mix task
- starter Haxe wrapper and TypeScript/TSX boundary/contract templates
- registry, generator, HXX, TypeScript, and React tests
- examples migrate only in later tasks

## ALGORITHM

1. Finalize phoenixhx.live-react@1 topology and ownership fields.
2. Parse sorted component entries and reject duplicate or invalid names/modules/exports.
3. Render a signature-owned static registry and closed component-name type.
4. Scaffold hand-owned files only when absent.
5. Generate an app-local discoverable Haxe wrapper with static name, ssr=false, closed assigns, and direct inline HXX.
6. Generate a trusted boundary that strips raw bridge fields, validates public props, and exposes semantic callbacks.
7. Remove registry membership without deleting hand-owned implementation files.

## FAILURE MODES

Duplicate/ambient/dynamic names; unowned registry overwrite; rerun overwrites edited starter; invalid module/export; raw bridge reaches inner props; removal deletes business source; manifest becomes a universal prop schema; legacy/raw HXX required.

## TESTS

Deterministic registry snapshots; add/rerun/remove; invalid and duplicate diagnostics; unowned collision; recovery after generated deletion; TypeScript component-name typecheck; exact prop/boundary tests; Haxe positive/negative wrapper fixtures; assertion against dynamic import/runtime glob.

## VERIFICATION

Run focused registry/generator, HXX, TypeScript, React, Vite, formatting, drift, and ownership tests. Confirm rerun byte identity and untouched hand-owned files.

## ROLLOUT

Experimental static registry and starter. Keep a low-level manual wrapper escape hatch. Do not promise automatic general Haxe-to-TypeScript prop generation.
design: Generalize the closed project manifest and static registry. Generated registry/topology files remain signature-owned; Haxe and TypeScript business contracts become hand-owned after creation. Existing @:component discovery owns strict assigns. The trusted boundary narrows LiveReact capabilities before invoking inner first-party React code.
acceptance_criteria: A closed manifest generates a deterministic static typed registry; a starter yields a discoverable app-local Haxe wrapper and trusted browser boundary; identity and ssr posture are static; reruns/removal preserve hand-owned code; exact prop/component tests pass; no runtime discovery, compiler hard-code, broad bridge, or universal schema is introduced.
notes:
2026-07-17 contract freeze: schema id is phoenixhx.live-react@1. It records tool version, vite mode, project-relative package root, portable Mix identity, relative npm file: reference, explicit false capability posture, sorted component entries, and owned files/markers. Unknown newer schemas refuse writes; older schemas require an explicit tested ownership-preserving migration. Manifest paths are project-relative without .. and it is not a universal prop schema.
2026-07-17 generated-output gate: production behavior authored in Haxe must check in and review the resulting Elixir as a first-class artifact. It must be idiomatic, readable, byte-stable on regeneration, warnings-as-errors clean, and acceptable as handwritten code. 2026-07-17 dogfood boundary: implement deterministic registry normalization/rendering, component-contract validation, and related product logic in Haxe by default so this feature exercises Reflaxe.Elixir. Keep only the thin Mix entrypoint, filesystem/atomic-write boundary, Mix dependency introspection, and compiler-unavailable recovery path handwritten in Elixir. Any broader handwritten-Elixir exception must cite a concrete host-API or generated-output limitation. Checked-in generated Elixir must remain idiomatic enough for handwritten review.
2026-07-18 sequencing note: this remains the immediate implementation slice. Close the deterministic registry and app-local wrapper foundation first, then hand the bounded browser component to haxe.elixir.codex-a06. Keep the registry compiler-agnostic, but ensure its generated contract can consume Genes TypeScript/TSX modules produced from inline HXX without a special-case path.
2026-07-19 closure audit: the Haxe-authored registry/lifecycle implementation already satisfies this slice. It normalizes and sorts closed manifest entries, rejects duplicate/dynamic/escaping identities before writes, renders a signature-owned static registry and ComponentName type, scaffolds direct-inline-HXX app wrappers with fixed name and ssr=false, narrows the stock LiveReact bridge in a trusted TSX adapter, and treats wrapper/boundary/inner source as hand-owned on rerun and removal. title: Prove managed cross-module ABI dispatch and inheritance
description: Prove that managed references form one stable language ABI across modules and separately compiled packages rather than only working inside one generated module.
design: Implement exported receiver, parameter, result, field, effect, callback, generic-capability, and runtime representation signatures. Route virtual dispatch through managed class tags while preserving the same handle. Validate inheritance, interfaces, overrides, generic witnesses, dependency manifests, cache invalidation, and generated-to-handwritten facade entry points. Reject mixed legacy tagged-map and managed-handle artifacts deterministically; never add an automatic compatibility wrapper because allocation identity and alias history cannot be recovered.

title: Harden closure ownership GC process and native boundaries
description: Close the lifecycle and interop gaps that prevent arbitrary managed-reference graphs from being release-ready.

Handle nested carriers in containers, same-node process sharing, per-operation linearizability, remote snapshot or deterministic rejection, incremental or dirty-scheduler collection, stale handles, NIF upgrades, DCE, Inspect, JSON, materialization, and typed Ecto, Phoenix, OTP, exception, and extern boundary diagnostics. title: Complete Dynamic reflection RTTI patterns and graph serialization
description: Make managed class, anonymous, collection, and ObjectMap graphs obey the Haxe Dynamic, pattern, Reflect, Type, Serializer, and Unserializer contracts, including aliases and cycles.

Hoist batch field projections before target patterns and guards, bind aliases to original handles, and make wrong-class or missing-field reads fail as source patterns require. Route carrier reflection through visible fields and class tags while retaining native-map behavior at explicit boundaries. Serializer caches use object identity and install entries before descent. Unserializer allocates empty carriers or ObjectMaps, caches before filling, and restores aliases and cycles. Preserve class versus anonymous forms, method identity, custom hooks, resolver behavior, inspection, and wire compatibility without exposing runtime IDs or resource terms.

title: Implement exact WeakMap semantics over managed identities

Define entry removal and iterator observations from the pinned Haxe contract, keep values and nested carrier edges according to that contract, and integrate weak processing with tracing rather than VM pointer guesses or periodic TTL cleanup. Native interop keys must diagnose or use an explicit boundary.

title: Restore exact ListSort node identity and mutation semantics

Preserve stability, left-to-right behavior, final next and prev invariants, and partial writes when a comparator throws. Diagnose representation conflicts rather than rebuilding native value nodes or adding traversal limits.

title: Implement exact ObjectMap and object-key Map specialization

Copy creates a new map identity and shallow entries; iterators snapshot entries outside locks. Generic object-key Map requires managed identity. Ordinary StringMap and IntMap follow the audited managed-map family when their Haxe mutators expose aliases, while explicitly target-native immutable maps remain raw BEAM maps. title: Implement the managed-reference core and alias-visible fields

Emit versioned representation manifests for exported types and callables. Add semantic allocation, get, put, identity, dispatch, collection, closure, dynamic, boxing, and materialization operations. Managed builders must never emit EReceiverEffect. Validate before initial receiver-effect lowering, lower managed operations before persistent-value passes, and validate again before printing. title: Choose the managed heap implementation and distribution ABI
description:
## Decision

After the bounded feasibility spike and qualified licensing decision, select the production managed-heap implementation, runtime package ABI, build and artifact policy, and supported platform matrix before compiler scaffolding or native production code lands.

## Rationale

The repository currently ships source-oriented Haxelib and Mix packages with no NIF build system. A native or hybrid heap adds scheduler, crash, upgrade, security, checksum, source-build, prebuilt artifact, OS, OTP, and licensing obligations. These are public runtime constraints and must be chosen deliberately from evidence.

## Alternatives Considered

- Direct C NIF with native heap and collector.
- Rust or Rustler NIF with native heap and collector.
- Minimal native lease and root registry with an Elixir or ETS-owned traced heap.
- Source-only native builds versus verified prebuilt artifacts.
- Runtime code embedded in generated applications versus a separately versioned Mix or Hex runtime package.
- Rejecting native code and threading an explicit functional heap through all generated calls and closures.

The task closes only after the feasibility and licensing evidence selects among these alternatives.
design: Choose the native implementation language, native-versus-Elixir heap split, resource and upgrade protocol, build system, runtime module boundary, Haxelib and Mix or Hex integration, source-build and prebuilt policy, supported OS and OTP matrix, security review surface, deterministic release inputs, and failure behavior. Incorporate the qualified licensing and generated-runtime distribution decision rather than inferring legal policy.
acceptance_criteria: A durable decision selects one implementable design; haxe.elixir.codex-0yn.4 is resolved and package licenses are explicit; OTP 25 plus primary Ubuntu and macOS lanes have a build plan; hot upgrade, dirty scheduler, stale handle, checksum, source-build, and rollback behavior are specified; current release-package parity tests have named extensions; compiler scaffolding is still byte-stable and no unsupported API is advertised.

title: Prove managed-reference runtime feasibility with a bounded spike
description: Test whether BEAM resource leases plus a tracing managed heap can provide allocation identity, alias-visible mutation, strong and weak graph edges, cyclic reclamation, and same-node process sharing without scheduler or package failures. This is an evidence spike, not production support.

Exercise last-lease destruction, root races, direct and nested carrier edges, a doubly linked cycle, weak entries, concurrent operations, stale or wrong-node handles, hot upgrade constraints, and bounded collector work. title: Adopt the selective managed-reference ABI for exact Haxe reference semantics
description:
## Decision

Adopt one selective managed-reference ABI for ordinary Haxe classes and anonymous objects when identity or alias-visible mutation is semantically observable. Keep explicitly native Ecto, Phoenix, OTP, JSON, tuple, list, string, exception, and extern values on native BEAM representations with typed diagnostics or explicit boxing and materialization at conflicts. This authorizes gated architecture and feasibility work, not speculative production lowering.

## Rationale

Exact ObjectMap, ListSort, WeakMap, reflection, and cyclic serialization require allocation-time identity, shared mutation, and graph lifetime. Persistent BEAM maps plus local rebinding cannot update aliases, and insertion-time identity cannot recover an allocation identity that was never represented. The complete applicable Haxe stdlib remains a 1.0 requirement, so these APIs cannot be left structurally approximate or permanently unsupported.

## Alternatives Considered

- Structural BEAM maps with hidden identity fields: rejected because visible state still does not mutate through aliases and hidden fields leak across boundaries.
- Wrapping only at ObjectMap or ListSort use: rejected because identity and aliases are already lost.
- ETS, process dictionaries, Agents, or one process per object without term-lifetime leases: rejected as the exact object heap because entries do not follow the last handle and cyclic lifetime remains unsolved.
- Rebuilding linked nodes or weakening serialization: rejected because it changes public Haxe semantics.
- Narrowing the 1.0 stdlib promise: rejected by the authorized direction; release guards remain strict.
design: Freeze semantic invariants and the selective representation boundary in a durable architecture document. Treat a GC-aware managed heap rooted by BEAM resource leases as the chosen direction, while requiring a bounded feasibility gate before selecting the native implementation language or native-versus-Elixir heap split. Require explicit compiler-owned closure capture edges before claiming cyclic graph reclamation. Make same-node sharing, remote snapshot/rejection, reflection, equality, serialization, inspection, JSON, Ecto/Phoenix interop, DCE, packaging, licensing, and minimum-toolchain behavior part of the ABI contract.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed architecture document states the decision, alternatives, invariants, component ownership, ordering constraints, boundary rules, unresolved gates, staged delivery, and rollback boundaries; haxe.elixir.codex-0yn.10.3 is decomposed into independently verifiable child work with dependency ordering; licensing/distribution and native packaging are explicit blockers; no ObjectMap/ListSort support claim or behavior-changing implementation lands as part of this decision task; documentation and task-graph checks pass.
notes: Accepted at baseline 6dc9c0dff1d8ca44c44394c0bd195eda17400ba7 after whole-repository architecture review. Durable contract: docs/05-architecture/MANAGED_REFERENCE_ABI.md. Validation: guard:docs-links, guard:stdlib-api-inventory, selected bead lint, dependency-cycle check, orphan check, and path hygiene. No compiler or runtime behavior changed.
close_reason: Selective managed-reference ABI accepted, documented, decomposed into gated work, and validated without enabling unsupported behavior.

title: Run the full stdlib tests against source and release packages
description: Individual module fixes do not by themselves prove that the shipped compiler supports the complete applicable Haxe stdlib as one coherent contract.
design: Regenerate the final inventory, run all available upstream unitstd plus focused local tests, compile generated Elixir with warnings as errors on minimum and primary toolchains, and repeat through the installed release package. Review every not-applicable reason and every Term/Dynamic or target escape hatch in the stdlib boundary. Publish a concise evidence report that a release reviewer can verify.

title: Close Haxe IO, network, SSL, process, thread, and database gaps
description: Current BEAM mappings still reject or narrow several runtime-relevant sys and IO operations, including caller-buffer reads, parts of sockets and SSL, lifecycle bridges, condition variables, and direct sys.db APIs. Full 1.0 stdlib support cannot leave these as documented exclusions.
design: Inventory exact Haxe semantics first, then map them to BEAM-native resources, processes, messages, binaries, drivers, or compatibility state without pretending immutable values mutate. Where Ecto is the preferred Elixir-first API, keep that recommendation while still providing the Haxe stdlib compatibility contract required by portable code. Split ambiguous architectural work for external review before landing broad repairs.

Coordinate stateful carrier identity, alias, same-node process transfer, lifetime, and cleanup with haxe.elixir.codex-0yn.10.3.10; a process-dictionary make_ref implementation is only partial until both API and carrier/lifecycle evidence pass.

title: Close Haxe core, collection, reflection, and serialization gaps
description: Close the runtime-relevant core, collection, reflection, RTTI, serialization, template, XML, ZIP, atomic, resource, and related utility gaps. Reference-dependent APIs now have an accepted selective managed-reference direction, but remain unsupported until the gated runtime and compiler slices prove exact semantics.
design: Run two explicit streams under this epic. The managed-reference stream follows docs/05-architecture/MANAGED_REFERENCE_ABI.md: feasibility, licensing and package decision, semantic scaffolding, carrier core, ObjectMap, ListSort, WeakMap, graph reflection and serialization, lifecycle and boundary hardening, then release evidence. The remaining value-semantic API rows are classified and split independently. Never lower reference-dependent operations structurally, wrap identity only at insertion, or claim support from compilation alone.
acceptance_criteria: Every applicable API owned by this epic has ordinary-Haxe runtime evidence and warning-clean generated output; all managed-reference gates are closed before ObjectMap, ListSort, WeakMap, reference caches, or cyclic carrier graphs are marked supported; native Ecto, Phoenix, OTP, JSON, and extern shapes retain their declared boundary ABI; remaining value-semantic rows are closed through focused children; source/package, minimum/primary toolchain, examples, and inventory guards pass.

title: List every Haxe stdlib API and make CI catch missing tests
description: The module-level gap report measures local files, not API support, and the upstream unitstd manifest has many no-spec rows. Major 1 needs an API-level source of truth derived from the pinned Haxe standard library.
design: Parse the pinned Haxe stdlib public surface into a deterministic inventory of modules, types, fields, overloads, and target conditions. Record implementation ownership, support state, version, and exact evidence. Allow not-applicable only for compile-time/compiler-display or other-target-only declarations with a narrow reason. Make CI detect new, removed, unclassified, partially covered, or stale entries.
acceptance_criteria: The complete pinned public stdlib surface is inventoried at API level; every row has an allowed applicability, implementation-owner, and evidence state; no runtime-relevant row is unclassified; CI regeneration is deterministic and fails on drift, unsupported/partial/unknown/untested runtime states, missing evidence, or stale documentation; module counts and API counts are shown separately so local override count is never presented as support coverage.
notes:
Implemented two fail-closed checks. Normal CI runs the deterministic inventory guard and rejects pinned-Haxe surface drift, missing or stale policy rows, invalid classifications, missing evidence files, and closed blocker references. The explicit release-readiness guard rejects every runtime row that is unsupported, partial, unknown, or lacks exact API-level runtime evidence; the release-policy loader also refuses to mark complete-haxe-stdlib complete while any such row remains. This keeps honest work-in-progress visible without making all 0.x CI permanently red, while making 1.0 fail closed. Current pinned Haxe 4.3.7 result: 204 modules, 3,692 public API rows, 1,981 runtime-relevant rows, and 1,981 release blockers. Verified with npm test, npm run ci:guards, focused inventory/release tests, deterministic regeneration, path hygiene, and the expected failing release-readiness guard.
Exact-SHA CI run 29411168009 exposed that the Java inventory profile depended on this workstation's global hxjava install. The task was reopened. Added haxe_libraries/hxjava.hxml with hxjava 4.2.0 pinned through the existing Lix install/run contract, validated that descriptor in the inventory tests, and recorded the adapter version in generated inventory metadata. Reproduced a clean machine with an empty HAXE_LIBCACHE: npx lix download installed nine scoped libraries and guard:stdlib-api-inventory passed with the same 3,692 rows. The full ci:guards bundle and 10 focused inventory tests pass; the 1.0 readiness guard still correctly reports 1,981 blockers.
Exact-SHA CI run 29412068381 found a second clean-checkout issue: the inventory launched typed profiles from an OS temporary directory, so the Java backend's nested `haxelib run hxjava` could not see the repository's Lix scope and fell back to a globally installed library. The runner now keeps temporary output paths but executes Haxe from the repository root, where Lix can find the pinned adapter. A regression test locks that working-directory contract. Verified from a fully isolated Haxe root with an empty legacy haxelib repository and empty library cache: `npx lix download` installed all nine scoped libraries and the deterministic 204-module/3,692-API guard passed. The full `npm run ci:guards` bundle also passes, including all pass-scope byte-parity checks.
close_reason: The pinned API inventory and fail-closed release policy are complete and now reproduce from a clean machine without global Haxe library state.

title: Prevent 1.0 until the full Haxe stdlib is supported
description: The release policy currently requires a human approval record, but it does not list complete Haxe stdlib support as a requirement that tooling can check. Some roadmap and readiness pages also say complete stdlib coverage can wait until after 1.0, which now contradicts the product decision.
design: Add explicit requirements for each stable major release and reject approval while any requirement is unfinished. List complete Haxe stdlib support alongside the other decisions that remain before 1.0. Rewrite roadmap and readiness wording in plain language, define what complete support means, distinguish tested upstream fallback from a local override, and document the post-1.0 typed Elixir stdlib and Mix-dependency adoption direction without presenting planned tooling as implemented.

close_reason: Major 1 now has named machine-checked requirements and cannot be approved while complete Haxe stdlib support or another requirement is unfinished. The roadmap and support docs define complete API-level evidence, explain current gaps in plain language, and track separate 1.x work for a fully typed Elixir stdlib and safe Mix dependency adoption. Release tests, stdlib guards, docs links, dependency-cycle checks, the full repository guard bundle, and npm test all pass.

title: Complete the Haxe standard library before 1.0
description: Version 1.0 must support the complete public Haxe standard-library surface that applies to generated Elixir programs. The current matrix still contains explicitly unsupported and partially implemented runtime behavior, while the module gap report only measures local target ownership and cannot prove support by itself.
design: Build a machine-readable inventory from the pinned Haxe standard library. Classify compile-time-only and other-target-only modules as not applicable with a source-backed reason. Every runtime-relevant public module, type, field, and operation must use a verified upstream fallback, compiler lowering, BEAM-specific override, or semantics-preserving helper. Resolve every current unsupported, partial, unknown, and untested runtime entry; do not reduce the count by copying unchanged upstream files. Require ordinary Haxe source tests, generated-output review where shape matters, BEAM runtime conformance, minimum and primary toolchains, warning-free generated Elixir, and source/package parity.
