title: Preserve lambda binders inside Result switch branches
description: A lambda authored directly inside a switch branch can capture the branch payload instead of its own parameter. In the OTP runtime prototype, case Ok(agent): Agent.get(agent, (value:Int) -> value) emitted Agent.get(agent, fn _value -> agent end), and Agent.update emitted fn _value -> agent + 5 end. Moving the same callbacks into a typed helper function emits correct lambdas, isolating the defect to binder handling across the switch-clause boundary.
design: Trace the typed lambda and clause binder through switch lowering, binder canonicalization, unused-parameter analysis, and closure capture. Fix the earliest incorrect binder identity mapping; do not special-case Agent, callback names, or generated variable names. Preserve nested shadowing and outer captures.
acceptance_criteria: A minimal ordinary-Haxe regression authored inside a Result switch branch emits callbacks that reference their own parameters; runtime assertions cover identity and arithmetic callbacks; negative coverage preserves intentional capture of the branch payload and nested shadowing; no name-based heuristic or target injection is used; full snapshots, runtime smoke, examples, and result invariants pass.
close_reason: Preserved lexical callback parameters inside Result branches with centralized free-variable analysis and scope-aware rewriting; added ordinary-Haxe snapshot/runtime regressions, direct OTP Agent callback coverage, clearer docs, and passed the full compiler, stdlib, examples, and todo-app browser QA matrix.

title: Preserve inner state in reducer callbacks nested inside outer reducers
description: A reducer-required inner loop nested inside an outer reducer can return the outer callback state instead of its own accumulator. Reproduction: an outer loop appends rows while an inner loop performs two row.push calls per item; generated Elixir ends the inner Enum.reduce callback with rows_acc, producing empty rows.
design: The typed loop builder already emits the correct inner and outer accumulator tails. Fix the earliest corrupting AST stage instead: add a reusable children-first traversal boundary to ElixirASTTransformer, then make ReduceAccAliasUnify scan self-appends, collect aliases, and rewrite only the current reducer callback scope. Treat nested EFn nodes as opaque lexical owners; the enclosing whole-AST traversal processes nested reducers independently before their parents. Do not classify generated names or repair printed Elixir.
acceptance_criteria: A Haxe-authored runtime regression proves nested two-append reducers preserve every inner row; generated Elixir returns row_acc from the inner callback and rows_acc from the outer callback; nested conditionals, break/continue/return, exceptions, evaluation order, full snapshots, runtime smoke, examples, and todo QA remain green.
notes: Root-cause trace: LoopBuilder output was correct; ReduceAccAliasUnify first changed inner row_acc assignments/tail to outer rows_acc because its flat transformNode scan crossed the nested EFn. Regression coverage now exercises ordinary Haxe nested loops with two inner Array.push calls and asserts every row at runtime; nested_loop_infrastructure locks the generated inner row_acc and outer rows_acc shapes. Verification: focused snapshot/runtime; npm test (all 398 positive outputs parse, 91/91 negative fixtures, 255 Mix tests); Haxe ExUnit stdlib 132/132; examples compile/output/WAE/runtime; handwritten-output; package source/install parity; async todo sentinel RUN_ID=1784027294 with 5/5 Playwright specs.
close_reason: Preserved lexical reducer ownership by stopping alias discovery and rewriting at nested EFn boundaries; added generated-output and Haxe runtime regressions and passed the full compiler, stdlib, examples, package, and todo-app browser QA matrix.

title: Approve or reject the Reflaxe.Elixir 1.0 release
description: Approve or reject Reflaxe.Elixir 1.0 for the exact reviewed release candidate and published support list. Major 1 requires complete support for every public Haxe standard-library API that belongs on generated Elixir programs, plus completed correctness, build safety, package, distribution, and external-test evidence. A version-number edit, marketing deadline, narrowed stdlib claim, or nearby green commit cannot approve it.
design: Review the published support list, complete Haxe stdlib inventory and behavior results, all open P0/P1 issues, external test report, package origin and hashes, supported toolchains, generated-file ownership behavior, licensing decision, remaining security risks, performance comparison, and documented framework/version bounds. Reject 1.0 if any named release requirement is pending or any runtime-relevant Haxe stdlib entry is unsupported, partial, unknown, or untested. If approved, record the durable decision and date before a later reviewed breaking Conventional Commit may produce version 1.0.0.
acceptance_criteria: A signed-off decision names the exact commit and package candidate, complete applicable Haxe stdlib promise, broader support list, external test period, evidence links, known remaining risks, and reviewers; all blocking dependencies and release requirements are complete; release/manifest.json remains unchanged on rejection or receives a valid durable approval record only when every requirement is satisfied; the decision itself does not publish, move, or recreate a release tag.

title: Test one 1.0 release candidate in clean external projects
description: Project-local CI does not by itself prove that a clean adopter can install the immutable package, add one module to an existing Phoenix project, upgrade without stale files or collisions, and roll back predictably. The final 1.0 decision needs evidence from clean workspaces over a defined test period.
design: Use one unchanged release candidate in clean workspaces outside the repository. Exercise fresh install, generated project, one-module gradual adoption, complete Haxe stdlib conformance, in-place and isolated output, minimum and primary toolchains, source/package parity, previous-release upgrade, source/namespace deletion, collision rejection, and rollback. Record exact artifacts, commits, checksums, test duration, failures, and resolutions.
acceptance_criteria: A durable external-test report covers every designed scenario with immutable package identifiers and exact commands; haxe.elixir.codex-0yn.10 and every other release requirement are complete; no unresolved P0/P1 issue remains; the candidate runs the complete applicable Haxe stdlib conformance suite without unsupported/partial/unknown/untested runtime entries or warnings; at least one clean external Phoenix workspace completes install, compile, runtime tests, upgrade, stale cleanup, collision rejection, and rollback; latest exact candidate CI is green for the full required evidence set.

title: Make the stdlib tests pass without compiler warnings
description: The Haxe-authored ExUnit stdlib suite provides required behavior evidence for 1.0, but it currently tolerates compiler warnings. Repeated warning noise can hide a new warning, so the complete suite must pass without unexplained warnings before 1.0.
design: Classify each current warning by its real source, fix compiler or fixture causes at their owner, and run generated stdlib ExUnit with warnings treated as errors in a way that works on the minimum Elixir version. Do not suppress broad warning classes or weaken upstream behavior tests.
acceptance_criteria: The complete stdlib runtime suite compiles and runs without unexplained warnings on minimum and primary toolchains; CI fails on a newly introduced warning; upstream unitstd and focused local runtime behavior remain green; any unavoidable toolchain warning is narrowly versioned and documented; this task is complete before the final stdlib audit and external release-candidate test.

title: Publish and test the exact Reflaxe.Elixir 1.0 support list
description: The repository has substantial feature documentation but no single checked list tying supported Haxe language forms, the complete applicable Haxe standard library, compiler flags, annotations, externs, generated module and function names, Mix tasks, framework APIs, and version bounds to executable evidence. Version 1.0 needs one reviewable support list, and it may not exclude an applicable Haxe stdlib API merely because that API is difficult to implement.
design: Create a checked inventory with supported, experimental, internal, unsupported, and non-applicable categories. The Haxe stdlib portion is stricter: every runtime-relevant public API for the pinned Haxe version must be supported and tested before 1.0, so unsupported, partial, unknown, and untested are unfinished states rather than allowed exclusions. Compile-time-only, compiler-display, and other-target-only modules may be non-applicable only with a narrow source-backed reason. Link every supported entry to compile and runtime evidence and show raw Elixir behavior where the mapping is not obvious. Include compatibility rules for generated module and function names and call shapes, Mix and build behavior, source and package use, and framework and toolchain versions.
acceptance_criteria: One canonical inventory lists the 1.0 language, complete applicable Haxe stdlib, framework, build, and generated module and function surface; each supported entry links to executable evidence and version bounds; the Haxe stdlib inventory has zero runtime-relevant unsupported, partial, unknown, or untested entries; non-applicable entries have narrow auditable reasons; docs-link and manifest guards reject missing or contradictory entries; public README, APIs, examples, support matrix, limitations, versioning policy, release requirements, and release notes agree.

title: Decide the 1.0 licensing and generated-runtime distribution policy
description:
## Decision

Choose the 1.0 licensing and distribution policy for compiler use, generated source, externs, and shipped runtime/support modules.

## Rationale

The repository is GPL-3.0 and generated applications may include support code originating here. Broad commercial Elixir positioning needs a qualified and visible policy before adopters can evaluate distribution risk. Engineering documentation must not infer legal obligations on its own.

## Alternatives Considered

- Keep GPL-3.0 as-is with explicit adopter guidance.
- Add a generated-output or runtime exception.
- License runtime/extern components separately.
- Offer dual licensing if ownership and contribution rights permit it.
design: Obtain qualified legal review rather than inferring obligations in engineering docs. Evaluate keeping GPL-3.0 as-is with explicit adopter guidance, adding an output/runtime exception, separately licensing runtime/extern components, or dual licensing. Record ownership and contribution prerequisites, package boundaries, migration impact, and how the chosen policy appears near installation and distribution instructions.
acceptance_criteria: A durable reviewed decision states the licenses for compiler, Mix integration, externs, generated source, and shipped runtime/support modules; README, package metadata, LICENSE/NOTICE material, and licensing guide agree; commercial and open-source adoption examples state what users must evaluate without presenting engineering text as legal advice; any relicensing has verified contributor/ownership authority.

title: Prove a bounded OTP lifecycle contract or narrow 1.0 scope
description: Compile examples cover GenServer, Supervisor, Registry, process, and child-spec shapes, but broad production wording needs runtime evidence for lifecycle and failure behavior. The 1.0 contract must either prove selected OTP semantics or explicitly exclude unproven paths instead of treating API-shaped output as operational parity.
design: Inventory each documented OTP surface and map it to raw Elixir behavior. Add Haxe-authored runtime conformance for initialization, calls/casts, state transitions, stop reasons, crashes, restart policy, child specs, registry references, mailbox behavior, and exception boundaries where claimed. Mark unsupported or experimental semantics clearly rather than inventing broad compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: The stable contract enumerates the supported OTP subset; every included lifecycle/failure behavior has runtime evidence against normal Elixir/OTP expectations; unsupported paths fail clearly or are documented outside the stable tier; generated output is warnings-as-errors clean; minimum and primary OTP/Elixir lanes, source/package parity, examples, and todo QA pass.
close_reason: Defined a small 1.0 OTP boundary instead of claiming broad lifecycle parity. Added Haxe-authored, warnings-as-errors runtime coverage for local Process, Task, and Agent operations; corrected closure spawn and self mappings to Kernel; kept typed application/child-spec boot evidence; documented raw Elixir equivalents and explicit GenServer, Supervisor failure/restart, Registry, TaskSupervisor, mailbox, distributed OTP, and upgrade exclusions; added minimum-toolchain CI coverage; and passed compiler, stdlib, Mix, examples, package-source, generated-output, docs, and Phoenix browser QA. The separately tracked P1 callback-binder bug 3qh.26 remains outside this subset.

title: Make generated Elixir ownership and cleanup fail closed
description:
## Problem

In-place generation can target paths beside hand-written Phoenix code, while current write and clean paths do not provide one authoritative ownership mechanism for every generated application module. A conflicting write can overwrite a differing file, and clean or upgrade behavior can miss generated files that lack the current marker.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure generated Elixir inside a Phoenix source tree that also contains hand-written modules.
2. Place an unowned file at a future generated target path, or remove a Haxe source whose generated application file lacks the marker used by clean.
3. Regenerate, upgrade, or run the current clean path.
4. Observe that collision prevention, stale deletion, and clean do not share one fail-closed ownership record for every path.
design: Define one manifest-backed generated-file ownership protocol shared by compiler output, optional formatting, Mix clean, upgrades, and rollback. Reject writes to unowned existing files; identify generated files without relying only on module text markers; delete stale owned files when sources or namespaces disappear; make manifest updates atomic; recover safely from interrupted builds; preserve isolated materialized output as a supported alternative.
acceptance_criteria: Tests prove first generation, unchanged regeneration, owned update, stale deletion, namespace move, interrupted manifest recovery, clean, upgrade, downgrade/rollback, and source/package parity; a hand-written collision fails before modifying either file; no clean operation removes an unowned file; Phoenix gradual-adoption examples exercise in-place and isolated modes; generated output remains deterministic.
close_reason: Implemented versioned hash-owned manifests, staged transactional publication, fail-closed collision/clean/recovery behavior, lifecycle regressions, example documentation, and package parity validation.

title: Track every effective Haxe build input in Mix invalidation
description:
## Problem

The Mix compiler currently decides freshness from one configured source directory, path-oriented configuration data, and source mtimes. HXML contents, defines, library resolution, compiler/toolchain identity, and additional classpaths such as shared source roots can change without forcing regeneration, allowing stale Elixir to survive a normal mix compile.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Compile a Mix project whose Haxe build references a nested HXML or an additional classpath outside the primary source_dir.
2. Change only that HXML, a relevant define/library setting, or a source file in the additional root.
3. Run the normal incremental mix compile path.
4. Observe that the current freshness inputs may report no rebuild even though effective compiler input changed.
design: Model the effective Haxe build graph as deterministic tracked inputs. Include recursively referenced HXML content, all source/classpath roots, relevant defines and output settings, scoped library resolution, compiler/Reflaxe identity, and generated configuration. Prefer content fingerprints or Mix manifest data over a single newest-mtime heuristic. Keep watch and clean behavior bounded and test both changed and unchanged builds.
acceptance_criteria: Focused Mix tests prove that edits to every effective source root, nested HXML, define/config value, library/compiler identity, and shared classpath trigger exactly one rebuild; unchanged inputs remain no-op; removed roots and files cannot leave stale generated output; timestamp tests contain real assertions; examples using src_shared rebuild correctly; package/source paths and minimum supported Elixir pass.
close_reason: Replaced single-root mtime invalidation with a deterministic content fingerprint covering recursive HXML (including -C/-r aliases), every Haxe classpath, resources, resolved libraries/package metadata, toolchain and stdlib identity, relevant environment/configuration, and declared macro inputs. Unified direct/server/watcher toolchain and manifest ownership, made legacy/unwritable manifests fail closed, captured pre-compile fingerprints to prevent input-change races, added synthetic and todo src_shared regressions, updated readiness/docs, and passed full compiler, Mix, examples, package, stdlib, budget, policy, and browser QA.

title: Prepare Reflaxe.Elixir for a trustworthy 1.0 release
description: Define and satisfy the evidence-backed requirements for Reflaxe.Elixir 1.0. The complete public Haxe standard-library surface that belongs on generated Elixir programs must be supported and tested. The documented language and framework APIs must behave correctly; generated-source adoption and cleanup must protect hand-written files; release packages must behave like the tested source checkout; distribution policy must be deliberate; and clean external users must be able to install, upgrade, roll back, and operate the supported paths. This does not promise every framework version, operating system, third-party BEAM library, or possible Haxe program shape.
design: Treat executable evidence as authoritative over README claims. Close all known P0/P1 defects; publish the exact supported API and version list; require zero unsupported, partial, unknown, or untested runtime-relevant Haxe stdlib APIs; test effective build inputs and generated-file ownership safely; decide licensing/distribution policy with qualified review; prove the documented OTP boundary; test one unchanged release candidate in clean external projects for a defined period; then record an explicit approve-or-reject decision for 1.0. Keep complete typed Elixir stdlib breadth and automatic Mix-dependency adoption after 1.0, but never defer Haxe stdlib correctness.
acceptance_criteria: Every child blocker is closed, including complete Haxe stdlib support in haxe.elixir.codex-0yn.10; the exact supported API and version list is published and backed by executable tests; every applicable public Haxe stdlib API has positive compile and BEAM runtime evidence with no unsupported, partial, unknown, or untested runtime entry; clean release-package install, gradual adoption, upgrade, stale deletion, collision rejection, rollback, minimum and primary toolchains, examples, source/package parity, and runtime/browser paths pass while testing one unchanged release candidate in independent real-world projects for a defined period; no known P0/P1 defect remains in scope; release/manifest.json records a reviewed major-1 approval only after every named release requirement is complete.

title: Preserve nested array comprehensions over dynamic iterables
description:
## Problem

The existing core/array_comprehension_nested fixture compiles a nested dynamic comprehension through nested generated accumulators. The inner accumulator tail is lost or substituted, so the outer result appends empty rows instead of mapped values.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Compile Haxe equivalent to [for (x in source) [for (y in source) x * y]] where source is dynamically iterable.
2. Run the generated Elixir with [1, 2, 3].
3. Observe empty or lost inner rows instead of [[1,2,3],[2,4,6],[3,6,9]].
design: Fix the earliest typed/preprocessor or comprehension-builder boundary so the inner fresh accumulator remains identifiable by TVar.id and its value flows into the outer append. Prefer nested Enum.map/comprehension output where proven. Do not key the repair on g names, post-process generated text, or weaken accumulator remapping. Keep ordinary nested reducers, shadowed user locals, exceptions, and evaluation order intact.
acceptance_criteria: A Haxe-authored runtime test proves dynamic iterable nested comprehensions return [[1,2,3],[2,4,6],[3,6,9]]; generated Elixir uses sound nested map/comprehension or equivalent reducers with no lost inner tail; typed-ID shadowing and outer accumulator remaps have focused negative coverage; source/package parity, full snapshots, stdlib runtime, examples, and todo QA remain green.
close_reason: Preserved nested dynamic comprehension values by allowing exact-TVar-proven tail accumulators to collapse directly to Enum.map under an outer name remap; added Haxe runtime coverage, updated the generated Elixir snapshot, retained all fallback reducer output, and passed full CI-equivalent, examples, source/package, stdlib, and todo-app browser QA.

title: Preserve break and continue in reducer-lowered accumulator loops
description:
## Problem

Accumulator loops containing source break or continue correctly fall back from the fresh-array Enum.map proof, but the established Enum.reduce path can emit uncaught internal throw(:break) or throw(:continue) control carriers. This predates the map optimization and appears in existing loop snapshots.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Author a Haxe accumulation loop whose body uses break or continue.
2. Compile it through the normal reducer-lowering path.
3. Run the generated Elixir.
4. Observe an uncaught internal loop-control throw instead of Haxe loop behavior.
design: Reuse the existing reduce_while loop-control state and wrapLoopControlTry conventions. Preserve accumulator state on continue, halt with current state on break, keep non-local return carriers distinct, and avoid changing loops without break/continue.
acceptance_criteria: Minimal Haxe-authored runtime tests prove break halts and continue advances in array/list accumulation loops; generated Elixir uses reduce_while or an equivalent caught carrier with no uncaught internal control throw; return, nested loops, exceptions, persistent iterators, snapshots, stdlib runtime, and examples remain green.
close_reason: Implemented reducer-local break/continue carriers with exact accumulator state, distinct non-local-return tagging, Haxe runtime regressions, snapshot coverage, and documentation; full npm test, example QA, stdlib runtime, and todo-app Playwright sentinel are green.

title: Lower tuple-shaped anonymous-object field access consistently
description: A function returning a Haxe anonymous object shaped as {_1, _2} emits an Elixir tuple, but accessing the returned value through tupleValue._1 or tupleValue._2 emits map-dot access (tuple_value._1) and raises KeyError at runtime. The existing tuple_elem_access snapshot does not execute field access on a function-returned tuple, so this semantic gap was found while extending non-Void tail runtime coverage.
design: Fix tuple representation and accessor lowering at the typed-expression/AST source of truth. Do not post-process generated Elixir or special-case fixture names. Decide whether {_1, _2} is always a tuple representation or preserve map representation consistently, then make construction, return, assignment, field access, pattern matching, and typing agree.
acceptance_criteria: A minimal Haxe runtime regression returns {_1: "tuple", _2: 4} from a function and safely reads both fields after assignment; generated Elixir uses consistent tuple construction plus elem/2 access (or a consistently map-based representation); existing tuple, object-literal, pattern, snapshot, runtime, examples, package parity, and todo sentinel gates remain green; architecture docs describe the chosen tuple-shaped anonymous-object contract.
notes:
Root cause fixed at the typed AST source of truth. AnonymousTupleShape now recognizes only complete contiguous _1.._N portable shapes or _0.._N-1 native-extern shapes; ObjectBuilder, FieldAccessBuilder, AssignmentBuilder, and the remaining FAnon fallback share that classifier. Tuple construction emits ETuple, reads and Haxe object-pattern binds emit elem/2, and local updates rebind through put_elem/3; mixed and gapped numeric shapes remain maps. Expanded the existing tuple regression into executable zero/one-based, nested, pattern, mutation, and negative-map coverage and added it to runtime smoke. Updated affected stdlib/Phoenix/OTP goldens, the mappings guide, compilation architecture, changelog, and the no-unrequested-upstream-PR agent policy. Local verification green: full nine-category snapshots; npm test (396 syntax validations, 91/91 negative, 255 Mix tests); 132 Haxe ExUnit stdlib tests; ci:guards including scoped/all-pass byte parity; all example compile/output/WAE/runtime QA; test:mix-fast; todo-app async sentinel and Playwright 5/5. The package smoke fixture now explicitly exercises tuple reads; exact committed source/package parity is the remaining gate before closure.
Exact committed artifact verification passed for 076fc01cf: Reflaxe package flattening, isolated haxelib installation, tuple-specific elem/2 assertions, byte-identical source/package generated Elixir, stdlib source-path checks, and exact-ZIP Mix/Phoenix compilation.
close_reason: Made canonical anonymous tuple construction, typed reads, object-pattern binds, and immutable updates representation-consistent, with executable regressions, docs, source/package parity, examples, and Phoenix browser QA.

title: Establish a handwritten-output corpus and structural quality gates
description: Turn the output audit into a durable, reviewable quality corpus spanning Elixir-first, portable, abstraction, Phoenix/LiveView/Ecto, stdlib-heavy, and imperative source. The previous idiomatic-output epic enforced warnings and naming but did not distinguish canonical formatting, target-native structure, semantic compatibility artifacts, or support-module footprint.
design: For each fixture, keep the Haxe source, generated Elixir, and a concise handwritten Elixir equivalent or target-shape explanation together. Classify checks into syntax/format, structural idioms, runtime/helper necessity, and semantic parity. Prefer focused structural assertions and reviewed snapshots over a brittle repository-wide ban or raw artifact count.
acceptance_criteria: Examples 13, 14, 16, and a representative todo/Phoenix slice have documented output expectations and meaningful compile/runtime coverage; CI checks canonical formatting and WAE for the selected corpus; unjustified `_ =` calls, pure IIFEs, helper leakage, reducer append patterns, and support-module footprint are measured with explicit allowances rather than silently accepted; raw Elixir/Phoenix equivalents are visible in docs where the mapping is non-obvious; the gate passes identically for source checkout and built package.
notes: Implemented in e76a84747. Added a four-project handwritten-output corpus linking real Haxe source, canonical generated snapshots, handwritten Elixir comparisons, structural allowances, and support-footprint budgets. Added path-independent scanner self-tests, CI/runtime/WAE wiring, source-vs-built-package structural parity, friendly README/architecture docs, and changelog coverage. Upgraded examples 14 and 16 to Mix projects with Haxe-authored ExUnit runtime tests and JavaScript cross-target execution for example 16. Fixed unused fixed-bound String.substr length lowering with a real Haxe regression, and corrected Kernel.typeOf boolean classification discovered during corpus review. Verification green: npm test; full snapshots and negatives; 132 Haxe ExUnit stdlib tests; 120 upstream-unitstd modules; full examples compile/output/WAE/runtime; complete ci:guards; mix-fast; handwritten corpus; exact e76a84747 source/package byte and structural parity plus packaged Phoenix compile; todo async sentinel and Playwright 5/5.
close_reason: Handwritten-output corpus, structural and footprint gates, meaningful example runtime/WAE coverage, documentation, and exact source/package parity are complete.

title: Integrate canonical Elixir formatting for generated output
description: Generated application files frequently fail mix format even when their structure is otherwise target-native. Add a documented formatter lifecycle using Reflaxe BaseCompiler.onOutputComplete, following Reflaxe.Rust's optional rustfmt precedent while respecting bare compiler environments that may not have Elixir or Mix installed.
design: Define explicit off/write/check behavior and the project/toolchain discovery contract. Formatting is presentation only: it must run after successful code generation and must never repair semantic output or parse failures. Generated Phoenix projects should use the appropriate Phoenix.LiveView.HTMLFormatter configuration. Pin a canonical CI formatter toolchain because formatting can vary across Elixir versions.
acceptance_criteria: A representative generated Mix/Phoenix project can opt into write and check modes through a stable documented compiler/build contract; check mode fails clearly on noncanonical generated files and write mode is deterministic/idempotent; environments without Elixir/Mix have an explicit supported off path; source checkout and built haxelib behave the same; selected generated examples pass mix format --check-formatted under the pinned CI toolchain; snapshots remain deterministic; formatter failures identify files and commands; docs and changelog distinguish formatting from semantic idiomaticity.
notes: Implemented in 2a336f7fb. Added manifest-scoped off/write/check formatting in BaseCompiler.onOutputComplete, deterministic batching and dry-run preflight, explicit project discovery/override, actionable failure diagnostics, and a source-map incompatibility guard for write mode. Formatting is presentation-only; default off preserves bare Haxe environments and existing snapshots. Added plain Mix and Phoenix.LiveView.HTMLFormatter lifecycle tests, idempotence and ownership checks, generator opt-in comments, pinned CI coverage, and exact source/built-haxelib byte parity. Documented modes, raw-output check semantics, external artifact checks, project/tool discovery, ownership, source/package behavior, source-map constraint, formatter-version pinning, and process/mtime tradeoffs in README, user guide, architecture docs, flags guide, generator docs, audit, changelog, and examples. Verification green: npm test; 120-module upstream guard; 132 Haxe ExUnit stdlib tests; all example compile/output/WAE/runtime gates; ci:guards; mix-fast 139/139; exact committed haxelib package smoke including Mix/Phoenix compile; async todo sentinel and Playwright 5/5; local path scan clean except intentional guard/docs/test examples.
close_reason: Canonical generated-output formatting lifecycle, documentation, source/package parity, full examples, stdlib, Phoenix browser QA, and repository policy validation are complete.

title: Emit bare effect calls instead of `_ = call` at statement origin
description: BareCallToUnderscoreAssign currently treats `_ = call(...)` as the idiomatic Elixir representation of a discarded effectful call. Normal handwritten Elixir uses a bare call in statement position, and generated Application, Supervisor, Router, plug, live, and ordinary effect calls expose unnecessary `_ =` assignments.
design: Represent statement context explicitly and emit bare calls there. Preserve `_ =` only when matching is semantically intentional. Fix this at builder/lowering origin and update downstream passes that currently key off the artificial match shape; do not add a final unwrap pass. Preserve receiver-return rebinding, macro expansion shape, tail-call values, exceptions, and Haxe left-to-right evaluation.
acceptance_criteria: Selected core and Phoenix snapshots emit bare statement calls, including Supervisor.start_link and router/plug/live DSL forms; tail calls still return their value; persistent receiver mutators still rebind correctly; calls embedded in larger expressions retain ordering and hoisting; no downstream transform depends on an obsolete `_ = call` shape; generated Elixir is formatted and WAE-clean; full snapshots, examples, runtime, package parity, and todo Playwright QA pass; docs/changelog explain the changed output shape.
notes: Implemented in 36f4b392d. Removed the global BareCallToUnderscoreAssign and PresenceBareCallPreserve passes so direct ECall and ERemoteCall nodes remain bare in block/statement position. Adapted Ecto migration chain parsing and changeset-tail preservation to the canonical bare-call AST while retaining exact receiver proof and genuine wildcard/rebinding semantics. Added executable statement-effect, ordering, embedded-call, and tail-value regression coverage; updated 402 reviewed snapshot/example artifacts, registry inventory/baseline, README, architecture/user docs, AGENTS guidance, and CHANGELOG. Validation is green: all nine snapshot categories; 91 negative fixtures; 396 Elixir parses; 255 Mix tests; runtime smoke; 132 Haxe ExUnit stdlib tests; full ci:guards and scoped/all-pass parity; all example compile, reproducibility, WAE, and runtime gates; mix-fast; exact committed source/package byte parity plus exact-ZIP Phoenix compile; async todo sentinel and Playwright 5/5. No upstream Reflaxe PR was opened.
close_reason: Canonical bare statement-call lowering, downstream compatibility, regression coverage, documentation, source/package parity, examples, and Phoenix browser QA are complete.

title: Scope framework passes and consolidate proven repair chains
description: Apply the pass-registry inventory by preventing framework-specific transforms from traversing unrelated modules and by replacing proven duplicate final/replay/repair chains with explicit phase contracts. This is an internal architecture cleanup, not a removal of the Elixir AST pipeline or target semantics.
design: Use module metadata and typed AST properties for applicability. Consolidate only where the inventory proves equivalent ordering and behavior. Move corrections to the earliest phase that owns the invalid shape, keep transforms deterministic and idempotent, and retain focused regression coverage for every removed or merged pass. Avoid name-based application heuristics and avoid a generic textual final cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: Core modules do not execute Phoenix/LiveView/Ecto/HXX/ExUnit transforms without matching metadata; framework modules still receive every required semantic transform; pass-count and timing baselines improve or remain justified; repeated passes selected for consolidation have before/after idempotence and regression evidence; representative generated output is unchanged except for separately approved correctness or idiom fixes; full snapshot matrix, stdlib runtime, examples/output/WAE/runtime, Mix, package parity, async todo Playwright QA, and latest CI pass.
notes:
Implemented explicit PassScopeManifest ownership and phase-boundary PassApplicability analysis from Haxe annotations, compiler-only metadata, and structured target API AST nodes. Source and built packages keep one scoped compiler pipeline; reflaxe_elixir_disable_pass_scopes is verification-only. Preserved the exact 578-pass effective name order, removed 50 later same-name registrations already discarded by RegistryCore plus 3 ignored missing runAfter edges, and retained every distinctly named replay/final chain because equivalence/idempotence was not proven. Inventory guard now requires zero duplicates, zero cycles, and no stale scoped IDs. Representative executed/skipped counts: core 407/171, stdlib 407/171, Phoenix 571/7, LiveView 575/3, Ecto 454/124, HXX 469/109, ExUnit 410/168. Added complete-tree byte parity for scoped vs legacy all-pass execution; all seven profiles are identical. Follow-up haxe.elixir.codex-3qh.22 tracks the non-Ecto coupling that keeps ChangesetEnsureReturn global.

Local evidence: npm test (all 9 positive categories, 91 negative fixtures, 396 Elixir parses, 255 Mix tests, result invariant, generator, runtime smoke); Haxe ExUnit stdlib 132/132; examples compile/output/WAE/runtime; full ci:guards; async todo sentinel with WAE, migrations, runtime probe, and Playwright 5/5. Haxelib smoke is green for prior committed HEAD and will be rerun against this task commit before push. README, architecture/contributor docs, AGENTS, generated inventory/order/baseline, and CHANGELOG are updated.
close_reason: Typed framework pass scoping, proven dead-registration cleanup, byte-parity guard, documentation, and required local validation are complete.

title: Inventory and phase the Elixir AST pass registry
description: A granular trace of a tiny unrelated module produced 578 pass snapshots, including many Phoenix, LiveView, Ecto, HXX, cleanup, final, replay, and repair transforms that were no-ops for that module. Build an authoritative map of pass ownership, phase ordering, applicability, interactions, and cost before consolidating the registry.
design: Treat the current custom Elixir AST pipeline as required compiler infrastructure. Classify passes into explicit semantic phases and scopes such as core, stdlib, Phoenix, LiveView, Ecto, HXX, ExUnit, and diagnostics. Identify duplicate/replay/repair chains and the earlier builder or lowering phase that should own each shape. This task must be output-preserving; do not remove a pass merely because its name looks redundant.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in architecture artifact documents every enabled pass or coherent pass family, phase, applicability predicate, input/output invariant, known downstream shape dependency, and representative tests; tooling reports deterministic per-module pass counts and timing without unbounded logs; representative core/stdlib/Phoenix/LiveView/Ecto/HXX/ExUnit modules establish a baseline; byte-level generated-output parity is retained unless a separately reviewed bug correction is required; full snapshots, examples, package parity, and todo QA pass.
notes: Implemented typed macro-context registry introspection and authoritative generated inventory for 578 effective passes across 7 phases/scopes, with deterministic order, replay-family candidates, and RegistryCore diagnostics (50 duplicate registrations across 38 names, 3 missing dependencies, 0 cycle nodes). Added bounded one-module profiling for core/stdlib/Phoenix/LiveView/Ecto/HXX/ExUnit: exactly 578 indexed pass records plus one summary per scenario; timing values are reference observations, while count/report shape is guarded. Normal generated Elixir remained byte-identical. Verified npm test, all example compile/output/WAE/runtime gates, 132 stdlib ExUnit tests, upstream manifest guard, source/package parity with installed-package Phoenix compile, full ci:guards, and todo sentinel + Playwright 5/5.
close_reason: Authoritative output-preserving registry inventory, bounded baseline tooling, docs, and all required validation are complete.

title: Enforce phase-level invariants for non-Void function results
description: Prevent future cleanup and repair passes from silently turning value-returning Haxe functions into nil-returning Elixir functions. The pipeline currently has enough late transformations that snapshot coverage alone did not detect the tail-literal loss.
design: Carry or derive a reliable return contract for generated functions and validate it at meaningful AST phase boundaries, not with text inspection. The invariant must understand legitimate branch/case/reducer return carriers, explicit target-native callbacks, Void functions, raises, and unreachable paths. Keep production overhead opt-in or negligible while making the assertion mandatory in compiler regression tests.

title: Make generated Elixir read like handwritten Elixir when semantics allow
description: Raise the output contract so functional, Elixir-first Haxe maps to direct target-native Elixir, while portable or imperative Haxe preserves exact Haxe behavior and only pays visible runtime/lowering cost when semantics require it. Keep one compiler pipeline. Do not create a backend/profile switch, remove the Elixir AST pipeline or custom semantic passes, or repair generated text after printing.
design: Execute in this order: correctness; phase-level invariants and pass architecture; canonical formatting and statement context; conservative functional idiom rewrites and runtime-footprint work; explicit target-native behaviour/protocol decisions; documentation and full source/package parity. Source shape should determine proximity to raw Elixir. Every rewrite must state proof conditions and preserve left-to-right evaluation, exceptions, mutation/rebinding, virtual dispatch, floats, reflection, and Haxe stdlib semantics.
acceptance_criteria: The confirmed non-Void tail-value regression is fixed and runtime-covered; selected Elixir-first and portable corpora are canonically formatted, warnings-as-errors clean, and structurally reviewed against handwritten equivalents; unjustified `_ =` calls and proven avoidable helpers/control-flow artifacts are removed at their source; generated support footprint is measured and reduced without breaking reflection/runtime needs; source checkout and built haxelib produce equivalent representative output; docs explain the authoring-to-output gradient and every retained semantic artifact; full snapshots, stdlib runtime, examples, package parity, Mix tests, todo-app async sentinel plus Playwright, and latest GitHub CI pass.
notes:
2026-07-12 audit evidence: examples/13 generated direct Phoenix, Enum, String, map, tuple, and HEEx shapes, but 8/11 app files failed file-level mix-format checks; examples/16 and 14 were 4/4 and 7/7 noncanonical. A tiny ImmediateRetryPolicy build traversed 578 granular pass snapshots. Example 13 emitted 58 files, reduced to 42 with -dce full. ImmediateRetryPolicy.nextDelayMs():Int lost its tail literal 0 in LocalAssignUnusedUnderscore_Scoped_Final and generated an empty function returning nil. Ruby is not a cleaner general baseline; Rust has a larger semantic gap but stronger formatter integration and a smaller, clearer pass runner.
The full investigation is preserved in docs/08-roadmap/generated-elixir-idiomaticity-audit.md. Beads are the execution graph; the audit is the durable rationale and evidence record.

title: Stdlib runtime: design Math special-float semantics before enabling upstream Math.unit.hx

title: UX audit: generated API ergonomics consistency
description:
## Goal
Eliminate remaining UX friction where compiler-generated APIs still feel manual or inconsistent, now that `@:schema + @:changeset` no longer requires hand-written `extern changeset` declarations.

## Why this task
While fixing the changeset declaration DX, we found similar ergonomics issues that still increase cognitive overhead:
- legacy snapshot/examples still encode manual/verbose patterns and can regress docs back to old guidance
- mixed naming/qualification style (`Module.Type` vs direct type imports/constructors) makes snippets noisy
- no explicit regression coverage for "optional explicit declaration still works" compatibility path

## Scope
1. **Ecto snapshot cleanup**
- Modernize legacy schema/changeset snapshots that still require manual `extern` declarations for generated APIs.
- Keep one explicit compatibility test proving explicit declaration remains allowed.

2. **Snippet/API style normalization**
- Audit docs/examples for over-qualified type/constructor usage where unqualified usage is unambiguous.
- Standardize to concise style in user-facing snippets (import + direct type/constructor names).

3. **Regression guardrails**
- Add or adjust minimal snapshots so manual-boilerplate regression cannot return silently.
- Ensure docs/tests clearly separate:
  - generated API defaults (recommended)
  - explicit declarations (optional compatibility path)

## Out of scope
- New Ecto features beyond API ergonomics and docs consistency.
- Breaking changes to existing user code style requirements.

## Acceptance criteria
- Legacy docs/snippets no longer imply manual declaration is required for generated schema changesets.
- Snapshot coverage includes:
  - no-manual-declaration path (already added)
  - explicit-declaration compatibility path (kept and documented)
- User-facing docs consistently prefer concise, unqualified usage when no ambiguity exists.
- CI snapshot suites pass after intended updates.
close_reason: Implemented: docs normalization + compatibility regression coverage

title: Iterators: define canonical IMap representation + unwrap API
description:
# WHAT
Decide and document the canonical runtime representation for Elixir-target `haxe.Constraints.IMap` values.

# WHY
Iterator helpers and boundary code need a stable, non-brittle way to access the underlying key/value store without shape-sniffing (e.g. checking `:h`, `:map`, `:data`).

# HOW
- Pick one canonical representation strategy:
  - (A) Plain Elixir maps (`%{}`) everywhere (preferred if semantics allow), or
  - (B) A single wrapper shape with a single storage field (e.g. `:data`) plus `__reflaxe_class__` dispatch.
- Provide a single unwrapping API (e.g. `reflaxe.elixir.runtime.IMap.unwrap/1` or equivalent) as the *only* place that knows the representation.
- Add docs:
  - architecture note under `docs/05-architecture/` and hxdoc pointers.

# Acceptance
- A documented contract: “an `IMap` is represented as …” and “unwrap via …”.
- No app-specific name heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: See Acceptance in description.
notes: Updated contract in docs/runtime and implementation: MapKeyValueIterator.new/1 now explicitly accepts plain Elixir maps or pair lists and no longer relies on wrapper shape sniffing. Remaining follow-up: decide/document canonical IMap unwrap helper API boundary.
close_reason: Added canonical Reflaxe.Elixir.IMap.unwrap/1 runtime helper, delegated MapKeyValueIterator normalization through it, documented the IMap contract, and covered plain maps/pair lists/runtime-struct rejection with Haxe-authored ExUnit plus iterator snapshots.

title: Iterators: implement ArrayIterator + MapKeyValueIterator in stdlib
description:
# WHAT
Implement `haxe.iterators.ArrayIterator` + `haxe.iterators.MapKeyValueIterator` as real Elixir-target stdlib/runtime modules (not transformer-injected).

# WHY
Transformer overrides are a CI safety net, not a long-term source of truth. These iterator modules are called by generated stdlib under WAE (`*.new/arity`) and must exist with correct semantics.

# HOW
- Place implementations under target-gated stdlib (`std/_std` / `std/*.cross.hx`) with upstream-matching API.
- Preserve stateful iterator semantics using process dictionary keyed by a unique ref (or another BEAM-safe mechanism) so `next(it)` advances without returning `it2`.
- Ensure `MapKeyValueIterator` works for:
  - plain `%{}`
  - canonical `IMap` representation chosen in task 1
  - `haxe.ds.BalancedTree` (via keys+get / unwrap contract)

# Acceptance
- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` succeeds in the WAE examples that exercised these paths.
- Runtime tests cover stateful iteration correctness.
acceptance_criteria: See Acceptance in description.
notes: Implemented canonical Elixir-target iterator runtimes in stdlib source-of-truth: added std/haxe/iterators/ArrayIterator.cross.hx runtime and replaced MapKeyValueIterator.cross.hx extern stub with runtime implementation. Verified with snapshot parity and mix-fast.

title: Stdlib parity: canonical IMap runtime + iterators
description:
# Goal
Eliminate iterator/runtime and map-boundary gotchas by making Elixir-target `IMap` + iterator behavior **canonical, testable, and WAE-safe**.

This is the follow-up to a CI-unblocker where iterator stubs were promoted to minimal runtime modules to satisfy `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`. The long-term goal is to move that logic out of transformer overrides and into a single, well-defined stdlib/runtime layer.

# Motivation
- CI WAE shards failed when generated stdlib called `ArrayIterator.new/1` / `MapKeyValueIterator.new/1` but the modules were docs-only stubs.
- Current runtime unwrapping for `IMap` is implemented via *shape sniffing* (checking for `:h`, `:map`, `:data`), which is brittle unless backed by an explicit runtime representation contract.
- We want “use Haxe Map everywhere” with predictable behavior and idiomatic Elixir output, and we want the server (Elixir) and client (genes/JS) story to remain coherent.

# Current state
- Iterator runtime exists as an AST override in `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/StdHaxeRuntimeOverrideTransforms.hx` (`ArrayIterator` + `MapKeyValueIterator`).
- The implementation preserves Haxe's stateful iterator calling convention by storing index state in the process dictionary keyed by a unique ref.
- Map unwrapping is currently shape-based.

# Proposed direction (single source of truth)
1) Define and enforce a **canonical Elixir representation for Elixir-target `IMap`** (one storage field or one runtime helper API).
2) Implement iterator modules as real Elixir-target stdlib/runtime modules (not emitted by transformer overrides), keeping the exact upstream Haxe API surface.
3) Keep transformer overrides only as a temporary safety net until the stdlib implementations are complete and covered by runtime tests.

# Non-goals
- Do not rewrite the entire compiler to an immutable iterator protocol in this epic (separate research).
- Do not introduce `Dynamic` public surfaces to paper over mismatches.

# Acceptance criteria
- A documented canonical `IMap` representation/unwrap contract (docs + hxdoc).
- `haxe.iterators.ArrayIterator` and `haxe.iterators.MapKeyValueIterator` have real Elixir-target implementations (stdlib/runtime) with `new/arity`, `hasNext/has_next`, and `next/1` semantics preserved.
- Remove (or greatly narrow) iterator logic from `StdHaxeRuntimeOverrideTransforms` without regressing WAE.
- Add runtime tests proving iterator semantics and key/value iteration across:
  - plain Elixir maps (`%{}`)
  - Haxe map-backed wrappers (whatever canonical form we pick)
  - `haxe.ds.BalancedTree` map impl
- CI `Examples (Elixir WAE)` remains green.

# References
- CI-unblocker hxdoc: `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/StdHaxeRuntimeOverrideTransforms.hx`
- WAE harness: `scripts/test-examples-elixir.sh`
acceptance_criteria: See Acceptance criteria in description.
notes: Closed after removing iterator runtime fallback from StdHaxeRuntimeOverrideTransforms. Canonical iterator runtime now lives only in std/haxe/iterators/*.cross.hx, with IMap runtime boundary in std/reflaxe/elixir/IMap.hx and architecture docs updated. Verification: npm run test:quick; npm run test:mix-fast; npm run test:examples-elixir; npm run guard:docs-links; git diff --check.

title: Stdlib parity roadmap (Haxe 4.3.x baseline)
description:
# Goal
Close the Elixir-target stdlib parity gap (Haxe 4.3.x baseline) so that normal Haxe code compiles and runs correctly on BEAM, while generated Elixir stays idiomatic.

This epic is about compatibility and correctness first, then idiomaticity/optimizations where semantics allow.

# Single source of truth
Module-level audit artifacts live in the repo and must stay current:
- `docs/08-roadmap/stdlib-parity/gap-report.json`
- `docs/08-roadmap/stdlib-parity/gap-report.md`
- Regeneration script: `scripts/stdlib-parity-report.sh`

Regenerate locally:
```bash
export HAXE_ELIXIR_REFERENCE=/path/to/haxe.compilerdev.reference
scripts/stdlib-parity-report.sh --json > docs/08-roadmap/stdlib-parity/gap-report.json
scripts/stdlib-parity-report.sh --markdown > docs/08-roadmap/stdlib-parity/gap-report.md
```

# Current baseline (June 2026)
Latest counts (reference vs local std modules present):
- Reference std modules: **204**
- Local std modules present: **98** (candidates scanned: 101)
- Intersection (local provides): **89**
- Missing locally (reference-only): **115**
- Local-only: **9**

Top-level modules missing locally (5):
- `Any`, `Class`, `Enum`, `EnumValue`, `StdTypes`

Note: The report counts compiler-emitted runtime overrides as present where applicable.

# Scope / Definition of parity
We need an explicit policy per module:

1) **Upstream fallback OK**
- Module compiles and behaves correctly on BEAM without overrides.
- Add focused snapshots/runtime tests for high-traffic modules.

2) **Needs Elixir override / BEAM mapping**
- Module relies on host APIs (`sys.*`), platform-specific assumptions, or produces invalid/non-idiomatic Elixir.
- Implement as `std/**/*.cross.hx` or target-gated `std/_std/**` when it is a stable API mapping.
- Prefer AST transforms only when the fix is shape-driven and not an API override.

3) **Explicitly unsupported (documented + fail fast)**
- Non-portable semantics that cannot be reproduced reasonably on BEAM.
- Must fail with actionable errors and docs; no silent stubs.

# Plan (phased)
Phase 0 — Audit + guardrails
- Keep `gap-report.*` current.
- Maintain/expand `docs/04-api-reference/STDLIB_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md` with clear supported/unsupported rationale.

Phase 1 — `sys.*` core
- `sys.io.Process` strategy is implemented.
- `sys.net.*`, `sys.thread.*`, `sys.ssl.*`, and `sys.Http` strategy/mappings are documented or implemented where appropriate.
- Remaining `sys.db.*` should be documented unsupported or mapped intentionally if a downstream library needs it.

Phase 2 — High-impact pure std modules
- Done: `Xml`, `UnicodeString`, `UInt`, `haxe.CallStack`, core map/iterator surfaces, bytes/io foundations, `haxe.Http` / `sys.Http`, and the `haxe.Serializer` / `haxe.Unserializer` portable data subset.
- Next candidates: `haxe.Template`, remaining `haxe.io.*` utilities, and Serializer/Unserializer class/enum/custom expansion if downstream libraries need it.

# Deliverables
- Gap report + support matrix docs are authoritative and easy to regenerate.
- Each implemented module has snapshot coverage and runtime tests where semantics matter.

# Acceptance criteria
- A documented, enforced policy for stdlib parity (supported vs needs-override vs unsupported).
- High-impact surfaces have either a BEAM mapping implementation or explicit unsupported docs.
- No public-surface `Dynamic` introduced as a workaround beyond canonical Haxe stdlib APIs that require `Dynamic`.
- Todo-app sentinel and WAE example checks remain part of verification for behavior-affecting stdlib work.

# Tracking
- Roadmap tasks are children of this epic.
- Support matrix pointer: `docs/04-api-reference/STDLIB_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md`.
notes: Runtime conformance track: snapshots validate generated Elixir shape; upstream Haxe unitstd specs should be reused through the Haxe→ExUnit lane to validate stdlib runtime behavior on BEAM for supported/overridden modules.
close_reason: All child tasks are complete and the stdlib parity roadmap epic is eligible for close.

title: HXX: make heexAST the primary lint source

## What
Ensure HXX linting always prefers `metadata.heexAST` and only uses string fallback when explicitly enabled.

## Why
TSX-level feedback relies on AST stability. String scanning is fragile and causes missed/false diagnostics.

## How
- Audit `HeexAssignsTypeLinterTransforms` fallback paths.
- Gate fallback behind a define (e.g. `-D hxx_allow_string_fallback`) and default it off when AST spans exist.

## Acceptance

- Todo-app templates still lint and compile.
notes: Implemented AST-first assigns validation: ERaw nodes now scan for @assigns usage + literal comparisons; string fallback now runs only when typed HEEx AST is missing, unless -D hxx_allow_string_fallback is set. npm test passes.

title: HXX: add opt-in strict unknown HTML tag checking
description:
## What
Add `-D hxx_strict_html` that errors on unknown HTML tags unless registered/whitelisted.

## Behavior
- Default: unknown tags are allowed; attribute validation is skipped.
- Strict: unknown tags are errors unless:
  - registered in the HTML registry, OR
  - a known component/dot-component, OR
  - explicitly allowed via an allowlist define.

## Acceptance
- Snapshot coverage (positive + negative) for strict mode.
- Docs explain strict mode + how to allow custom tags.
notes: Added -D hxx_strict_html: unknown HTML/custom tags error unless registered or allowed via -D hxx_strict_html_allow_tags=... . Added negative snapshot test/snapshot/negative/hxx_strict_html_unknown_tag. make -C test summary-negative passes.

title: TSX-level HXX typing + extensibility
description:
# TSX-level HXX typing + extensibility

## Goal
Make HXX/HEEx authoring feel as close as possible to TSX:
- Strong, actionable compile-time feedback for tags/attrs/slots/events/hooks.
- Clear, documented escape hatches (raw HEEx strings / untyped tags) without punishing early adopters.
- A stable “vocab” that apps can extend (custom tags/components/hooks/events) without patching compiler internals.

## Scope
- Compiler-side linting/type checks: `HeexAssignsTypeLinterTransforms` and related passes.
- Registries in stdlib: HTML tags/attrs, dot-components, hooks/events.
- Docs + app-template recommendations (strict flags, registries, best practices).
- Optional IDE tooling index (JSON) generated from the same registries.

## Non-goals (for now)
- Haxe 5 support work.
- Full editor integration (we’ll emit an index; IDE plugins can come later).

## Acceptance Criteria
- New strict modes are opt-in, documented, and covered by snapshot tests.
- Default behavior remains permissive for unknown/custom tags.
- Prefer AST metadata (`metadata.heexAST`) over string scanning.
close_reason: All scoped child tasks delivered (strict modes, AST-first linting, extensibility registries, tooling index, diagnostics).

acceptance_criteria: - Repeated start/stop of todo-app dev uses stable wait ports (no relocation in normal case)\n- Haxe server startup is consistently fast; no leaked --wait processes remain
notes: Fix: set per-VM HAXESHIM_SERVER_PORT (avoids default 6001 port churn) and start HaxeServer automatically in mix haxe.watch for incremental cache reuse.

title: mix haxe.watch: --hxml ignored by initial compile
description: Mix.Tasks.Haxe.Watch builds config using :build_file for HaxeWatcher, but compile_once uses HaxeCompiler.compile which reads :hxml_file. Result: --hxml works for the watcher’s recompiles but the initial compile uses the wrong build file.
acceptance_criteria: - mix haxe.watch --hxml build-client.hxml compiles the client build immediately\n- mix haxe.watch without flags keeps existing defaults
notes: Fixed: Mix.Tasks.Haxe.Watch now keeps :hxml_file and :build_file in sync so --hxml affects the initial compile as well as watch recompiles. Also switched to 'mix app.start --no-start' to avoid starting full app tree.

title: Tighten LoopIR into a closed builder-local plan
description:
The existing `LoopIR` demonstrates the value of builder-local planning but is not yet a complete normalized plan: successful paths can contain `ENil` placeholders, correctness is selected through a confidence score, emitters re-read `originalExpr`, and `EnumReduce` falls back to legacy emission. Tighten it without introducing a whole-compiler CFG or changing loop behavior implicitly.

## FILES

- `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/loop_ir/LoopIR.hx`
- `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/analyzers/BaseLoopAnalyzer.hx`
- `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/analyzers/RangeIterationAnalyzer.hx`
- `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/builders/LoopBuilder.hx`
- focused loop plan/unit tests
- ordinary-Haxe loop snapshots and Haxe-authored runtime tests
- compiler architecture and imperative-to-functional documentation

## ALGORITHM

1. Replace confidence-driven mutation of a partially initialized record with a closed result such as RangeFor, CollectionFor, While, and NoMatch/Unsupported reason variants.
2. A successful plan contains every source, binder, body, effect, accumulator, early-exit, and representation fact its emitter needs. It contains no placeholder target nodes and emitters do not read the original `TypedExpr` again.
3. Keep the original expression only outside a successful plan in the explicit legacy/fallback path.
4. Validate plan completeness before emission and keep unsupported strategies disabled or explicit rather than advertising a stub that falls back silently.
5. Inspect and test `RangeIterationAnalyzer.findIncrement`; do not assume its current `findAll(..., FunctionCall)` query is wrong without executing a minimal ordinary-Haxe case.
6. Preserve current loop output and runtime behavior first. Approve Enum/comprehension optimizations separately with evaluation, effect, early-return, and zero-iteration evidence.

## FAILURE MODES

- using a floating confidence score to choose correctness;
- `ENil` or another target node serving as “fill later” data;
- emitter re-analysis disagreeing with the analyzer;
- claiming reduce/reduce_while support while silently falling back;
- changing evaluation order, accumulator state, early exits, exceptions, or zero-iteration results;
- escalating a local loop plan into a universal SSA/CFG without cross-feature evidence.

## TESTS

- plan construction and NoMatch reasons for ranges, collections, while loops, accumulators, filters, nested loops, and early exits;
- completeness validator and no-placeholder assertion;
- focused increment detection cases;
- emitter test proving no successful path reads `originalExpr`;
- existing generated-byte parity;
- ordinary-Haxe runtime traces for order, side effects, exceptions, zero iteration, and nested state.

## VERIFICATION

Run focused loop tests, affected/full snapshots, result invariants, handwritten-output, Haxe-authored runtime tests, pass docs/inventory/scope guards, examples/output/WAE/runtime, source/package parity, async todo-app sentinel plus Playwright, and exact-head CI/CodeQL.

## ROLLOUT

Output-preserving local-plan cleanup. Remove placeholders and dead claims incrementally. Any new optimized lowering is a separate reviewed behavior slice; this task does not create a second persistent IR.
design: Replace placeholder and confidence-based LoopIR mutation with closed successful plan variants and explicit NoMatch. A successful emitter consumes only the plan; fallback retains the original TypedExpr outside it.
acceptance_criteria: Successful loop plans contain no placeholders, confidence score, or originalExpr re-analysis; unsupported strategies are explicit; increment analysis is executed and verified rather than assumed; existing output and runtime semantics remain stable; no universal CFG or second persistent IR is introduced.

title: Extract proven semantic owners from the mega-transformer
description:
After structural interpolation, receiver-plan ownership, and executable invariants prove behavior, extract those implementations and their request-local state from the mega-transformer into focused modules without changing stable pass identity, order, scope, or generated output.

## FILES

- `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/ElixirASTTransformer.hx`
- focused interpolation module under `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/**`
- `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/ReceiverEffectLoweringTransforms.hx`
- focused validation modules under `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/validation/**`
- `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/registry/ElixirASTPassRegistry.hx`
- `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/registry/groups/CoreGuardsAndInterpolation.hx`
- `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/registry/PassInventory.hx`
- `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/registry/PassScopeManifest.hx`
- generated pass inventory/order docs
- focused pass parity/profile fixtures
- `docs/03-compiler-development/LEAN_PASS_PIPELINE.md`
- `docs/05-architecture/COMPILATION_FLOW.md`

## ALGORITHM

1. Use inventory and invariant evidence to draw exact module ownership boundaries; do not split by line count alone.
2. Move one owner at a time with private request-local analysis state and documented input/output/invariants.
3. Preserve stable pass IDs, description, applicability, runAfter/runBefore dependencies, actual list placement, and lean bundle membership.
4. Prove byte-identical scoped/all-pass output and runtime behavior after each move before deleting the old implementation.
5. Remove dead duplicate scanners/helpers only when the structural owner covers every call site.
6. Measure compiler time and memory; reject extraction that introduces material regression without a named semantic benefit.
7. Update source trees and contributor docs to the actual post-extraction ownership.

## FAILURE MODES

- mechanical file splitting with shared mutable state left behind;
- pass rename/reorder or changed scope during extraction;
- duplicate old/new implementation both reachable;
- same-name registrations assumed redundant without registry proof;
- weakened snapshots or raw injection used to force parity;
- line-count success without clearer ownership or invariants;
- stale docs claiming all passes live in one file.

## TESTS

- exact registry ID/order/scope assertions;
- scoped versus all-pass byte parity;
- before/after generated tree hashes for representative core, stdlib, Phoenix, LiveView, Ecto, OTP, ExUnit, and bootstrap fixtures;
- focused runtime parity for interpolation and receiver effects;
- deterministic repeated/parallel compilation;
- pass metrics and compile-time budget comparisons;
- dead-code/audit guard for removed duplicate owners.

## VERIFICATION

Run `npm run docs:passes`, pass inventory/scope/order guards, bounded baseline profiles, all snapshot chunks, result and semantic invariants, handwritten-output, Haxe-authored runtime suites, examples/output/WAE/runtime, package parity, async todo-app sentinel with Playwright, and exact-head CI/CodeQL.

## ROLLOUT

Pure internal ownership refactor after semantic slices ship. Land one owner per reviewed commit when practical. Roll back a move independently if parity or performance changes; do not alter public flags, profiles, generated ABI, or managed-reference support status.
design: Extract only the interpolation, receiver-plan, and invariant owners already proven by prior children. Preserve stable registry identity/order/scope and move private state into focused request-local modules.
acceptance_criteria: Proven owners live in focused documented modules with request-local state; stable pass IDs, order, scope, dependencies, and lean bundles are unchanged; old duplicate implementations/scanners are unreachable or removed; scoped/all-pass and source/package output are byte-identical except separately approved quality diffs; runtime and performance evidence plus full compiler/example/QA/exact-head CI gates pass.
notes: 2026-07-19 sequencing correction: ownership extraction is last. It depends on transparent traversal/groups, request-local state, legality, receiver/result/interpolation, printer-policy migration, and the LoopIR audit. Do not preserve the old seven executable bundles as hidden runners; preserve the seven nested group identities while keeping every granular child visible.

title: Keep Elixir string interpolation structural through printing
design: Represent interpolation as literal and ElixirAST expression parts. Make traversal and transformations structural and leave quoting, escaping, and interpolation punctuation to the printer.
acceptance_criteria: Compiler-owned interpolation no longer becomes ERaw or target-coded EString; embedded expressions retain metadata/source positions and remain traversable by all affected analyzers/rewriters; the printer alone owns syntax/escaping; obsolete interpolation scanners are removed or restricted to named raw authority; left-to-right behavior, runtime bytes, exceptions, generated quality, and source/package output pass focused and full gates.
notes: 2026-07-19 sequencing correction: structural interpolation is still the first new structural-node slice, but it must wait for exhaustive traversal, transparent pass boundaries, legality scaffolding, receiver ownership, and printer-independent result flow. Use the shared child/pattern schema from haxe.elixir.codex-75i.6; do not build another mapper inside this task.

title: Dogfood the Phoenix client scaffold through Haxe-to-Elixir
design: Use typed Haxe plus the existing Haxe-authored project-patch transaction surface as the single scaffold policy owner. Checked-in generated Elixir is the production artifact. A minimal Mix bootstrap module may remain handwritten only if it must load before generated code, and it must document that exact timing constraint.

title: Dogfood PhoenixHx LiveReact integration tests through Haxe-to-ExUnit
description:
The LiveReact lifecycle and registry are now Haxe-authored, but their public integration suite remains a large handwritten ExUnit module. Migrate that deterministic repository-owned test logic to the established Haxe-to-ExUnit path so the integration exercises Reflaxe.Elixir in both production and test code. A minimal `test_helper.exs` bootstrap may remain only because it must invoke Haxe and load generated test modules before ExUnit can execute them.

## FILES

- `test/exunit/haxe_phoenix_live_react_test.exs` as the migration input to remove
- a dedicated source root under `test/haxe_exunit/live_react/src_haxe/**`
- `test/exunit/test_helper.exs` only for generic compile/load bootstrap changes
- reusable typed ExUnit, Mix, File, Path, System, JSON, process, and test-helper surfaces under `std/**` or `test/support/**`
- generated Haxe-to-ExUnit artifacts under the existing ignored test fixture root
- focused compiler/DSL snapshots when migration exposes a general Haxe-to-Elixir gap

## ALGORITHM

1. Inventory the handwritten module's tests and helper functions, preserving fixture topology, dependency injection, exact failure messages, byte snapshots, external-project smoke, and cleanup semantics.
2. Add a dedicated Haxe test source root and compile it through the existing test-helper bootstrap alongside the stdlib Haxe ExUnit modules.
3. Port tests incrementally using `exunit.TestCase`, typed assertions, and typed Elixir/Phoenix/Mix host APIs. Extend the smallest reusable extern, library, ExUnit DSL, or generic compiler layer when a stable capability is missing.
4. Keep filesystem/process/Mix calls in Haxe. Do not use `__elixir__`, `untyped`, `Dynamic`, raw target strings, application/path heuristics, or a handwritten adapter to bypass compiler gaps.
5. Compare the generated ExUnit with the handwritten reference for semantics and target quality, then delete the handwritten suite once every public assertion passes through Haxe.
6. Keep only the generic bootstrap loader in `.exs`, with an adjacent comment naming the compile-before-load requirement.

## FAILURE MODES

- retaining duplicate handwritten and generated suites;
- weakening assertions, deleting conflict/recovery/removal cases, or replacing public API calls with lower-level helpers;
- using target injection or broad `Term`/`Dynamic` merely to complete the port;
- putting LiveReact-specific behavior into compiler passes or the generic ExUnit DSL;
- generating unreadable ExUnit, excess support modules, IIFEs, `_ =` wrappers, or warnings;
- making normal Mix tests require a Haxe server, watcher, network access, or unbounded process;
- treating TypeScript-only conformance assertions as application behavior instead of keeping that irreducible boundary minimal.

## TESTS

- complete parity for all lifecycle/registry tests currently in `haxe_phoenix_live_react_test.exs`;
- generated ExUnit shape snapshots or focused output assertions for new DSL/compiler behavior;
- setup/check/remove, migration, registry sorting, duplicate/collision, hand-owned retention, lockfile, package-root, dependency-identity, and external installed-task cases;
- compile-failure regressions for any newly discovered compiler defect;
- `npm run test:mix-fast`, complete LiveReact Haxe-authored module, generated-output quality, Haxe formatting, and regeneration drift.

## VERIFICATION

Run bounded Haxe test compilation, the generated LiveReact ExUnit module, `npm run test:mix-fast`, relevant snapshot categories and negatives, `npm run guard:hx-format`, `npm run guard:live-react-core`, `npm run test:handwritten-output`, generated Elixir formatting/WAE, path hygiene, Beads lint/graph checks, and exact-head CI/CodeQL before closure.

## ROLLOUT

This is an internal test-source ownership migration with no public runtime or CLI change. Land it before closing the static-registry task. Downstream applications remain free to use Haxe, Elixir, TypeScript, or a deliberate mixture; this repository dogfood rule does not constrain them.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

All deterministic LiveReact integration tests are authored in Haxe and execute as idiomatic generated ExUnit with public-behavior parity; the handwritten `haxe_phoenix_live_react_test.exs` suite is removed; any remaining `.exs` is a minimal documented compile/load bootstrap; no raw target injection, Dynamic escape, LiveReact-specific compiler logic, duplicate suite, weakened assertion, or unbounded test process remains; focused, Mix, output-quality, formatting, CI, and CodeQL gates pass.

title: Replace vendored Genes with pinned genes-ts and prove PhoenixHX parity
description:
Replace the repository's modified Genes 0.4.14 source tree with one immutable
genes-ts dependency resolved by Lix. Preserve PhoenixHX's existing classic ESM
contract while adding a strict TypeScript/TSX lane for Haxe-authored LiveReact
components. The committed dependency must never be a machine-local Genes
checkout path. Contributors may use `$GENES_CHECKOUT` or `$GENES_WORKTREE` through
an uncommitted `lix dev` override.

## FILES

- `haxe_libraries/genes.hxml` and the canonical `genes-ts` scoped library file

- Phoenix scaffold templates and generated `haxe_libraries/*.hxml`

- LiveReact Haxe/Genes TypeScript/TSX fixture and Vite consumer
- exact dependency/compatibility receipt and contributor workflow docs
- package contents, clean-install, source-map, and rollback evidence

## ALGORITHM

1. Freeze the current repository commit as the rollback point.
2. Inventory every behavior the vendored tree supplies: classic split ESM,
   async/await, inline markup, naming/import behavior, DCE/library roots,
   source maps, and any local compiler patches.
3. Map each requirement to a green immutable genes-ts commit or identify a
   generic missing capability. Do not patch Genes inside this repository.
4. For a missing capability, reduce it without PhoenixHX/LiveReact symbols in
   an isolated `$GENES_WORKTREE`, test strict TS/TSX and classic JS, push the
   branch to a shareable fork, and temporarily pin that exact fork SHA here.
5. Replace a temporary fork pin with the merged upstream commit or release
   before declaring the integration releasable.
6. Commit an exact Lix GitHub/release pin and retain `-lib genes` only as a
   compatibility alias if existing public scaffolds require it. Local sibling
   checkouts remain optional uncommitted `lix dev` overrides.
7. Compile all current PhoenixHX browser consumers through the classic profile
   and compare module ABI, runtime traces, DCE, imports, source maps, and Vite
   consumption with the rollback baseline.
8. Add a tracked Haxe-authored React fixture using genes-ts strict TS/TSX,
   static LiveReact registry consumption, exact prop/event contracts, source
   maps, Vite, and runtime/component evidence. Keep TypeScript-authored tests
   only for irreducibly TypeScript-specific negative conformance and explain
   them next to the file.
9. Remove `vendor/genes` and every stale vendoring/path claim only after source
   and installed-package parity pass.

## FAILURE MODES

- committing a local checkout/worktree path, `haxelib dev`, or another floating
  dependency;
- consuming a dirty/unpushed checkout that CI cannot reproduce;
- framework-specific logic or symbols in genes-ts;
- silently changing the current classic ESM module/import/runtime contract;
- adopting strict TypeScript while leaving classic PhoenixHX clients untested;
- keeping vendored and external Genes as two active sources indefinitely;
- weakening Haxe/TSX props, event types, JSX runtime, DCE, or source maps to make
  the migration pass;
- treating `tsc` success alone as runtime or semantic compatibility;
- shipping a temporary fork SHA as a stable release without an explicit owner,
  PR, expiry, and replacement gate.

## TESTS

- vendored-patch capability inventory against the selected genes-ts revision;
- every existing `-lib genes` PhoenixHX client build and generated output;
- classic ESM semantic/output/source-map/DCE/import parity;
- strict Haxe-to-TypeScript/TSX LiveReact component and registry fixture;
- TypeScript exact-prop/event negative checks and React/Vite runtime tests;
- scaffold setup/rerun/remove in Genes and plain-JS modes;
- example compile/output/WAE/runtime/browser gates;
- clean Lix download, installed-package smoke, package contents, and path guard;
- rollback replay against the checkpoint commit.

## VERIFICATION

Run bounded focused Genes consumers first, then Haxe/Genes TSX typecheck and
runtime tests, Mix/scaffold tests, all JS client examples, relevant snapshot and
handwritten-output gates, example compile/output/WAE/runtime/QA, package smoke,
docs links, path hygiene, Beads graph checks, and exact-head CI/CodeQL. Record
the exact Genes repository, version, commit, tree/release artifact when
available, temporary-fork status if any, and rollback commit.

## ROLLOUT

Land behind an immutable pin with the current classic ESM profile as the
compatibility lane and strict TS/TSX as the new Haxe-first React lane. A local
worktree is a contributor convenience only. A shareable fork commit may bridge
pre-merge development, but a public/stable PhoenixHX release must consume a
merged upstream commit or release. The rollback is the last commit retaining
`vendor/genes` plus its known-green parity matrix.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

One immutable Lix-resolved genes-ts source replaces the vendor; every current
PhoenixHX classic ESM consumer preserves reviewed semantics and module ABI; a
tracked Haxe-authored TS/TSX LiveReact fixture proves the new lane; local
worktrees/forks follow the documented generic-fix and exact-pin workflow; any
temporary fork pin is explicit and removed before stable release; source and
installed-package gates pass; stale vendoring claims and the vendored tree are
removed; the rollback commit and exact admitted Genes identity are recorded.
