title: Align React island events with PhoenixHx Live Event Protocols
description:
React islands need typed client-to-LiveView events, but PhoenixHx already has a normalized Live Event Protocol system. Reuse that source of truth and invalid-payload behavior instead of adding a parallel event model.

## FILES

- existing Live Event Protocol model/manifest owners identified during implementation
- a focused LiveReact adapter/generator, not a duplicate model
- generated TypeScript contract templates/output
- Haxe snapshots and negative fixtures
- TypeScript/React event tests
- documentation finalized later

## ALGORITHM

1. Audit the normalized event model and emitted manifest/hash.
2. Define the closed payload subset that can be represented honestly in TypeScript.
3. Render stable names, interfaces, and validators from the same model or manifest.
4. Translate semantic boundary callbacks into upstream pushEvent at the trusted adapter.
5. Preserve explicit server dispatch and known-invalid consumption.
6. Require app-owned adapters for unsupported custom codecs/open terms.
7. Include protocol identity in drift checks where available.

## FAILURE MODES

Second event enum or DSL; Haxe/TypeScript drift; any/unknown/Dynamic widening while claiming safety; malformed known events falling through; raw bridge in inner props; runtime dependency on compiler internals; guessed custom codecs.

## TESTS

Scalars, named typedefs, optional fields, wire-name overrides, malformed known payloads, unknown fallback, duplicate names/keys, unsupported open payloads and codecs, TypeScript exact objects/enums, React callback to expected upstream function, and Haxe server snapshot/runtime handler.

## VERIFICATION

Run focused Live Event Protocol snapshots/negative tests, TypeScript typecheck/tests, Haxe server/client builds where applicable, Mix fast tests, and docs links. Prove existing protocol users are unchanged when LiveReact is absent.

## ROLLOUT

Opt-in adapter. Manual strict TypeScript decoders remain an escape hatch. Typed replies and server-to-client subscriptions remain out of scope unless already provided by the underlying protocol.
design: Adapt the existing normalized Live Event Protocol model to the trusted LiveReact boundary. Haxe server handlers keep explicit generated dispatch; Genes clients keep current helpers; supported TypeScript contracts derive from the same facts. Inner components receive semantic callbacks, not raw pushEvent.
acceptance_criteria: LiveReact event contracts derive from or are checked against the existing normalized protocol source; supported payloads have deterministic Haxe/TypeScript evidence; malformed known payloads remain safely consumed; unsupported codecs fail honestly or require explicit adapters; inner components receive semantic callbacks; existing protocol behavior stays compatible.
notes:
2026-07-17 contract freeze: adapt the existing LiveEventProtocolModel normalized names, payload fields/kinds, manifest, hash, and explicit dispatch. Automatic TypeScript projection is limited to honestly representable closed built-in payload kinds. Custom codecs and open/unsupported terms require an app-owned adapter and may not be widened to any, unknown, or Dynamic while claimed type-safe.
2026-07-17 generated-output gate: production behavior authored in Haxe must check in and review the resulting Elixir as a first-class artifact. It must be idiomatic, readable, byte-stable on regeneration, warnings-as-errors clean, and acceptable as handwritten code. Fix poor output in Haxe/compiler source; do not hide it with raw target injection or manual edits to generated files.

title: Implement mix haxe.phoenix.live_react setup, check, and remove
description:
Developers need one supported command that composes stock LiveReact and Vite into canonical PhoenixHx projects, verifies drift without writing, and removes only owned changes. The current local JavaScript binder is app-specific.

## FILES

- lib/haxe_phoenix_live_react.ex
- lib/mix/tasks/haxe.phoenix.live_react.ex
- lib/mix/tasks/haxe.gen.project.ex
- canonical integration templates
- Mix task, generator, and fixture tests
- implementation documentation finalized later

## ALGORITHM

1. Parse setup by default, mutually exclusive --check/--remove, --yes, non-destructive --warn-only, and a project-relative --package-root; reject unrecognized capability or identity-bypass flags.
2. Discover project topology, client mode, asset lanes, and resolved Mix LiveReact identity.
3. Build a normalized desired-state plan for Vite, package dependencies, hooks, watcher, aliases, root assets, registry entrypoint, and manifest.
4. Validate every ownership and topology constraint.
5. Apply atomically, compare read-only in check mode, or delete only owned state in remove mode.
6. Invoke the same module after the ordinary project scaffold for --live-react.
7. Print exact next commands and unsupported capabilities.

## FAILURE MODES

Conflicting modes; non-Phoenix or unsupported topology; ambiguous LiveSocket/Vite insertion; Mix/npm source mismatch; conflicting package keys; unowned markers/files; two bundlers; removal of hand-owned code; broken base scaffold; --live-react treated as client mode; SSR silently accepted.

## TESTS

Genes and plain-JS setup; check success/drift; byte-idempotent rerun; deleted-owned-file recovery; malformed markers; unowned collisions; package equal/conflict; supported/custom Vite; tested package roots; setup/remove; retained hand-owned React/Vite; generator composition; unsupported SSR; dependency mismatch; zero partial writes.

## VERIFICATION

Run focused Mix and generator tests, formatters, representative generated-project Haxe/Mix compile, source/package task smoke, and help/docs link checks with bounded commands.

## ROLLOUT

Experimental opt-in command. Default projects remain unchanged. Unsupported topologies receive a manual-integration report, never heuristic mutation.
design: Implement an Elixir Mix task backed by a dedicated integration module and the shared patch primitives. Setup is default; --check is strictly read-only; --remove is reversible. Compose with Genes/plain-JS, use Mix as source of truth, point npm at the same checkout, keep Vite as sole bundler, and reject SSR in this slice.
acceptance_criteria: Apply/check/remove and greenfield composition work for the tested Genes/plain-JS shapes; reruns are byte-idempotent; conflicts fail before writes; Vite is the one bundler; Mix/npm identity matches; removal preserves hand-owned files and a compiling base project; the complete lifecycle matrix passes.
notes:
2026-07-17 contract freeze: setup is default; --check and --remove are mutually exclusive; --yes is noninteractive; --warn-only never bypasses ownership, identity, malformed-marker, or unsupported-SSR errors; --package-root accepts only a project-relative root that remains inside the project. Mix lock identity is canonical and npm must use a checked project-relative file: reference to that exact checkout. No general identity override ships in the initial contract. Root/assets package roots and genes/plain-js become supported only for exact tested matrix rows.
Dependency bootstrap clarification: the tool version carries a checked default LiveReact Mix declaration. Apply adds it when absent, retains a supported existing resolution, rejects a conflict, and must obtain a lock identity before reporting success; tracked intermediate edits participate in rollback. Ignored dependency-cache downloads may remain after a failed fetch. --check is network-free and reports a missing/stale lock as drift.
2026-07-17 implementation evidence: added the handwritten-Elixir ring-0 lifecycle module and public Mix task, composed --live-react after the existing Phoenix scaffold, and covered exact root/assets package roots with Genes/plain-JS topology. Apply/check/remove now validate the full plan before atomic publication, keep Mix as the canonical stock LiveReact resolver, derive the npm file reference from that checkout, preserve unrelated lock/package/source edits, restore clean round trips byte-for-byte, recover deleted signature-owned files, and reject unowned/custom/SSR/identity drift before writes. Generated Mix/config output is mix-format clean and generated JS/Vite output passes node syntax checks. Focused ownership/generator/lifecycle coverage is 37 tests; npm run test:mix-fast passed (147 tests in the final stale run), npm run test:generator passed, and docs link guard passed. A real external path-dependency consumer ran the public apply/check/remove task. Installed-package parity, example/browser proof, and cross-platform compatibility remain explicitly deferred to msb.8/msb.9.
Post-close verification refinement: added an explicit fail-closed package-root traversal regression. Focused ownership/generator/lifecycle coverage is now 38 tests, and the final npm run test:mix-fast stale run passed 148 tests.
close_reason: Implemented and verified the opt-in stock LiveReact/Vite lifecycle task: fail-closed apply/check/remove, Mix-canonical dependency identity, root/assets and Genes/plain-JS topology, exact reversible ownership, generator composition, external consumer smoke, format/syntax gates, and focused/official test coverage. Installed-package, example, browser, and broader compatibility proof remain in the downstream graph.

title: Extract reusable fail-closed Phoenix project patch ownership primitives
description:
The existing Phoenix scaffold and project-local LiveReact binder both contain ownership ideas, but the reusable integration must not copy another ad hoc patch engine. Extract the minimum internal project-mutation primitives while preserving existing scaffold behavior.

## FILES

- lib/haxe_phoenix_scaffold.ex
- a repository-consistent internal module such as lib/haxe_project_patch.ex
- existing scaffold Mix task tests
- new shared patch-unit tests
- no example migration in this task

## ALGORITHM

1. Inventory marker, generated-signature, atomic-write, confirmation, package-key, and removal helpers.
2. Define structured read-only discovery and file-create, marker-upsert/remove, package-key, plan, and atomic-publish operations.
3. Validate every operation before any write.
4. Migrate existing scaffold callers without output changes.
5. Expose only internal seams needed by LiveReact.
6. Compare Genes and plain-JS scaffold trees byte for byte.

## FAILURE MODES

Unintentional scaffold drift; partial writes; tolerated missing/duplicate/inverted markers; unowned overwrite; unrelated JSON churn; warn-only destructive mutation; public unstable subsystem; or copied project-local JavaScript logic.

## TESTS

Existing setup/rerun/convergence tests; byte-stable Genes/plain-JS fixtures; marker zero/one/multiple/inverted cases; signature recovery/collision; package equal/conflict/unrelated keys; all-validation-before-write; atomic failure simulation where practical.

## VERIFICATION

Run focused scaffold and shared patch Mix tests, generator tests, formatting, git diff --check, and representative generated-tree comparison with bounded commands.

## ROLLOUT

Land as an internal output-preserving refactor. Existing public commands and files remain compatible. Do not publish a generic patch API before two callers prove it.
design: Refactor HaxePhoenixScaffold only where required into reusable internal discovery, plan, marker/signature ownership, package-key validation, atomic writing, and diagnostics. Keep framework-specific policy in callers. Avoid a generic template engine or public API.
acceptance_criteria: The internal patch layer covers required ownership operations; existing Phoenix scaffold output/removal remains byte-compatible or has an explicitly reviewed migration; writes are atomic and fail closed; LiveReact can reuse the primitives without copying the local script; focused and generator tests pass.
notes:
2026-07-17 contract freeze: validate and render the whole mutation plan before writes; stage same-filesystem replacements and retain originals for rollback on any reported publication failure; publish the manifest last; make check/rerun recover externally interrupted state. Per-file replace is atomic, but do not claim process-kill, kernel-failure, or power-loss-level multi-file filesystem atomicity.
2026-07-17 implementation boundary: bootstrap/recovery infrastructure that must work when Haxe compilation is unavailable or broken remains handwritten Elixir. Above that ring-0 boundary, prefer Haxe-authored production surfaces only when their checked-in generated Elixir is idiomatic, readable, byte-stable, warnings-as-errors clean, and acceptable in a handwritten code review. Raw target injection and hand-editing generated output are not quality escape hatches; output defects must be fixed at the source/compiler layer.
2026-07-17 implementation evidence: added internal HaxeProjectPatch planning, marker/signature/package ownership, staged same-filesystem publication, rollback, manifest-last ordering, and journal recovery; migrated HaxePhoenixScaffold without generated-tree drift. Focused patch/scaffold suite: 32 tests, 0 failures. Full Mix suite: 280 tests, 0 failures. Generator gate and docs-link guard passed. A direct pre-refactor-vs-current comparison proved complete Genes and plain-js fixture trees byte-identical. No compiler or user-facing generated Elixir changed in this slice, so no example output migration was required.
Final API review added recovery_status!/1 so --check can report rollback or commit-cleanup pending without writing; setup reruns continue to recover through recover!/1. Focused suite remained 32/32 and the repository fast Mix gate reran 163 affected tests with 0 failures.
close_reason: Reusable fail-closed patch ownership, read-only recovery status, staged publication, rollback/recovery, and byte-identical scaffold migration implemented and fully validated.

title: Add API-faithful Haxe and HXX bindings for stock LiveReact
description:
PhoenixHx needs a supported Haxe surface for referring to stock LiveReact modules and rendering LiveReact.react from direct inline HXX without raw target strings. The low-level surface must remain API-faithful and must not claim arbitrary prop validation.

## FILES

- std/phoenix/live_react/LiveReact.hx
- std/phoenix/live_react/ReactComponentName.hx
- std/phoenix/live_react/ReactIslandOptions.hx
- optional Reload.hx and Test.hx only for verified public surfaces
- test/snapshot/phoenix/live_react_low_level and focused negative HXX fixtures
- API references finalized by the documentation child

## ALGORITHM

1. Inspect public upstream modules/functions used by the pinned canary.
2. Add direct native/extern declarations through existing PhoenixHx conventions.
3. Compile a minimal app-local wrapper containing a module-qualified direct-inline HXX call.
4. Confirm ordinary HEEx and no runtime wrapper or raw injection.
5. Keep strict prop validation in the app-local wrapper when std discovery cannot prove it.
6. Add erased/static component-name types only when they preserve upstream string compatibility.

## FAILURE MODES

Wrong target module/function; false optional/open prop precision; Dynamic used as a safety claim; legacy HXX or raw HEEx required; guessed test/reload signatures; compiler special cases; copied runtime code; or importing the namespace installs dependencies.

## TESTS

Positive low-level and app-local wrapper snapshots; direct-inline HXX guard; missing/wrong wrapper prop fixtures; fixed name and ssr=false shapes; formatter and warnings-as-errors checks; later installed-package import smoke.

## VERIFICATION

Run focused Phoenix snapshots and negative HXX fixtures, Haxe formatting, generated Elixir parsing/WAE where applicable, and Mix fast tests using bounded repository commands.

## ROLLOUT

Opt-in imports only. Document the low-level call as API-faithful/advanced and the app-local wrapper as recommended. Unrelated PhoenixHx builds gain no runtime dependency.
design: Add the smallest std/phoenix/live_react declaration family that maps to stock modules. Prove ordinary module-qualified HXX output. Do not change compiler lowering, copy LiveReact behavior, or promise strict validation for open low-level props. Only map reload/test helpers when primary upstream evidence supports honest types.
acceptance_criteria: Supported direct inline HXX emits a normal stock LiveReact.react call; the namespace is small and API-faithful; app-local wrappers retain closed typed assigns; no compiler special case, raw injection, runtime copy, automatic dependency, or false precision is introduced; positive and negative gates pass.
notes:
2026-07-17 contract freeze: the low-level owner is phoenix.live_react.LiveReact mapped to upstream module LiveReact. RepoDiscovery intentionally excludes compiler std/dependency roots, so this declaration names the upstream component but does not own strict app prop discovery. Positive/negative typing belongs in a discoverable app-local @:component wrapper. Reload/Test may be added only from verified public signatures; open helper results remain honestly open.
2026-07-17 implementation evidence: audited upstream LiveReact at examples/12-phoenix-chat/deps/live_react commit 055e80e6a4e6d009df5e229eb39e7f85f03fea22. Added only the verified open LiveReact.react/1 declaration returning opaque Term; Reload/Test/name/options surfaces remain deferred because this slice has no equally precise closed public contract for them. Added a discoverable app-local typed wrapper snapshot plus missing-prop and wrong-type negatives. Direct static extern calls exposed a generic compiler bug where late Web/app qualification rewrote exact @:native modules; repaired it by carrying typed native-module metadata through static-call AST construction and requiring generated-module registry evidence before printer-side app qualification. No LiveReact name/path/compiler special case or runtime copy exists. Validation green: focused and all snapshot categories, 93/93 negatives, result invariant, pass-scope byte parity, 132 stdlib runtime tests, upstream unitstd/layout/API guards, full examples compile/output/WAE/runtime, handwritten-output corpus, Mix fast, docs links, no-Dynamic, Haxe formatting, todo sentinel, five Playwright smoke specs, and full npm test (401 Elixir syntax validations, 266 Mix tests, runtime smoke, output quality/formatting). git diff check and changed-file path hygiene are clean. Repository-wide lint:hxdoc still reports four pre-existing unrelated transformer files; none is edited by this task.
close_reason: Verified API-faithful stock LiveReact.react/1 declaration, app-local typed HXX wrapper, generic exact-native module preservation, docs, positive/negative regressions, full compiler/Mix/example/runtime/Playwright gates.

title: Freeze the PhoenixHx LiveReact ownership, API, and compatibility contract
description:
The project-local proof establishes feasibility but leaves reusable ownership, public API, dependency identity, supported topology, Genes posture, and release boundaries implicit. Freeze a decision-complete contract before implementation.

## FILES

- plans/active/phoenixhx-live-react-integration.md
- ROADMAP.md
- docs/08-roadmap/phoenix-surface-parity.md
- docs/08-roadmap/stdlib-and-package-ecosystem.md
- an architecture decision file only if repository convention requires one

## ALGORITHM

1. Audit current HXX component discovery, Phoenix scaffold client modes, Live Event Protocol output, package layout, example 12 binding, upstream LiveReact exports, and both Genes sources.
2. Resolve names, commands, modes, manifest schema, dependency identity, generated ownership, supported project shapes, removal semantics, status, compatibility matrix, and non-goals in a decision table.
3. Keep the current vendored Genes lane compatible but make no sibling-path dependency; leave genes-ts migration to its separate task.

## FAILURE MODES

Ambiguous public names; Vite treated as a client mode; false claims that std-root discovery validates app props; independent Mix/npm pins; hidden SSR/raw-bridge scope; dependency on generic Mix adoption; direct use of ../genes; or an unresolved design choice passed downstream.

## ROLLOUT

Planning/contract only. Do not advertise the feature as implemented. Keep it experimental 1.x work.
design: Adopt the active-plan decisions: same monorepo/Haxelib initially; phoenix.live_react namespace; dedicated setup/check/remove; orthogonal --live-react; upstream runtime; Mix-canonical npm-same-checkout identity; app-local typed wrappers; static registry; client-only default; existing Live Event Protocol reuse; two independent consumers; explicit compatibility matrix; current genes/plain-JS compatibility; and later split criteria.
acceptance_criteria: The active plan and roadmap record all accepted and rejected decisions; command, namespace, manifest, dependency identity, HXX boundary, Genes posture, two-consumer gate, compatibility policy, and split criteria are explicit; every child agrees; no 1.0 dependency or machine-local path is introduced; docs links and Beads lint pass.
notes: 2026-07-17 completed contract audit. Observed the app-local HXX seam, std-root discovery exclusion, two existing client modes, project-local ownership proof, normalized Live Event Protocol model, pinned upstream LiveReact exports, and hermetic vendored Genes lane. Frozen namespace/CLI/schema, Mix-canonical same-checkout identity, whole-plan mutation contract, bounded topology/compatibility statuses, app-local strict wrapper ownership, upstream runtime ownership, current Genes posture, two-consumer promotion, and package split criteria. Focused epic/child lint: zero findings. Docs links, diff whitespace, and path hygiene: clean. title: PhoenixHx: first-class opt-in stock LiveReact integration
description:
PhoenixHx has a successful project-local proof that Haxe-authored Phoenix components can render trusted React islands through stock LiveReact and Vite, but the integration is not yet a supported reusable PhoenixHx surface. Build a first-class opt-in authoring and setup layer in the current monorepo/Haxelib under `phoenix.live_react`. Stock LiveReact remains the runtime. All Elixir-target product logic that Reflaxe.Elixir can express is authored in Haxe and checked in as idiomatic generated Elixir; handwritten Elixir is limited to minimal comment-justified host/bootstrap boundaries. This is experimental 1.x work and is not a Reflaxe.Elixir 1.0 blocker.

## FILES

- `plans/active/phoenixhx-live-react-integration.md`
- Haxe/HXX declarations under `std/phoenix/live_react/**`
- Haxe-authored tooling core and checked-in generated Elixir plus thin Mix/filesystem adapters
- Mix lifecycle/generator integration, templates, ownership tests, and compiler/DSL/library regressions exposed by dogfooding
- app-local typed wrappers, static registry, trusted browser boundary, and Live Event Protocol adapter
- example 12 rich migration, example 18 independent minimum, and todo-app incremental adoption
- canonical guide/API docs, compatibility matrix, installed-package smoke, package audit, and focused CI

## ALGORITHM

Execute children in dependency order: freeze the contract; add low-level Haxe/HXX declarations and shared project-patch ownership; prove setup/check/remove; migrate its deterministic core to Haxe-generated Elixir and fix generic compiler/DSL/library gaps; add registry/wrapper scaffolding; align events; migrate example 12; add example 18 and the todo-app section; publish one canonical documentation set; then close compatibility, installed-package, package-content, and CI evidence. Re-plan through Beads and the active plan when evidence disproves an assumption.

## FAILURE MODES

Reject a LiveReact port/fork, compiler hard-code, LiveReact/todo-app name or path heuristic, raw target injection, unjustified handwritten Elixir, second JavaScript bundler, new client mode, broad default bridge, unowned mutation, mismatched Mix/npm identity, a second-consumer claim based on another example-12 route, machine-local dependency, missing useful fallback, documentation ahead of evidence, or any edge into the 1.0 blocker graph.

## TESTS

Children must provide HXX snapshots and negative fixtures, Haxe-authored lifecycle/planner behavior and reviewed generated Elixir, Mix ownership/idempotency/removal tests, strict TypeScript/React tests, three distinct application proofs with useful fallback and bounded browser evidence, source maps, snippet/command documentation smoke, explicit compatibility data, and installed-package/package-content smoke.

## VERIFICATION

Before closure run every child gate, compiler/DSL semantic regressions, docs and generator guards, example WAE/runtime/QA, async todo/chat sentinels, package parity/smoke, handwritten-output quality, Beads lint/dependency checks, path hygiene, exact-head full CI, and CodeQL.

## ROLLOUT

Ship experimental and opt-in in the existing Haxelib. Projects that do not enable it remain unchanged. Promote only after the rich, minimal, and todo-app proofs, canonical docs, package smoke, and compatibility/CI evidence pass. Keep Haxe-authored inner React components, SSR, extended capabilities, Genes migration, and possible Haxelib extraction separate.
design: Keep a two-plane architecture. PhoenixHx owns typed Haxe/HXX authoring, a Haxe-authored deterministic tooling core, app-local wrappers, static registry/setup ownership, event adapters, docs, and evidence. Thin handwritten Elixir may own only necessary Mix/bootstrap, dependency-introspection, external-command, and filesystem/recovery host operations, each with an adjacent concrete justification. Upstream LiveReact owns the Phoenix component, hook, DOM protocol, React lifecycle, Vite plugin, slots, uploads, and SSR. Vite is the sole bundler while Genes may emit ESM source. Mix is canonical and npm consumes the same checkout. Fix missing compiler/DSL/library capabilities generically, never through LiveReact or app-name heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: The epic closes only when: the opt-in namespace ships in this monorepo/Haxelib; stock LiveReact remains the only runtime; supported direct inline HXX emits an ordinary module-qualified LiveReact.react call; all expressible Elixir-target integration logic is Haxe-authored with review-quality generated Elixir and every narrow handwritten host/bootstrap exception has an adjacent concrete justification; app-local wrappers provide static identity and closed assigns; setup/check/remove and generator composition are deterministic and fail closed; Vite is the one bundler with Genes/plain-JS orthogonal; Mix/npm identity is proven; registry, trusted boundary, exact props/events, source maps, and useful fallback are evidenced; existing Live Event Protocols are reused; example 12 uses the public integration; an independent minimal example uses the same lifecycle; todo-app proves polished incremental adoption without making React essential; one canonical guide/API set documents install, authoring, generated target shape, events, debugging, testing, recovery/removal, security, compatibility, and non-goals; source and installed-package smoke pass; deferred capabilities have separate issues; and no issue in this graph blocks haxe.elixir.codex-0yn.
notes:
Historical project-proof records cited by the planning input are intentionally absent from the main Beads database. No missing dependency targets were invented and no branch-owned records were imported into main.
2026-07-17 contract freeze: public namespace phoenix.live_react; lifecycle command mix haxe.phoenix.live_react with setup/check/remove; app-local @:component wrappers own strict props because compiler std roots are outside app discovery; Mix is canonical and npm consumes the same checkout through a checked project-relative file: reference; current vendored Genes/plain-js remain inputs; no implementation has started.
2026-07-17 implementation boundary: bootstrap/recovery infrastructure that must work when Haxe compilation is unavailable or broken remains handwritten Elixir. Above that ring-0 boundary, prefer Haxe-authored production surfaces only when their checked-in generated Elixir is idiomatic, readable, byte-stable, warnings-as-errors clean, and acceptable in a handwritten code review. Raw target injection and hand-editing generated output are not quality escape hatches; output defects must be fixed at the source/compiler layer.
2026-07-17 project-wide Haxe ownership rule: any Elixir-target behavior that Reflaxe.Elixir can express must be authored in Haxe. Handwritten Elixir is limited to a concrete minimal host/bootstrap boundary and must carry an adjacent source comment explaining why Haxe cannot own it. Compiler, structured DSL, or target-library gaps exposed by the work should be fixed generically with semantic regressions, never with LiveReact-specific heuristics or raw target injection. haxe.elixir.codex-msb.10 migrates the immediate lifecycle core and now blocks further registry expansion.
2026-07-17 example/docs expansion: the epic now requires three distinct application stories—example 12 rich migration, example 18 clean-room minimum, and todo-app incremental Haxe-first adoption. Canonical documentation is a separate task (.msb.12); compatibility/package/CI closure remains .msb.9. The todo-app island is useful but nonessential and retains a native fallback.
2026-07-18 Genes TSX/HXX promotion: haxe.elixir.codex-a06 is now an active P1 gate after the static-registry task and before the independent example and todo-app consumers. It owns revalidating and admitting the latest canonical exact genes-ts release, preserving the classic ESM corpus, and proving one bounded Haxe-authored React component through Genes TypeScript/TSX inline HXX. This supersedes the older rollout sentence that kept all Haxe-authored inner React work separate from the epic; broad arbitrary React compatibility remains outside the bounded proof. The LiveReact graph still does not block Reflaxe.Elixir 1.0.

title: Require useful beginner-readable commit bodies
description: Add the requested repository-wide commit-message rule to the root contributor instructions so non-trivial changes explain their outcome, rationale, verification, behavior impact, and deliberately deferred scope.
design: Extend the existing root Commit Standards section rather than duplicating the rule in a nested AGENTS.md. Preserve Conventional Commits and the no-AI-attribution rule. Use the user-supplied wording without diff markers or line numbers.
acceptance_criteria: Root AGENTS.md contains the general commit-message guidance in the existing commit standards area; the guidance requires a concise conventional subject plus a friendly useful body for every non-trivial change; docs and path checks pass; the task is committed and pushed separately after the prior main CI is green.
notes: Added the requested guidance to the root AGENTS.md Commit Messages section. Verified no stale heading links, git diff whitespace, documentation links, and bead lint. No compiler or runtime behavior changed.
close_reason: Repository-wide commit-body guidance added and validated in the canonical root contributor instructions.

title: Publish and enforce the complete typed Elixir stdlib contract
description: Users need a clear answer to which native Elixir API exists in Haxe, how it is spelled, what it generates, and when Term is genuinely part of the Elixir contract.
design: Turn the inventory into browsable reference docs and focused tutorials. Include complete imports, one useful Haxe example, the raw Elixir equivalent, and the typing benefit for non-obvious mappings. Run drift guards, positive and negative compiles, warnings-as-errors, runtime conformance, and installed-package parity across the supported Elixir version line.
acceptance_criteria: The public reference covers every inventoried API and version bound; beginner learning paths explain common collections, strings, files, processes, tasks, errors, and macros without jargon; non-obvious examples show equivalent Elixir; CI rejects documentation/inventory/code drift; the complete suite passes from source and installed packages on minimum and primary versions; remaining open Term boundaries quote the native typespec category and explain safe decoding.

title: Cover Elixir macros, protocols, behaviours, and callback contracts
description: A complete Elixir stdlib surface is more than remote functions. Public macros, behaviours, callbacks, protocols, guards, and compile-time APIs need source shapes that Haxe can validate and lower correctly.
design: Classify each macro as direct compiler lowering, a typed Haxe DSL, or a narrowly documented low-level boundary. Model behaviours and callbacks with typed metadata/interfaces and validate required signatures. Model protocols and guard-safe APIs without pretending ordinary runtime calls are macro expansions. Show generated Elixir require/use/defimpl/callback shapes beside the Haxe source.
acceptance_criteria: Every inventoried public macro, behaviour, callback, protocol, and guard surface is typed or has a narrow documented source-backed boundary; invalid callbacks, options, protocol implementations, and macro-only use fail during Haxe compilation; representative generated modules compile warning-free and match ordinary Elixir forms; there is no blanket raw-Elixir escape hatch used to claim coverage.

title: Implement precise Elixir-style Haxe types for functions and data
description: Existing core externs are useful but uneven: some APIs are well typed, while others are absent or expose Term where the native contract is narrower.
design: Use the shared BEAM contract IR to generate or verify native externs, literal atoms, tuples/results, keyword options, structs, maps, lists, streams, functions, exceptions, generics, and remote types. Keep an exact low-level facade close to Elixir names and add hand-maintained ergonomic Haxe wrappers only where they remove real friction. Preserve direct target calls.
acceptance_criteria: Every inventoried public Elixir function and data type is exposed with an honest Haxe contract or an explicit source-backed open term; no missing API or guessed broad type remains; positive and negative Haxe fixtures prove type checking; generated output snapshots show ordinary direct Elixir calls with no unnecessary runtime layer; minimum and primary supported Elixir versions pass.

title: Inventory the complete public Elixir stdlib by supported version
description: The repository has a hand-picked std/elixir surface, but no versioned list of every public Elixir module, function, macro, callback, and type it does or does not expose to Haxe.
design: Derive a deterministic inventory from the official Elixir release artifacts and documentation metadata for each supported version. Distinguish functions, macros, protocols, behaviours, callbacks, exceptions, structs, types, deprecations, and intentionally internal modules. Link every row to its source contract and current Haxe owner.
acceptance_criteria: Every public API in the selected supported Elixir line appears exactly once with version bounds and status; CI detects upstream additions, removals, deprecations, signature drift, duplicate ownership, and undocumented omissions; internal/private rows are excluded by source-backed rules; the inventory never treats a local file count as API coverage.

title: Dogfood dependency adoption and document companion package promotion
description: Users need believable end-to-end examples across resolved Mix dependency sources, and maintainers need a rule for when repeated app-local contracts become a reusable Haxelib companion package.
design: Choose one simple and one structurally rich real dependency, with at least one Hex dependency and focused Git/path-resolution coverage in the discovery fixtures. Check in discovery snapshots, generated contracts, Haxe positive/negative compile fixtures, raw Elixir output, and a small runtime call without retesting the dependency itself. Write a beginner tutorial covering install, discover, review, compile, test, upgrade, omissions, and escape hatches. Define runtime ownership, naming, versioning, compatibility, release, and security rules for companion packages.
acceptance_criteria: Two resolved dependencies exercise simple and complex metadata, while fixtures also prove Hex, Git, and path identities are handled correctly; generated contracts are used by ordinary Haxe code and call normal dependency APIs at runtime; docs show every command, complete imports, generated files, review diagnostics, exact Elixir equivalents, common failures, and update flow; one package is promoted or a concrete promotion packet is produced; companion layers keep Mix and the original dependency source as runtime owners and pass deterministic inventory, snapshot, compile, and runtime-call gates.
notes: 2026-07-16 planning note: the PhoenixHx LiveReact integration is an early hand-maintained first-class Phoenix companion surface rather than generated dependency-adoption dogfood. It must follow this task’s runtime-ownership, compatibility, versioning, security, and possible separate-Haxelib promotion rules, while stock :live_react remains the runtime owner. Generic Mix dependency discovery is not a prerequisite for the LiveReact integration.

title: Add explicit ownership-safe dependency adoption writes and updates
description: A dependency-level generator must survive reruns and dependency upgrades without silently replacing hand-written Haxe or losing reviewed refinements.
design: Use separate discover and explicit write modes. Store a versioned inventory, diagnostics, and generated-file ownership record. Reject unowned collisions and modified owned files; stage complete updates before publication; show added, removed, changed, and newly uncertain contracts on dependency upgrades. Keep reviewed app wrappers separate from mechanically generated native contracts.
acceptance_criteria: The canonical command supports no-write discovery plus explicit contract generation; first write, no-op rerun, dependency upgrade/downgrade, removed module, interrupted write, modified-owned file, unowned collision, and clean are regression-tested; failures leave live Haxe sources untouched; generated contracts and review metadata are deterministic and portable; existing mix haxe.gen.extern remains a clearly documented single-module scaffold or migrates compatibly.

title: Lower Elixir typespecs into precise reviewable Haxe contracts
description: The current extern generator emits Term for every input and result, which is a useful scaffold but not a properly typed package layer.
design: Introduce a target-contract IR for functions, macros, callbacks, remote/local types, unions, literals, tuples, maps/structs, lists, keyword options, function types, generics, exceptions, and deprecations. Map only proven shapes. Native term() remains Term because that is precise; unsupported or ambiguous specs are omitted with source-positioned diagnostics rather than widened. Preserve native names and arities while allowing a separate ergonomic wrapper layer.
acceptance_criteria: Supported BEAM specs round-trip into deterministic compile-ready Haxe without Dynamic or guessed Term; overloaded and generic contracts, literal atoms, ok/error tuples, option lists, structs/maps, callbacks, behaviours, remote types, and recursive types have positive/negative fixtures; uncertain signatures are omitted with actionable diagnostics; emitted calls lower directly to the original module/function or documented macro expansion; the IR is reusable by the full typed Elixir stdlib epic.

title: Discover Mix dependency contracts from BEAM metadata without loading modules
description: Package adoption needs more than module exports, but introspection must not execute dependency on-load hooks or guess from runtime values. The selected dependency may come from Hex, Git, or a local path.
design: Resolve the selected dependency from the active Mix graph and configuration, include its lock entry when one exists, canonicalize its compiled roots, and read exports, embedded documentation, specs, types, callbacks, macro metadata, behaviours, deprecations, and source references from BEAM artifacts. Record a stable source identity for Hex, Git, and path dependencies. Produce deterministic inventory and diagnostics output. Reject missing, ambiguous, escaped, uncompiled, or mismatched dependency inputs before writes.
acceptance_criteria: Read-only discovery records the exact dependency name, source kind, resolved identity/version, applicable lock identity, and all inspectable modules/contracts deterministically; repeated runs are byte-identical; tests prove dependency on-load code is not triggered; unsafe paths, missing specs/docs, duplicate modules, optional deps, umbrella layouts, Git/path deps, and stale compiled artifacts fail closed or produce explicit review diagnostics; no Haxe files are written in discovery mode.

title: Generate reviewable typed Haxe layers for Mix dependencies
description: Calling one existing Elixir module is possible today, but mix haxe.gen.extern only inventories exported names and gives every parameter and result the generic Term type. A resolved dependency can contain many modules, types, callbacks, macros, configuration steps, and version-specific behavior. Users need a deterministic dependency-level adoption path, not a pile of guessed externs.
design: Keep Mix and the original Hex, Git, or path source as the runtime owners. Add a read-only discovery phase for a dependency selected from the resolved Mix graph, inspect compiled BEAM documentation, exports, attributes, callbacks, and typespecs without loading arbitrary dependency modules, then lower proven contracts through the same reviewed contract model used by the typed Elixir stdlib. Use an explicit write phase, fail-closed ownership and collision rules, precise-or-omitted signatures, review diagnostics, Haxe compile checks, and a small runtime call test. Start with app-local layers; promote stable popular integrations into separate companion Haxelib packages instead of hard-coding them into compiler core. LLM help may propose a patch only after deterministic discovery and never removes review markers without evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A documented dependency-level command can discover and generate contracts for a Mix dependency resolved from Hex, Git, or a local path; discovery records its exact name, source kind, resolved identity/version, applicable lock identity, modules, exports, specs, callbacks, macros, omissions, and diagnostics deterministically; inspection does not trigger dependency module on-load code; writes are explicit, repeatable, ownership-safe, and reject unowned collisions; supported typespecs become precise Haxe types and uncertain APIs are omitted with actionable diagnostics rather than widened; generated contracts pass snapshots plus positive/negative Haxe compile tests and at least one real dependency runtime call; beginner docs show install, discover, review, compile, test, update, and companion-package promotion with the equivalent Elixir calls.

title: Provide a complete typed Haxe surface for the Elixir standard library
description: After 1.0, Elixir-first Haxe should be able to use the complete public Elixir standard library for the supported Elixir release line without dropping to raw target strings or vague Term types where the native contract is more precise.
design: Inventory public modules, functions, macros, callbacks, types, and version bounds from official Elixir documentation and BEAM metadata. Feed them through one reviewed contract model shared with Mix dependency adoption. Map literal atoms, unions, tuples, maps, structs, keyword options, functions, generics, remote types, exceptions, and callbacks into honest Haxe types. Use Term only when the native typespec truly says term or an open boundary is unavoidable. Generate direct native Elixir calls and document the raw target shape beside non-obvious Haxe APIs.
acceptance_criteria: For the supported Elixir version line, every public standard-library module/API is inventoried as typed, intentionally open according to its native spec, macro/DSL-owned, deprecated, or narrowly non-applicable; no API is silently omitted; generated Haxe contracts compile in positive and negative fixtures; representative runtime conformance and output snapshots prove direct native calls; version drift is detected in CI; user docs include complete imports, Haxe usage, raw Elixir equivalents, and migration notes; no blanket Dynamic or guessed Term signatures are used to claim completeness.

title: Showcase typed Ecto and PhoenixHx value in the README
description: Replace the weak README slogan and add an evidence-backed product showcase built from real compiling Haxe sources and their generated Elixir. Lead with compile-time checked Ecto queries, show the early failure mode, and highlight PhoenixHx, shared browser/server contracts, Haxe-authored ExUnit, and OTP without overstating pre-1.0 maturity.
design: Use checked excerpts from executable examples and snapshot/negative fixtures. Keep Haxe and target Elixir adjacent, include enough imports/types to understand the checked boundary, link canonical full sources, explain why the Haxe layer improves the target primitive, and keep the landing page concise. Retain MessageRules static inline constants if experiment/evidence shows they avoid Haxe static-field runtime machinery, and document that reason in source.
acceptance_criteria: README has a stronger accurate headline; a real TypedQuery example and generated Ecto.Query output; a compile-time invalid-field example tied to negative coverage; a compact high-value PhoenixHx/shared-contract/testing/OTP path; MessageRules inline intent is explicit; markdown links, focused Ecto positive/negative fixtures, relevant example output/runtime/WAE, path hygiene, package parity, and exact-SHA CI are green.
close_reason: Replaced the README headline; added checked Haxe-to-Ecto source/output and invalid-field evidence; showcased typed LiveView events, routes, OTP, ExUnit, and portable BEAM/JS domain logic; documented why MessageRules uses static inline final. Focused Ecto fixtures, all examples QA, full npm test, CI guards, docs links, Haxe formatting, snippet syntax, and path hygiene pass. Package parity and exact-SHA CI will gate the push handoff.

title: Verify CI-downloaded security tooling and define dependency upkeep
description: CI downloads a security-scanner binary without independently verifying its release artifact, while automated dependency update pull requests are disabled. Existing advisory gates reduce risk but do not define how pinned tooling and dependencies are authenticated and kept current.
design: Use a pinned trusted action or verify downloaded artifacts against a pinned checksum/signature from an authenticated source. Document the dependency review cadence and ownership while retaining bounded npm and Hex advisory gates. Avoid broad automatic updates that bypass project-specific compatibility review.
acceptance_criteria: Security tooling provenance is verified before execution; a negative test or reviewable CI check detects a mismatched artifact; dependency update ownership and cadence are documented; pinned Actions and scanner versions are auditable; security docs state actual coverage and residual gaps.
close_reason: CI now verifies the pinned Gitleaks archive fingerprint before extraction or execution, rejects tampered bytes in a regression test, and guards every external GitHub Action with a full commit SHA. Dependency ownership, monthly and pre-release review cadence, update steps, actual coverage, and remaining trust limits are documented. Focused security/workflow/docs checks, all repository guards, full npm test, and npm/Hex advisory audits pass; the pushed Ubuntu CI job will verify the real Linux binary path.

title: Narrow ChangesetEnsureReturn to Ecto-owned AST
description: Pass-scope parity showed ChangesetEnsureReturn changes tail carriers in the ordinary regression/ElixirInjectionExpansion fixture even though its documented contract says it only handles functions containing structured Ecto.Changeset calls. Diagnose the earlier shape/metadata coupling and make the pass truly Ecto-scoped without changing non-Ecto function results.
design: Use per-pass AST snapshots and the function-result invariant to identify why the pass reports hasChangeset for unrelated generated modules or why later hygiene depends on its appended carrier. Fix the earliest incorrect shape or analysis boundary; do not key on module names, weaken result invariants, or update snapshots to nil-returning output.
acceptance_criteria: ChangesetEnsureReturn is eligible only for typed Ecto capability; regression/ElixirInjectionExpansion and representative core/stdlib output remain byte-identical; Ecto changeset fixtures retain their return values; a focused regression or invariant test captures the coupling; full snapshots, runtime, examples, package parity, and todo QA pass.

title: Emit native float comparisons for proven finite operands
description: Known-finite Haxe Float comparisons currently lower through Reflaxe.Elixir.HaxeFloat helpers, so even a comparison such as a method result against the finite literal 1.5 emits HaxeFloat.neq/2. The helper is required whenever an operand may be a tagged Haxe NaN or +/-Infinity sentinel, but it is avoidable when the compiler can prove both evaluated values are ordinary finite BEAM numbers. Improve handwritten-looking Elixir without weakening the existing Haxe special-float contract.
design: Add a conservative proof in the numeric operator lowering source of truth, not a late AST/text cleanup. Start with intrinsically finite typed constants and other locally provable finite shapes; do not assume arbitrary Float-returning calls, Dynamic values, extern/native results, parsing, arithmetic with overflow/domain behavior, or values crossing reflection/serialization boundaries are finite. Preserve left-to-right evaluation and evaluate each operand exactly once. Emit native Elixir comparison operators only when both operands are proven unable to carry HaxeFloat sentinels; otherwise retain HaxeFloat.eq/neq/lt/lte/gt/gte. Keep this as one compiler pipeline and document why portable output sometimes retains the helper.
acceptance_criteria: Focused snapshots show native ==/!= and ordered comparisons for every accepted proven-finite shape and retain HaxeFloat calls for unknown Float, Dynamic, NaN, +/-Infinity, extern/native, and sentinel-producing arithmetic shapes; runtime tests cover finite equality/order plus Haxe NaN/infinity semantics and demonstrate no duplicated or reordered side effects; proof logic is centralized, conservative, and documented with WHAT/WHY/HOW/EXAMPLES; generated-output audit documentation classifies retained HaxeFloat calls as semantic compatibility artifacts; full snapshots, Haxe ExUnit stdlib parity, examples WAE/runtime, Mix tests, source/package parity, and todo sentinel Playwright remain green.

title: Document the authoring-to-output gradient and prove final source/package parity
description: Close the workstream with documentation that a Haxe developer unfamiliar with Reflaxe can use to predict generated Elixir: Elixir-first functional source should approach raw Elixir; portable/imperative source may retain explicit semantic machinery; formatting is distinct from structural idiomaticity; runtime helpers must have a stated reason.
design: Keep the roadmap audit as historical evidence and update canonical authoring, compiler-development, production-readiness, README navigation, examples, and changelog surfaces with the final contract. Show representative Haxe, generated Elixir, and raw handwritten Elixir together. Record remaining justified artifacts and future work rather than claiming all Haxe can erase into native syntax.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical docs explain the output gradient, one-pipeline/profile contract, formatter modes, DCE/runtime footprint, virtual-dispatch and stdlib helper reasons, behaviour/protocol decisions, and how to review generated code; examples include compile-ready context and raw Elixir equivalents; source checkout and built haxelib generate equivalent representative core/stdlib/Phoenix output; full CI-equivalent suite, stdlib runtime, guards, examples/output/WAE/runtime, Mix, package smoke, path scan, async todo Playwright sentinel, and latest GitHub CI are green; epic evidence records exact commands and results.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-07-13 documentation/evidence slice complete. README now shows checked Elixir-first, imperative-to-Enum.map, and PhoenixHx HXX-to-~H source/output pairs; the canonical runtime guide distinguishes compiler-only -D reflaxe_runtime from generated helper calls and records conservative HaxeFloat/HaxeThrow module retention. The sibling comparison adopted Ruby's concise compiler/framework product framing and Rust's compiler-first/runtime-fallback framing where accurate. Verified: guard:docs-links, test:handwritten-output, ci:guards, npm test, test:examples, test:examples-qa, test:haxelib-package, path scan, and the async todo Playwright sentinel (5/5). This advances but does not close 3qh.18 because its remaining optimization and target-contract dependencies are still open.

title: Reduce generated runtime/support footprint and make DCE policy explicit
description: The Elixir-first LiveView example emitted 58 files for 11 application modules; `-dce full` reduced it to 42, leaving both build-policy debt and target runtime/facade opportunities. Examples 14 and 16 cannot simply enable full DCE because their compile-only modules are not reachable.
design: First give representative compile-only examples a meaningful reachable runtime harness. Then classify emitted modules as application, semantically required runtime, reflection support, type-only facade, or accidental reachability. Use Haxe/Reflaxe reachability and package layout mechanisms, not deletion of generated files after compilation.
acceptance_criteria: Examples 13, 14, and 16 have documented reachable-entry/DCE contracts and meaningful runtime coverage; a checked-in report records before/after module categories and sizes; type-only facades and unused runtime modules are suppressed only when reflection/constructor/exception/stdlib tests prove safety; source checkout and built package emit the same required module set; package smoke, examples output/WAE/runtime, stdlib, and todo QA pass; CI detects material unexplained footprint regressions without a brittle exact global count.

title: Normalize pure nested tail branches to idiomatic cond
description: Straight nested tail-position if/else-if chains often remain parenthesized nested `if` expressions. Handwritten Elixir generally uses `cond` when several ordered predicates choose one result.
design: Rewrite only branch chains that share one value context and have equivalent lazy predicate ordering, lexical scope, exception timing, and branch result type. Do not rewrite two-way conditions where `if` is clearer, mutation/rebinding chains that require explicit threading, or branches with compiler return carriers.
acceptance_criteria: Focused core and Elixir-first snapshots show direct cond output for three-or-more pure ordered branches; runtime tests prove first-match and fallback semantics; negative fixtures retain if/case for two-way branches, pattern matching, receiver mutation, non-local returns, and side-effect-sensitive conditions; formatter, WAE, snapshot, example, and runtime gates pass.

title: Use native String operations when Haxe semantics are provably identical
description: Even Elixir-first output can leak StringTools helpers for operations whose concrete argument shapes may permit direct String calls. Keep StringTools when Haxe semantics differ, but avoid it when equivalence is statically proven.
design: Create an operation-by-operation semantic table before rewriting. Proof conditions must cover empty strings, separators, Unicode/codepoint behavior, negative or out-of-range indexes, nullability, replacement rules, and exception behavior. Reuse target-native extern surfaces where possible. Never apply a broad name-based StringTools replacement.
acceptance_criteria: Each optimized StringTools operation has upstream or local Haxe-authored runtime parity tests for edge cases and a documented native equivalence rule; representative Elixir-first output calls String directly where proven; portable cases with semantic differences retain the helper and explain why; source and package output agree; upstream-unitstd, full snapshots, examples, and todo QA remain green.

title: Replace avoidable pure expression IIFEs with ordinary Elixir bindings
description: Generated output sometimes uses `(fn -> ... end).()` only to sequence pure local calculations inside an expression. Handwritten Elixir normally hoists these calculations into ordinary bindings in the surrounding block. Some IIFEs are semantically required for scope or control-flow isolation, so this must be selective.
design: Track expression purity, binding scope, and evaluation order in the AST. Hoist only when bindings cannot escape or collide, surrounding short-circuit/lazy behavior is unchanged, exceptions occur at the same point, and no non-local return or receiver-rebinding carrier crosses the boundary. Do not strip anonymous calls after printing.
acceptance_criteria: Representative Elixir-first and portable fixtures lose avoidable pure IIFEs and show readable pre-bindings; negative fixtures preserve IIFEs or another explicit boundary for short-circuit branches, local shadowing, closures, exceptions, mutation threading, and non-local returns; no numeric-suffix/name-hygiene regressions appear; structural snapshots and runtime assertions cover both paths; full generated-output and runtime gates pass.

title: Lower proven pure append accumulators to Enum.map or comprehensions
description: Portable array-push loops can currently become Enum.reduce with repeated Enum.concat, as in the portable chat Transcript example. When a loop only builds one output element per input and the accumulator is otherwise unobserved, handwritten Elixir should use Enum.map or a for-comprehension and avoid O(n²) append behavior.
design: Implement a proof-driven IR rewrite, not source-name heuristics. Require a fresh accumulator, one order-preserving append per iteration, no reads of partial state, no break/continue/non-local return carrier, no receiver mutation, and no index/state dependency that changes semantics. Fall back to the existing reducer whenever proof fails.
acceptance_criteria: The Transcript fixture emits Enum.map or an equally direct comprehension and preserves exact ordering/content at runtime; negative fixtures retain reducers for conditional append, multiple append, break/continue, iterator rebinding, partial-accumulator reads, exceptions, and stateful receivers; the experimental idiomatic-comprehensions define is either made meaningful with a documented contract or retired without creating a second backend; generated code is formatted; snapshots, stdlib runtime, examples, and todo QA pass.
notes: Implemented in 5315834b9. Added a typed, proof-driven fresh Array projection rewrite that emits direct Enum.map only for one ordered append per Array input; conditional or multiple appends, partial accumulator reads, control-flow carriers, persistent iterators, stateful receivers, self-iteration, non-fresh arrays, and ambiguous inherited remaps retain established lowerings. Retired the unused idiomatic_comprehensions define and updated the changelog, README, lowering guide, feature docs, audit, agent guidance, package fixture, corpus, and reviewed snapshots. Verification green: npm test across all positive and negative categories, 398 Elixir parses, 255 Mix tests, runtime and formatting gates; ci:guards; 132 Haxe ExUnit stdlib tests; full examples output/WAE/runtime/corpus QA; async todo QA run 1783968691 with Playwright 5/5. Exact committed source/package parity passed for 5315834b9, including explicit Enum.map assertions, byte-identical generated Elixir, structural parity, canonical formatting, and installed-package Phoenix compile. Discovered pre-existing correctness bugs are tracked separately as 3qh.23 and 3qh.24.
close_reason: Proven fresh one-to-one Array append loops now emit direct Enum.map with conservative semantic fallbacks, complete docs and regression coverage, final source/package parity, full CI-equivalent validation, and Phoenix Playwright QA.

title: Migrate release documentation and prove the simplified protocol live
description: Update the canonical versioning, releasing, package-consumer, recovery, README, AGENTS, and historical architecture documentation to describe durable policy rather than generated current prose. Record haxe.elixir.codex-m81 and v0.14.23 as predecessor happy-path evidence, not the reference design. Migrate without rewriting or deleting existing public v0.14.x tags.
acceptance_criteria: Docs explain major-zero initial development versus SemVer prerelease syntax, tag-owned version lineage, Conventional Commit bump behavior, per-major approval, two-phase normal publication plus existing-tag repair, immutable remote tags, and consumer digest verification; stale generated markers and current-version prose are removed or made dynamic; the first simplified release records source SHA, tag, run/job IDs, asset name, bytes, SHA-256, tag relationships, and host immutability; an immediately subsequent docs/no-release commit proves a clean no-op; full repository, package, Phoenix dogfood, sentinel, release-contract, and recovery tests plus GitHub CI are green.
close_reason: Published and verified immutable v0.14.26 reference release, proved the immediate docs-only no-op, corrected and regression-tested release-note rendering in immutable v0.14.27, and recorded exact CI, tag, artifact, digest, host-control, consumer, and attestation evidence.

title: Stdlib parity: typed array and ArrayBufferView semantics
description: Classify and validate haxe.io.ArrayBufferView plus Float32Array, Float64Array, Int32Array, UInt8Array, UInt16Array, and UInt32Array against the official Haxe implementations. The primary semantic risk is shared Bytes storage across sub/subarray/fromBytes views under BEAM immutability; numeric width, endian behavior, bounds behavior, and mutation return values must also match.
acceptance_criteria: All seven official upstream unitstd specs are enabled and run on BEAM or any adaptation is narrowly justified; classification selects official fallback, a real BEAM override, or explicit unsupported behavior from evidence; shared-view mutation, offsets/lengths, integer wrapping, floats, and fromBytes behavior are covered; no duplicate stdlib source is added if fallback works; source/package parity, snapshots, docs/changelog, examples, full CI, and async todo-app Playwright QA pass.
close_reason: Verified official Haxe fallback for ArrayBufferView and all six typed arrays; fixed grouped constructor values and typed method defaults through Reflaxe metadata; added upstream runtime, snapshots, package parity, docs/changelog; full CI-equivalent suite and async Phoenix Playwright QA pass. Follow-ups track reflaxe_runtime UX and StringTools diagnostics separately.

title: Stdlib parity: classify haxe.io.Mime and haxe.io.Scheme
description: Classify the reference-only haxe.io.Mime and haxe.io.Scheme modules before adding any target code. Both are official Haxe enum abstracts over String, so verify whether unchanged upstream fallback preserves constants, String conversion, and custom values on BEAM and through the built Reflaxe package.
acceptance_criteria: Classification is documented as upstream fallback or changed only with concrete contrary evidence; no duplicate target override is added when official Haxe std works; local Haxe-authored ExUnit covers representative constants and custom String values; the upstream unitstd manifest records the no-spec decision; source-checkout and built-package smoke exercise the same fallback; parity/docs/changelog are updated; focused runtime, package, guards, full CI, and async todo-app QA pass.
close_reason: Classified Mime and Scheme as verified official Haxe String enum-abstract fallbacks; added BEAM runtime, snapshot, source/package parity, manifest, changelog, roadmap, and README documentation coverage; full local CI and async Playwright QA pass.

title: Reconcile false v1 history with the real 0.x public posture
description: Audit public and historical docs that conflict with the real v0.14.x lineage. README and VERSIONING_AND_STABILITY correctly say pre-1.0, while production-readiness, PRDs, patterns, and AGENTS text still describe v1.0.x or v1.1.x as shipped/current. Preserve genuine historical intent but prevent those pages from being read as current release truth.
acceptance_criteria: Every current-facing entrypoint obtains its posture from generated manifest blocks or links to the canonical posture page; historical v1 plans are explicitly dated and labeled unshipped/superseded where appropriate; no current page claims a v1 tag or stable line that does not exist; navigation/link guards cover the canonical status path; README, docs index, releasing guide, production-readiness page, relevant PRDs, and AGENTS wording are reviewed.
close_reason: Reconciled current-facing documentation with the real pre-1.0 lineage, labeled unshipped v1 milestones as superseded history, required canonical posture links in public entrypoints, and made release fixtures advance from the manifest version.

title: Normalize haxe.Exception Reflaxe source layout
description: Move the authored Elixir haxe.Exception override from src/haxe/Exception.cross.hx to std/elixir/_std/haxe/Exception.hx without changing executable code or target semantics. Keep source development wired through scoped HXML, let Reflaxe build generate packaged .cross.hx, update guards/docs/changelog, and validate compiler, package, PhoenixHx, examples, stdlib, snapshots, and todo-app QA.
acceptance_criteria: No checked-in src/**/*.cross.hx remains; source-mode haxe.Exception resolves from std/elixir/_std; built package contains src/haxe/Exception.cross.hx; generated Elixir is unchanged except source-map path metadata; full local CI parity and async Playwright QA pass; latest pushed workflows are green.
close_reason: Completed conventional Reflaxe source/package layout hardening: external source checkouts render canonical scoped HXML; releases publish a Reflaxe-built zip; source and installed-package compilation emit byte-identical Elixir; full snapshots, stdlib runtime, examples/WAE, docs smoke, dogfood, Mix, and async todo-app Playwright QA pass.

title: Guard installed package CLI entrypoint
description: Extend the haxelib package smoke to validate the installed package CLI entrypoint and fix the package layout issue it exposed: BEAM sys.* replacements must be authored under std/elixir/_std/sys so Reflaxe packages them as .cross.hx instead of shadowing host/eval sys.* during CLI runs.
acceptance_criteria: BEAM sys.* replacements live under std/elixir/_std/sys; the layout guard rejects new plain std/sys modules; package smoke asserts packaged sys.* files are .cross.hx, runs the installed Run version command with the pinned Haxe binary, documents the convention in changelog/docs, and local package/layout/example checks pass.
close_reason: Moved BEAM sys.* std replacements into std/elixir/_std/sys, guarded plain std/sys, validated package CLI/artifact behavior, full snapshots, stdlib runtime, examples, Mix fast, and async todo-app Playwright sentinel.

title: Guard Reflaxe package artifact layout
description: Strengthen haxelib package smoke coverage so the installed artifact keeps using Reflaxe build flattening instead of source-only std layouts or hand-rolled package structure.
acceptance_criteria: Package smoke asserts source-only std/elixir/_std and haxelib reflaxe metadata are absent from installed artifacts while flattened .cross.hx overrides remain present; docs/changelog record the release-validation convention; local package/layout guards pass.
close_reason: Implemented package artifact layout guard; validated stdlib layout, docs links, diff check, and haxelib package smoke.

title: Enable upstream Date and DateTools stdlib runtime specs
close_reason: Enabled upstream Date and DateTools unitstd runtime specs, fixed Date/Date_Impl_ BEAM semantics, updated docs/snapshots/examples, and verified stdlib/runtime/examples/QA sentinel.

title: Stdlib parity: classify haxe.ds.Option target surface
description: Classify haxe.ds.Option as the local Elixir-target option enum surface rather than an untriaged no-upstream-spec gap. Add focused Haxe-authored ExUnit runtime coverage for Some/None pattern matching and core OptionTools behavior, then update the upstream unitstd manifest and stdlib support matrix wording.
acceptance_criteria: Local stdlib runtime tests cover Option enum pattern matching plus representative OptionTools helpers; manifest and support matrix explain the target surface and lack of upstream unitstd spec; stdlib parity guards pass.
close_reason: Classified haxe.ds.Option as the local Elixir-target option surface, added Haxe-authored ExUnit coverage for Some/None and representative OptionTools helpers, fixed OptionTools.all to preserve None semantics on BEAM without relying on return-in-reducer lowering, updated generated option-patterns output/map, manifest, and support matrix. Verification: test:haxe-exunit-stdlib; guard:hx-format; guard:upstream-unitstd; guard:stdlib-parity; guard:docs-links; test:quick; test:examples-output; test:examples-elixir; test:examples-runtime. title: Generate typed LiveView hook protocol bindings
description: Adopt and implement PhoenixHx typed LiveView event protocols as an opt-in framework macro layer. Developers declare a shared Haxe enum protocol once; PhoenixHx generates event names, target-native JS hook push helpers, target-native Elixir/JS payload encode/decode helpers, and server LiveView dispatch helpers. LiveViews keep normal Phoenix-shaped handleEvent(event, params, socket) and explicitly call the generated dispatcher. No metadata means no behavior change. WirePayload/WireCodec remain low-level manual/open-boundary tools, not the default generated protocol path.
design:
Adopt protocol-first, explicit-dispatch, handler-validated v1. Prefer @:liveEventProtocol on a shared enum and @:liveEvents(ProtocolEnum) on the LiveView, with derived names by default and string overrides for interop. Do not auto-wrap or replace handleEvent in v1. Do not infer protocols from arbitrary handleEvent bodies. Defer typed replies and custom runtime event systems. Use docs/08-roadmap/phoenixhx-live-event-protocols.md as the source of truth.

Implementation note from Tink Web: build a normalized macro model first (LiveEventCollection, LiveEventSignature, LiveEventPayload, LiveEventField), then generate browser push helpers and server dispatch helpers from that same model. Borrow Tink Web's declaration -> model -> client/server generation pattern, but not its HTTP router complexity, handler-body inference, or unstable generated counters.
acceptance_criteria:
A shared enum protocol such as ProfileHookEvent generates a companion such as ProfileHookEvents with typed encode/decode and per-event JS push helpers.
The macro implementation first normalizes protocol declarations into a deterministic shared model used by both generated client helpers and generated server dispatch helpers.
ProfileLive can opt in with @:liveEvents(ProfileHookEvent), gets a derived dispatchProfileHookEvent helper, and keeps an explicit dispatch-first handleEvent fallback.
Generated built-in payload encoders/decoders use target-native JS object and Elixir map operations, not WirePayload/WireCodec runtime helper plumbing; generated Elixir/JS is snapshot-tested and reviewable.
Known events with malformed payloads are consumed safely instead of falling through as unknown events.
Diagnostics cover duplicate event names, unsupported Dynamic/map payloads, duplicate wire keys, missing/wrong handlers, and dispatcher-call validation; dispatcher-call validation is warning by default and strict-mode error under a define.
Todo-app migrates clipboard_copied and ping from manual HookEvents to generated protocol helpers while direct Phoenix handleEvent remains documented as the baseline alternative.
Validation includes Haxe client/server builds, snapshots/diagnostics, todo-app ExUnit coverage, and async QA sentinel with Playwright for clipboard flash and ping no-op behavior.
