title: Add RailsHx-inspired PhoenixHx todo learning example
description:
PLAN_REF: plans/active/railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo-example.md

FILES
- New example root: examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/
- Example docs: examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/README.md and examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/docs/RAILSHX_TO_PHOENIXHX.md
- Example Haxe app: examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/src_haxe/**
- Example assets/client: examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/assets/**, build-client.hxml, package.json if needed
- Example tests: examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/src_haxe/test/** and examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/e2e/**
- Build/config: examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/build.hxml, build-tests.hxml, build-client.hxml, mix.exs, config/*.exs
- QA registry: examples/qa-manifest.json
- Examples index/docs links: examples/README.md and any canonical docs index that lists numbered examples
- Source reference only, do not modify unless explicitly required: https://github.com/fullofcaffeine/reflaxe.ruby/tree/main/examples/todoapp_rails

WHAT
Create a didactic Phoenix/Reflaxe.Elixir example that ports the RailsHx todo app UX from https://github.com/fullofcaffeine/reflaxe.ruby/tree/main/examples/todoapp_rails/ while using Phoenix-native architecture. The output should teach how the same Haxe-authored product surface maps differently to Rails and Phoenix: RailsHx uses ActiveRecord, ActionController, HHX-to-ERB, Turbo Streams, Devise, and Rails route helpers; PhoenixHx should use Ecto, contexts, LiveView, inline HXX function components, PubSub/LiveView updates, session/on_mount auth, and Phoenix routes.

USER-FACING UX CONTRACT
- Preserve the RailsHx visual hierarchy and interaction vocabulary where practical: authenticated app chrome/top bar, guest sign-in/demo access, todo composer, summary/empty state, todo cards/list, completion/toggle/delete flows, user attribution, status/flash polish, and progressive focus/scroll niceties.
- Include chat and user-management panels only if they fit cleanly after the todo/auth slice. If they are too broad, create follow-up child tasks for them instead of overloading the first implementation.
- The app should feel like the RailsHx sample viewed through Phoenix conventions, not like a clone of the existing examples/todo-app product surface.

ALGORITHM / IMPLEMENTATION PLAN
1. Inventory RailsHx source
   - Read https://github.com/fullofcaffeine/reflaxe.ruby/tree/main/examples/todoapp_rails/README.md, models, controllers, views, shared/TodoHooks.hx, client/TodoClient.hx, and e2e/todoapp.spec.ts.
   - Write the UX contract into the new README before implementation drifts.

2. Scaffold a numbered Phoenix example
   - Use existing local Phoenix example patterns, preferring compact shapes from examples/13-elixir-first-liveview or examples/15-phoenix-chat-haxe-first over copying the heavyweight examples/todo-app wholesale.
   - Keep Phoenix project files idiomatic: mix.exs/config/router/assets remain Phoenix-shaped; Haxe owns app/domain/UI/test code where the example is trying to teach Haxe authoring.

3. Port Rails domain to Ecto/Phoenix boundaries
   - Todo/User required; ChatMessage optional follow-up unless implemented within the same bounded scope.
   - Model fields and validations become Ecto schema + changeset + context functions.
   - Rails strong params become context-layer changeset casting/validation. Do not create a fake strong-params API.
   - Owner/user fields must be server-controlled, matching the RailsHx security intent.

4. Port routes/auth/session edges
   - Implement Phoenix routes for home/todos and demo guest sign-in/logout.
   - Use Phoenix session/controller/on_mount conventions instead of Devise/Warden compatibility facades.
   - Document where a real production auth library would replace the demo session flow.

5. Port UI to LiveView and inline HXX
   - Use inline HXX/TSX authoring. Do not use hxx('...') / HXX.hxx('...') except for explicit legacy coverage, which this task is not.
   - Extract function components for top bar, composer, summary, todo list/card, and optional side panels.
   - Use LiveView events for create/toggle/delete and PubSub/handle_info where cross-session updates are shown.
   - Use CSS/assets adapted from the RailsHx sample as a visual reference, while keeping Phoenix asset conventions.

6. Port progressive client behavior
   - Create typed shared hook constants equivalent to RailsHx shared/TodoHooks.hx.
   - Compile Haxe client hooks through Genes if the example has browser-only behavior.
   - Keep client code progressive. It may handle autofocus, scroll preservation, small status flashes, or key handling; it must not duplicate server-rendered HTML.

7. Tests and QA
   - Add Haxe-authored ExUnit tests for route/session/LiveView CRUD flows.
   - Add a thin Playwright smoke based on the RailsHx spec and selectors.
   - Register the example in examples/qa-manifest.json with meaningful runtime/E2E coverage or an explicit compile-only rationale for any intentionally uncovered layer.
   - Update example generated output/snapshots if this repo tracks generated output for the new example.

8. Documentation
   - README must link to https://github.com/fullofcaffeine/reflaxe.ruby/tree/main/examples/todoapp_rails/ and explain how to run and validate the PhoenixHx port.
   - Add docs/RAILSHX_TO_PHOENIXHX.md with a concrete crosswalk: ActiveRecord -> Ecto, ActionController -> LiveView/controller edges, strong params -> changeset, HHX partial -> inline HXX component, Turbo Streams -> LiveView/PubSub, Devise -> session/on_mount auth, Rails routes -> Phoenix routes, Rails tests -> Haxe-authored ExUnit/Playwright.
   - Include a future-tooling section separating deterministic conversion inventory from human decisions and possible later Haxe abstractions.

FAILURE MODES / GAPS TO SURFACE
- If Phoenix route helper/verified route typing is too weak, use a small example-local wrapper and document the gap; do not invent non-existent Phoenix APIs.
- If typed function component/local ergonomics are missing compared to RailsHx HHX partials, document the gap and create a follow-up task instead of widening types to Dynamic.
- If chat/user-management make the task too broad, split them into child tasks after the todo/auth slice.
- If the app needs compiler/framework surface changes, stop and create separate narrowly scoped tasks with regression coverage.
- Do not commit generated files containing machine-local absolute paths.

TESTS
- Haxe compile for the new example via its build.hxml/build-tests.hxml.
- Haxe-authored ExUnit tests for create/toggle/delete/session/empty-state flows.
- Playwright smoke for home/demo sign-in/todo composer/list/toggle/delete using resilient selectors.
- examples/qa-manifest.json guarded by npm run guard:examples-qa.
- Example compile/output/strict/runtime suites updated as appropriate.

VERIFICATION
- npm run guard:examples-qa
- npm run test:examples
- npm run test:examples-output
- npm run test:examples-elixir
- npm run test:examples-runtime
- New example runtime smoke via scripts/qa-sentinel.sh with --async and --deadline if a Phoenix server is booted.
- For any todo-app-adjacent runtime verification, use the QA sentinel only; never run mix phx.server in the foreground.

ROLLOUT
- Add as a new numbered example; do not replace examples/todo-app.
- Keep the example self-contained and educational.
- Commit docs, source, tests, manifest updates, and intended generated-output changes together.
- Push after local verification, then confirm latest main CI is green before starting the next task.

title: IMap design: native %{}-backed haxe.ds.Map surface
description:
# WHAT
Decide whether the Elixir target should implement the `haxe.ds.*Map` family as a thin, native `%{}` wrapper where `get/set/exists/remove/keys/iterator` compile to `Map.get/3`, `Map.put/3`, etc.

# WHY
Boundary values (Phoenix params, Presence lists, JSON payloads) are frequently plain Elixir maps. When Haxe code expects a `Map<K,V>` API, we either:
- convert at the boundary (allocations + less idiomatic), or
- make the Elixir target’s Map implementation *be* a native map (best DevX, but requires careful parity + macro safety).

# OPTIONS
A) Boundary conversion only
- Keep `haxe.ds.*Map` as-is (tree-backed / wrapper structs).
- Convert boundary `%{}` to Haxe Map at decode boundaries.

B) Native map-backed `haxe.ds.*Map` (Elixir-target implementation)
- `new Map()` produces a `%{}` (or a tiny wrapper) and methods compile to `Map.*` calls.
- Great DX at client/server boundaries; less “gotcha” behavior.
- Needs careful work for:
  - macro/eval safety (dual-mode stubs)
  - iteration semantics / stable ordering expectations
  - `IMap` typing surface compatibility

# ACCEPTANCE
- Record a decision with explicit tradeoffs and impact on:
  - WAE
  - macro/eval
  - performance
  - portability to non-Elixir targets
- If (B) is selected, spin up an implementation plan under the stdlib parity epic with runtime behavior tests.
acceptance_criteria: - Decision recorded with pros/cons and chosen direction\n- If chosen, follow-up tasks created for implementation + tests
close_reason: Chose staged native-map backing for Elixir built-in Haxe map surfaces: Map/StringMap/IntMap use native %{ } and Map.* lowering, while ObjectMap identity semantics and Map abstract conversion/copy behavior remain explicit follow-up work. Documented WAE, macro/eval, performance, and portability tradeoffs; created follow-ups haxe.elixir-hm47.23.7, haxe.elixir-hm47.23.8, and haxe.elixir-hm47.23.9.

title: Stdlib parity: runtime behavior test harness (Haxe→ExUnit)
description:
# WHAT
Add a reusable runtime behavior test harness for stdlib parity work (authored in Haxe, compiled to idiomatic ExUnit).

# WHY
Snapshot tests lock code shape, but many stdlib surfaces are semantic (iterators, exceptions, Bytes IO, regex, map semantics). We need executable runtime tests to prove behavior matches Haxe expectations on BEAM and to prevent regressions that snapshots can’t catch.

# HOW
- Define a consistent location and conventions for stdlib runtime tests (for example: a Haxe folder compiled into the existing ExUnit test project).
- Provide tiny helpers to:
  - compile/run only the runtime suite quickly
  - print clear diffs/assert messages
  - keep execution bounded (no hanging processes)
- Seed with a few canonical tests (exceptions + Bytes IO) and make it the place where future stdlib-parity tasks add their behavior assertions.

# Acceptance
- One command runs the runtime suite locally (bounded) and is wired into CI `Tests`.
- At least one behavior-oriented stdlib test exists that would not be caught by snapshots alone.
acceptance_criteria: - Runtime test harness exists and is documented\n- CI runs the runtime suite in the Tests job\n- Initial tests cover at least one semantic surface
close_reason: Implemented focused Haxe-authored ExUnit stdlib runtime harness command, wired it into CI Tests, documented conventions, seeded BytesInput/BytesOutput runtime assertions, and fixed Bytes mutation semantics on BEAM exposed by the harness.

description:
# Goal
Improve codegen for user-written “imperative array mutation loops” by rewriting proven-safe patterns into `Enum.map/2` (or `Enum.with_index/1 |> Enum.map/2`) so output is both idiomatic and efficient.

# Problem
Today, a loop like:

```haxe
var i = 0;
while (i < array.length) {
  array[i] = transform(array[i]);
  i++;
}
```

**compiles correctly**, but because `Array` is represented as an immutable list for the Elixir target, indexed updates require rebuilding the list. In a loop this can become O(n²) and the generated Elixir is less idiomatic.

We already generate optimal code for *Haxe-desugared* `array.map/filter` patterns, but not for arbitrary user-authored while loops.

# Desired behavior
When the compiler can prove the loop is a pure “map-in-place” (or map-with-index) and the counter is not semantically observed afterward, rewrite to:

- `array = Enum.map(array, fn item -> ... end)`
- or `array = Enum.with_index(array) |> Enum.map(fn {item, i} -> ... end)` when index is used in the RHS.

# Safety constraints
Only rewrite when all of the following hold:
- loop condition is a simple bound over `i` vs `array.length`
- body has exactly one array element update and one counter increment (no early returns, break/continue, or additional mutations)
- the counter’s post-loop value is not observed (either it’s a synthetic `_g*` var or provably unused after the loop within the containing block)
- array reference is stable (local or a stable captured value)

# Tests
Add a focused snapshot under `test/snapshot/core/` that:
- compiles the imperative loop form
- validates the output is rewritten to Enum.map/with_index
- includes a “do not rewrite” negative/adjacent case (e.g. i used after loop)
close_reason: Implemented safe map-in-place array loop lowering to Enum.map/Enum.with_index with block-level counter-use guard, docs, focused snapshot, full chunks, examples WAE, mix-fast, and todo-app Playwright sentinel.

title: HXX: TSX-like diagnostics (precise spans + suggestions)
description:
## What
Improve the TSX-like UX by making HXX/HEEx diagnostics point to the exact tag/attr span in the original Haxe string, and add low-noise suggestions.

## Why
TSX feels good because errors land on the exact JSX node/prop with actionable suggestions. We already carry some spans; this task makes them consistent and used everywhere.

## How
- Ensure HEEx fragment metadata always includes spans for:
  - tag name span
  - attribute name span
  - attribute value span
- Update linter errors (unknown tag/attr, strict modes, phx-* registry checks) to use these spans rather than whole-~H positions.
- Add "did you mean" suggestions for:
  - mistyped attributes on registered tags
  - unknown dot-component prop names (when component resolves)

## Acceptance
- New/updated snapshots show errors pointing to the correct column range.
- No new string-only heuristics; use heexAST + spans.
close_reason: Implemented and verified

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Completed TSX-like diagnostics: added precise tag/attr/value spans in HEEx AST metadata (ElixirAST + HeexFragmentBuilder), threaded span-aware positions through HeexAssignsTypeLinterTransforms, and added low-noise did-you-mean suggestions for HTML attrs, Phoenix core attrs, and user component props. Also ensured span fields survive AST transform mapping in ElixirASTTransformer. Verification: npm run test:phoenix (70/70), make -C test summary-negative (66/66), make -C test -j1 summary-negative-safe (66/66), npm run test:quick (core/stdlib/regression + syntax validation), npm run test:mix-fast, npm run qa:sentinel (RUN_ID=1770837674 DONE status=0). title: PERF: Replace O(n²) hygiene passes with O(n) single-pass implementations
description:
## Problem
Multiple AST transformation passes use O(n²) algorithms where for each statement, they walk all remaining statements to check variable usage. This causes builds to take 2+ hours for large files like TodoLive.hx (1407 lines).

## Current State
- fast_boot flag added to bypass slow passes (commit 28dfed65)
- Build time reduced from 2+ hours to 5.4 seconds
- Trade-off: Some unused variable warnings in generated Elixir

## Solution
Replace O(n²) per-statement checks with O(n) single-pass collection:
1. Create OptimizedVarUseAnalyzer with single-pass usage collection
2. Update each slow pass to use the new analyzer
3. Remove fast_boot guards once optimized

## Affected Passes (VarUseAnalyzer or usedLater pattern)
- UnusedLocalAssignUnderscoreFinalTransforms
- DefParamUnusedUnderscoreTransforms (3 instances)
- LocalAssignUnusedUnderscoreScopedTransforms
- FinalUnderscoreRepairTransforms
- LocalUnderscoreBinderPromoteTransforms
- CasePatternUnusedUnderscoreTransforms
- AssignmentChainCleanupTransforms
- ControllerLocalAssignUnusedUnderscoreTransforms
- TopLevelNilAssignDiscardTransforms
- FunctionParamUnusedUnderscoreFinalTransforms
- CaseClauseUnusedBinderUnderscoreFinalTransforms

## Success Criteria
- All tests pass without fast_boot flag
- Build completes in <30 seconds for todo-app
- Zero Elixir warnings for unused variables

title: Phase 1.2: Create UnusedIntermediateVarRemovalTransforms - remove raw_params_*, this1, result vars
description:
## Problem
Variables like raw_params_title, broadcast_result, this1, result are generated but never used.
This produces ~12+ Elixir compiler warnings about unused variables.

## Root Cause
AST builders generate scaffolding variables that aren't cleaned up:
- FunctionBuilder generates this1 for return value tracking
- EctoQueryBuilder generates intermediate query vars
- Other builders generate temp vars for complex expressions

## Solution
Create a FINAL pass that removes all unused intermediate variables by:
1. Collecting all variable assignments in module
2. Checking if each is used (via VarUseAnalyzer)
3. Removing unused assignments entirely (not just underscore prefixing)

Key insight: Remove the assignment entirely rather than underscore-prefixing.
```elixir
# Before
raw_params_title = params["title"]  # unused, generates warning
# After  
# (line removed entirely)
```

## Files to Modify
- src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/builders/FunctionBuilder.hx - Avoid this1 generation where possible
- src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/EctoQueryIIFEInlineTransforms.hx - Inline scaffolding
- NEW: src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/UnusedIntermediateVarRemovalTransforms.hx

## Dependencies
- Depends on: Phase 1.1 (VarUseAnalyzer consolidation for reliable usage detection)

## Acceptance Criteria
- No unused intermediate variable warnings in todo-app
- raw_params_* variables either used or removed
- broadcast_result variables either used or removed
- npm test passes
- mix compile --force shows reduced warnings

## Effort: 4-6 hours | Impact: Fixes 12+ warnings

title: Phase 1.0B: Architectural fix in TypedQueryLambda.hx - eliminate this1 at macro source
description:
## Problem
TypedQuery macros generate ERaw nodes via `__elixir__()` which contain `this1` sentinel patterns that AST transforms cannot see or clean up.

## Root Cause
TypedQueryLambda.hx line 35:
```haxe
macro new ecto.TypedQuery.TypedQuery(untyped __elixir__($v{code}, $ethis, $right));
```

This generates code like:
```elixir
(fn ->
  this1 = nil
  this1 = Ecto.Query.from(t in Todo, [])
  this1
end).()
```

The `this1` is Haxe's internal pattern for abstract method chaining return values.

## Solution: Generate Structured AST
Instead of `__elixir__()` -> ERaw, TypedQuery should generate structured AST:

Option 1: Use ERemoteCall instead of __elixir__()
```haxe
return ERemoteCall(EAtom("Ecto.Query"), "where", [
    buildQueryAst(thisExpr),
    lambdaBinding,
    buildConditionAst(right)
]);
```

Option 2: Restructure to avoid this1 entirely
Generate: Ecto.Query.where(query, [t], condition) without intermediate this1 sentinel

## Files to Modify
- src/reflaxe/elixir/macros/TypedQueryLambda.hx - Restructure macro to avoid this1

## Dependencies
- Depends on: Phase 1.0A (string cleanup provides immediate relief while this is developed)
- Blocks: Final 1.0 release (this is the proper long-term solution)

## Acceptance Criteria
- TypedQuery.where() generates clean Ecto.Query.where() calls
- No this1 pattern in generated TypedQuery code
- EFnTempChainSimplifyTransforms can see and process all query AST
- npm test passes
- All existing TypedQuery tests continue to work

## Effort: 4-6 hours | Impact: Eliminates root cause, prevents future this1 issues
notes: Reopened (was closed by mistake; pending work + verification).

title: Phase 1.0A: this1 string-level cleanup in ElixirASTPrinter.hx
description:
## Problem
Generated Elixir code contains unused `this1` variable warnings in 3 files:
- todo_live.ex (load_todos function)
- user_changeset.ex
- user_controller.ex

## Root Cause Analysis (Investigation Complete)
1. TypedQuery macros use `__elixir__()` for query generation
2. `__elixir__()` creates ERaw nodes - opaque strings in AST
3. Haxe generates `this1` sentinel for abstract method chaining: `var this1 = nil; this1 = expr; this1`
4. AST transforms can't see inside ERaw - EFnTempChainSimplifyTransforms is blind to it
5. When ERaw is multi-line, `sanitizeArgPrinted()` wraps in string-level IIFE
6. Cleanup passes already ran on AST, so they never see these string-level IIFEs

## Example of Problematic Generated Code
```elixir
defp load_todos(_user_id) do
    TodoApp.Repo.all((fn ->
      query = Ecto.Query.where((fn -> query = Ecto.Query.from(t in TodoApp.Todo, [])
      this1 = nil      # <-- WARNING: unused
      this1 = query
      this1 end).(), [t], t.user_id == ^(user_id))
      this1 = nil      # <-- WARNING: unused
      this1 = query
      this1
    end).())
end
```

## Solution: String-Level Cleanup (Quick Win)
Add post-processing cleanup in ElixirASTPrinter.hx after IIFE wrapping.

## Files to Modify
- src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/ElixirASTPrinter.hx - Add string cleanup in sanitizeArgPrinted() or new helper

## Acceptance Criteria
- No this1 warnings in todo_live.ex, user_changeset.ex, user_controller.ex
- npm test passes
- mix compile --force shows no this1 warnings

## Effort: 2-3 hours | Impact: Fixes ~6 warnings immediately

title: Repin PhoenixHX Genes to the canonical merged or release commit
description:
Replace the temporary, fetchable Genes topic-branch SHA admitted by the
vendored-to-external migration with the exact commit that lands on canonical
`genes-ts` `main`, or with the exact commit identified by an admitted release.
This is a release-promotion task: the experimental downstream lane may use the
topic SHA, but a stable PhoenixHX/LiveReact release must not retain it.

## FILES

- `tooling/phoenix_scaffold/src_haxe/phoenix_scaffold_tooling/GenesContract.hx`
- generated scaffold contract and manifest under `lib/haxe_phoenix_scaffold/**`
- root and scaffolded `haxe_libraries/genes-ts.hxml` descriptors
- `docs/03-compiler-development/GENES_DEPENDENCY_WORKFLOW.md`
- Genes compatibility receipts in active plans and roadmap documentation
- regenerated classic browser artifacts and their source maps when the pin changes output

## ALGORITHM

1. Obtain the upstream merge or release identity from canonical Genes history;
   for squash merge use the squash commit, and for merge-commit workflow use
   the merge commit.
2. Verify that the canonical tree contains every generic output-quality and
   portable-source-map change admitted from the topic branch.
3. Change the Haxe-owned `GenesContract.COMMIT` and provenance note, regenerate
   all owned descriptors, and download from a clean Lix cache path.
4. Rebuild every PhoenixHX classic Genes consumer and the strict TSX/React
   fixture. Review runtime, module ABI, DCE, imports, generated quality, and
   source-map identity rather than treating compilation as sufficient.
5. Update the migration receipt with canonical repository, commit, release/tag
   when applicable, and verification evidence; remove temporary-topic wording.

## FAILURE MODES

- retaining the pre-merge topic SHA because its tree appears equivalent;
- pinning a branch, local checkout, worktree, dirty tree, or unpushed commit;
- assuming a tag identifies the correct tree without verifying its commit;
- accepting unrelated upstream regressions in classic ESM or strict TSX;
- updating hand-rendered descriptors without regenerating the Haxe-owned contract;
- claiming stable promotion while dependency identity or package smoke is unresolved.

## TESTS

- clean Lix download of the exact canonical SHA;
- downstream TSX/classic runtime and source-map parity fixture;
- all existing Genes-backed PhoenixHX client builds and generated output review;
- scaffold setup, rerun, migration, removal, and installed-package smoke;
- docs, path-hygiene, Mix, examples, and applicable browser QA gates.

## VERIFICATION

Run the bounded Genes integration, Haxe formatting, generated-core guards,
Mix/scaffold tests, example compile/output/WAE/runtime gates, package smoke,
path scan, Beads checks, and exact-head CI required by `AGENTS.md`. Record the
canonical Genes SHA and the downstream commit that adopts it.

## ROLLOUT

Do not change output profiles or introduce a second Genes source. Preserve
classic ESM as the compatibility lane and strict TypeScript/TSX as the typed
React lane. If the canonical commit fails admission, keep the explicit
experimental topic pin and report the upstream regression; do not patch Genes
inside this repository.
design: Canonical Genes history owns the stable dependency identity. The current exact topic SHA is reproducible and acceptable for the experimental integration lane only; stable promotion requires the actual canonical merge or admitted-release commit plus full downstream admission evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The exact canonical genes-ts merge or admitted-release commit replaces the topic SHA in the Haxe-owned scaffold contract and every generated descriptor; the canonical tree is verified to contain the admitted generic fixes; classic ESM and strict TSX/runtime/source-map/package gates pass; temporary-topic language is removed; no local, moving, or second Genes source remains.

2026-07-18 admission evidence: canonical genes-ts v1.36.7 commit 25a5e3015f8b0f0e4447b8fd0590124548f132da verified to contain PR #5 merge d2e881c7 and reviewed source-map commits 20e2bd0b/184b45de. Final landing evidence: downstream commit fba43c8182f7b669f20a31eb24e17d0593481059 was reviewed against canonical genes-ts v1.36.7 commit 25a5e3015f8b0f0e4447b8fd0590124548f132da and merged by PR #39 as merge commit 3a9b6cfc1b22bd5ba0920fed3f2d4d1c42937841. title: Evaluate extracting phoenix.live_react into a separately versioned Haxelib
description:
Revisit package separation only after adopter and release-cadence evidence exists. Sharing a Git monorepo, Haxelib, Hex dependency, and npm dependency are distinct decisions.

## FILES

- package ownership and cadence evidence
- current Haxelib contents/size data
- candidate package manifest and compatibility policy if justified
- migration and release plan
- source/package parity fixtures

## ALGORITHM

1. Measure release coupling, package impact, adoption, ownership, and compatibility cadence.
2. Compare same-package and separate-Haxelib operation in the same monorepo.
3. Preserve stock LiveReact as external runtime.
4. Decide keep or split with evidence.
5. If split, define import compatibility, versioning, migration, rollback, security, and release automation.

## FAILURE MODES

Split for aesthetics; new Git repository by assumption; copied runtime; incompatible imports without migration; weak version policy; duplicated source; no package parity.

## TESTS

Package contents, install, source/package parity, compatibility resolution, migration/rollback, both examples, and release smoke when a split is proposed.

## VERIFICATION

Run package build/install smoke, compatibility guards, examples, path hygiene, docs, and latest CI for either decision.

## ROLLOUT

No split until evidence crosses the plan criteria. Default is same monorepo and current Haxelib.
design: Evaluate independent Haxelib cadence while retaining one Git monorepo by default. Original LiveReact remains the Mix/npm runtime owner.
acceptance_criteria: An evidence-backed keep-or-split decision exists; any split has a migration/release/security plan and source/package parity without breaking existing imports.

title: Evaluate LiveReact slots, uploads, streams, and advanced bridge capabilities
description:
Evaluate slots, uploads, streams, and broader bridge access independently after the trusted client-only boundary ships. Each capability changes ownership, data shape, or authority and must not enter the default bridge accidentally.

## FILES

- capability matrix and threat/ownership review
- separate child issue specs per accepted capability
- focused Haxe declarations, adapters, and tests only after decisions
- compatibility and user documentation

## ALGORITHM

1. Audit each upstream capability separately.
2. Define source contract, capability flag, trusted boundary, lifecycle, and failure behavior.
3. Decide upstream contribution versus narrow adapter.
4. Split accepted capabilities into independently testable children.
5. Keep rejected/unimplemented capabilities diagnosed.

## FAILURE MODES

Expose entire raw bridge; bundle unrelated capabilities; weak open types; call trusted boundary a sandbox; fork upstream protocol; enable by default; hide unresolved work in one task.

## TESTS

Per-capability compile, runtime, security, lifecycle, removal, fallback, and compatibility fixtures, plus default-boundary regression proving no capability leakage.

## VERIFICATION

Run each child contract plus the base client-only integration and package/CI gates. Keep capability matrix synchronized.

## ROLLOUT

Independent explicit opt-ins only. This epic is a visibility container and does not block initial LiveReact.
design: Use separate capability flags and reviews. Preserve exact upstream behavior and an upstream-first policy. Default inner component types remain narrow.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed capability matrix and separate implementation decisions exist; each enabled capability has exact tests; unsupported capabilities reject rather than pass through; the default boundary remains narrow.

title: Add opt-in LiveReact SSR after the client-only contract stabilizes
description:
Evaluate and add SSR only after client-only setup, ownership, and compatibility stabilize. SSR changes runtime topology, deployment, memory, hydration, and failure behavior and is not a checkbox in the first epic.

## FILES

- SSR compatibility/architecture decision
- setup/check/remove and manifest capability changes
- upstream LiveReact SSR declarations/config
- Node supervision/release fixtures
- hydration, source-map, deployment, and fallback tests
- user/deployment docs

## ALGORITHM

1. Audit current upstream ViteJS and NodeJS SSR contracts.
2. Select development and production runtime ownership.
3. Model Node supervision, release artifacts, health/failure behavior, memory, hydration, and removal.
4. Add explicit opt-in manifest/configuration.
5. Prove no-SSR projects remain unchanged and fallback remains usable.

## FAILURE MODES

PhoenixHx renderer fork; SSR enabled by default; orphan Node worker; mismatched server/client sources; hydration drift; undocumented release artifact; destructive removal; broad compatibility claim.

## TESTS

Development and production SSR, hydration, failure/restart, release packaging, source maps, check/remove, client-only regression, fallback, package smoke, and bounded version matrix.

## VERIFICATION

Run focused upstream-compatible SSR integration and deployment fixtures, both no-SSR and SSR examples, package smoke, docs/path guards, and latest CI.

## ROLLOUT

Explicit experimental opt-in after the client-only integration ships; no default topology change.
design: Use stock LiveReact SSR.ViteJS/NodeJS surfaces. PhoenixHx owns typed setup and operational evidence, not the renderer. Treat runtime supervision and deployment as first-class contracts.
acceptance_criteria: SSR has separate compatibility/deployment evidence, explicit opt-in, clean removal, hydration/failure tests, package smoke, resource posture, and no PhoenixHx runtime fork.

title: Preserve abstract identity carriers before late repair
description: One-argument abstract implementation conversions such as AgentRef.named, GenServerRef.fromVia, and RegistryKey.fromInt currently pass through an intermediate empty-body shape after RedundantAssignmentCleanup. AbstractImplIdentityStubTransforms restores the correct identity value before printing, and the phase-level result invariant verifies that restoration. Remove the upstream bad shape so correctness no longer depends on the late repair.
design: Trace the authored abstract assignment through builder and cleanup using granular pass snapshots. Preserve value context at the earliest semantically correct phase without retaining unused binders or changing unrelated hygiene output. Once source and package snapshots prove the body remains valid throughout the pipeline, narrow or remove the generalized late identity repair.
acceptance_criteria: Granular phase snapshots show representative abstract identity conversions never transition to an empty result; generated Elixir remains identity-returning and warnings-as-errors clean; no unrelated snapshot drift; source-checkout and built-package parity pass; full snapshots, stdlib runtime checks, examples, and todo-app QA remain green.

title: Emit useful typespecs for stable target-native public surfaces
description: Most generated application modules omit @spec even though the compiler has typed Haxe information and an ElixirTyper layer. Handwritten Elixir does not require a spec on every function, but stable public Phoenix/Ecto/OTP and domain boundaries benefit from accurate specs.
design: Start with types that have faithful Elixir representations and explicit target-native public APIs. Define conservative fallback to term() rather than incorrect precision. Avoid specs for generated private plumbing unless useful, and avoid claiming Haxe nullability/generic guarantees that the BEAM representation cannot enforce.
acceptance_criteria: A documented initial surface emits valid, formatted @spec declarations for representative domain functions and selected target-native callbacks; optional values, Result tuples, maps/structs, enums, generics, Dynamic/Term, and overloaded Haxe signatures have tested mappings or explicit conservative fallback; Dialyzer or Elixir compiler validation catches malformed specs; generated output remains readable and WAE-clean; source/package parity and full relevant suites pass.

title: Decide a sound defprotocol/defimpl contract for Haxe-authored abstractions
description:
## Decision

Decide whether and how Haxe-authored target-native abstractions can generate sound Elixir defprotocol/defimpl constructs. Current `@:protocol`/`@:impl` examples generate ordinary dispatch modules, while Elixir protocols dispatch on native data type and many Haxe instances share a map-backed representation.

## Rationale

Native protocols would improve Elixir interoperability and handwritten fidelity, but an unsound mapping could dispatch every Haxe object through the same map implementation, break consolidation/package behavior, or silently change the ABI of the existing portable abstraction surface.

## Alternatives Considered

- Keep the current ordinary dispatch modules and name/document them as portable abstractions.
- Add a separate explicit target-native protocol surface restricted to native structs or other provably distinct BEAM representations.
- Change existing metadata to emit defprotocol/defimpl with a versioned migration.
- Defer native protocol generation until the object representation can support correct dispatch.
design: Evaluate native structs, map-backed Haxe objects, Any fallback, consolidation, deriving, package boundaries, implementation overlap, reflection, and source/package compilation. Compare raw Elixir protocol expectations with the existing portable abstraction contract. Prefer an explicit target-native surface; do not relabel map-dispatch helpers as protocols or silently change ABI.
acceptance_criteria: An ADR adopts, rejects, or defers defprotocol/defimpl lowering with concrete compiled prototypes and dispatch evidence; the decision states compatible metadata/API, representation requirements, package/consolidation behavior, migration and SemVer impact, and how portable abstractions continue to work; if adopted, create scoped implementation and migration beads with dependencies; if rejected/deferred, docs accurately name the existing surface and point Elixir-first users to the supported native interop path.

title: Emit native Elixir behaviour contracts through an explicit versioned surface
description: The abstraction lab's behaviour-style Haxe declaration currently generates an ordinary Elixir module whose functions raise, rather than `@callback` declarations and implementation modules carrying `@behaviour`. Native behaviours improve interoperability, Dialyzer/editor understanding, and handwritten fidelity, but changing existing metadata silently could break callers.
design: Document and approve a compatibility contract before code changes. Either version the existing annotation semantics or add an explicit target-native surface, then lower typed signatures to valid callback types and attach @behaviour to implementations. Preserve the current portable module/function abstraction where native callback semantics are not requested. Do not infer behaviours from names.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in compatibility decision defines old/new metadata and migration; a focused example emits valid @callback, optional callbacks when supported, and @behaviour on implementing modules; Elixir compilation catches a deliberate missing/wrong callback in negative coverage; Haxe type checking remains useful; generated runtime behavior and existing portable abstraction users remain compatible; docs show raw Elixir alongside Haxe; snapshots, examples, package parity, and todo QA pass.

title: Devirtualize method calls only for proven exact receivers
description: Public Haxe instance calls currently preserve virtual dispatch through dynamic class-map lookup and apply, which is correct but visibly generated. Direct module calls are possible for some final, private, static-exact, or otherwise closed-world receivers.
design: Base devirtualization on typed closed-world proof, not class or method names. Preserve Haxe override/interface semantics, reflection, null checks, Dynamic receivers, extern/native classes, and subclass construction across modules. Record why a call was or was not devirtualized in opt-in diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Final/private or otherwise formally proven exact calls emit direct module functions in focused snapshots and run correctly; override, interface, Dynamic, reflection, and open-world fixtures retain virtual dispatch; no receiver-return rebinding or evaluation-order regression occurs; diagnostic output explains proof decisions without normal-build noise; compile-time and generated-size impact are measured; full suites and package parity pass.

title: Lower proven Result or Option chains to Elixir with
description: The IR supports `with`, but normal generated application code does not currently use it. Straight-line Elixir-first Result/Option flows with early error propagation can read like handwritten Elixir when emitted as `with`, but arbitrary Haxe switches and imperative control flow are not equivalent.
design: Define a narrow typed pattern for sequential success extraction with unchanged error values and no intervening mutation, catch behavior, variable-scope dependency, or custom branch logic. Preserve unmatched/error clause semantics exactly. Keep case for general matching and avoid making `with` a formatting preference.
acceptance_criteria: A focused Elixir-first fixture emits idiomatic with for a multi-step Result/Option flow and matches a raw Elixir equivalent; runtime tests cover success, each failure position, guards, and else mapping; negative fixtures retain case for transformed errors, side effects, mutation, overlapping patterns, non-local returns, and scope-sensitive variables; no portable semantics change; full snapshots and runtime gates pass.

title: Enable EReg upstream runtime parity

title: Perf: measure todo-app watch cycle time (mix haxe.watch)
description:
# WHAT
Add a bounded measurement of edit→rebuild latency when using `mix haxe.watch` / the todo-app watcher.

# WHY
The biggest DevX pain is often the incremental “watch” cycle, not the cold compile. We need a baseline to know what “good” looks like and to detect major regressions.

# HOW
- Create a small script that:
  - starts the watcher in the background (bounded; auto-terminates)
  - touches a single representative Haxe file in the todo-app (or a generated copy) to trigger rebuild
  - measures time until “compile done” signal appears in logs
  - repeats N times and outputs p50/p95
- Keep it non-gating by default; store results as JSON.

# Acceptance
- Running the script locally prints a short summary and writes a JSON artifact.
- The script is bounded (uses `scripts/with-timeout.sh`) and leaves no background processes.
acceptance_criteria: - Script reports watch cycle latency distribution (p50/p95)\n- Output includes environment + phases\n- Docs explain how to run locally

title: Spike: formalize portable|metal contract for reflaxe.elixir while preserving elixir-first ergonomics
description:
## Why
Current Elixir model is strong architecturally, but `portable vs elixir-first` is mostly documented as authoring guidance. We need an explicit profile contract aligned with family semantics and CI gates.

## Inputs
- Family/canonical references from Go:
  - `../haxe.go/docs/portable-canonical-contract.md`
  - `../haxe.go/docs/profiles.md`
  - `../haxe.go/docs/phase2-roadmap.md`
- Elixir references:
  - `docs/02-user-guide/AUTHORING_STYLES_PORTABLE_VS_ELIXIR_FIRST.md`
  - `src/reflaxe/elixir/CompilerInit.hx`
  - `src/reflaxe/elixir/macros/StrictModeEnforcer.hx`
  - `src/reflaxe/elixir/macros/BoundaryEnforcer.hx`

## Spike Scope
1. Define how to express Elixir `portable|metal` as compiler contract (not replacing authoring docs).
2. Specify profile presets over orthogonal axes:
   - strictness policy
   - runtime/support-module policy
   - interop boundary policy
3. Propose migration plan with low disruption:
   - optional fallback/warn mode for metal migration
   - contract tests for portable semantic subset
   - docs consolidation path

## Deliverables
- Architecture spike doc with:
  - current vs target model
  - compatibility risks
  - implementation phases
  - CI test-matrix changes
- Follow-up beads tasks (prioritized; default low priority unless blockers).

## Future Follow-up Trigger
After `haxe.go` selective runtime + metal fallback lands, run a new GPT-5.2 Pro comparative spike across Go/Rust/Elixir/hxhx using updated code and docs to finalize family spec.
close_reason: Architecture spike complete: documented the Reflaxe.Elixir authoring-profile contract in docs/05-architecture/AUTHORING_PROFILE_CONTRACT.md, linked it from user and architecture docs, clarified that portable and Elixir-first are authoring profiles rather than backend switches, scoped metal to local escape hatches, captured compatibility risks/CI axes/implementation phases, and created follow-up haxe.elixir-960 for optional diagnostic-only profile linting.
